recipes.recipe_name: Baked Banana and Oat Pudding with Cardamom Milk
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of baked oat pudding served in a shallow, wide-rimmed white porcelain bowl. The pudding is a thick, textured square with a golden-brown crust and visible toasted oat grains. A pool of creamy, pale-yellow saffron milk surrounds the base. Resting on the pudding is a whole banana half, seared to a deep mahogany brown with a glistening caramelized surface. Vibrant green slivered pistachios and thin red saffron threads are scattered precisely over the top. The setting features a dark walnut wood table, a neutral linen napkin, and a small polished brass spoon. The lighting is soft, natural, and directional, emphasizing the contrast between the crisp pudding edges and the smooth milk.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve warm as a concluding course for a celebratory meal
Accompany with a small cup of masala chai
Use a traditional brass or silver spoon for an authentic feel
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C.
Toast oats in 20g ghee over medium heat until fragrant.
Mash three bananas in a large bowl.
Mix mashed bananas, toasted oats, jaggery, salt, and 100ml milk.
Pour mixture into a greased baking dish.
Bake for 25 minutes until firm and golden.
Simmer remaining milk with cardamom and saffron in a small pot.
Reduce milk by one-third over low heat.
Slice remaining banana into four long halves.
Sear banana halves in remaining ghee until caramelized.
Cut baked pudding into four thick squares.
Place one square in each shallow bowl.
Pour warm saffron milk around the pudding base.
Place one caramelized banana half on top.
Garnish with slivered pistachios.
notes: Ensure the bananas are very ripe for maximum sweetness
The milk reduction should be thick enough to coat the back of a spoon
Do not overbake to maintain a moist interior texture

recipes.recipe_name: Pollo e Peperoni alla Romana with Rigatoni
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Pollo e Peperoni alla Romana served in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl. The base consists of rigatoni pasta coated in a vibrant, glossy sauce of reduced white wine and chicken juices. Intermingled with the pasta are soft, julienned strips of red and yellow bell peppers and translucent red onion wedges showing light caramelization. Resting prominently on top are two whole, golden-brown pan-seared chicken thighs with visible crispy skin. The dish is garnished with scattered fresh oregano leaves and a drizzle of extra virgin olive oil. The setting is a dark wood bistro table with a clean cotton napkin. Natural light emphasizes the textures of the seared chicken and the silkiness of the pepper sauce.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty ciabatta to mop up the sauce
Pair with a crisp Italian white wine like Frascati
Enjoy as a 'Piatto Unico' combining protein and starch

ingredients.name: Red and yellow bell peppers, julienned

instructions: Season chicken with salt and pepper.
Heat oil in a large pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down until golden and crispy.
Flip chicken and cook until internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove chicken and keep warm.
Add onions and peppers to the same pan.
Sauté vegetables until softened and slightly charred.
Add garlic and dried oregano. Cook 1 minute.
Pour in white wine. Scrape the pan bottom.
Add chicken stock. Simmer until liquid reduces by half.
Boil rigatoni in salted water until al dente.
Drain pasta and reserve 50 ml of pasta water.
Toss pasta with peppers and sauce. Add pasta water if needed to emulsify.
Divide pasta into bowls. Place whole chicken thighs on top.
Garnish with fresh oregano.
notes: Always use skin-on chicken for maximum flavor and texture
Ensure the pasta water is as salty as the sea
Do not slice the chicken before serving to retain juices

recipes.recipe_name: Mexican Charro Beans with Smoked Sausage and Charred Corn
recipes.visual_description: A deep, rustic terracotta cazuela holds a hearty portion of Mexican Charro bean stew. The broth is a rich, opaque reddish-brown color, filled with tender, whole pinto beans. Large, 2cm thick chunks of browned smoked sausage and small bits of crispy bacon are distributed throughout the stew. Bright yellow corn kernels with distinct black char marks provide a vibrant visual contrast. The dish is finished with a generous scattering of freshly chopped green cilantro. The cazuela sits on a dark, weathered wooden table. A side of three warm, slightly charred corn tortillas is folded in a traditional woven basket. Fresh lime wedges and a small bowl of salsa verde are placed nearby. Natural window light creates a soft glow on the steam and the glossy surfaces of the sausage.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Warm corn tortillas
Fresh lime wedges
Salsa verde
Pickled jalapeños
instructions: Soak pinto beans in water for 8 hours.
Drain beans. Place in a large pot with chicken stock.
Simmer beans for 90 minutes until tender.
Heat a dry skillet over high heat. Char corn kernels until dark spots appear. Remove.
Sauté diced bacon in a separate pan until crispy.
Add sausage chunks to the pan. Brown for 5 minutes.
Add onion, garlic, and jalapeño. Cook until soft.
Stir in tomatoes, oregano, and cumin. Cook for 5 minutes.
Combine sausage mixture and charred corn with the beans.
Simmer for 15 minutes to marry flavors.
Season with salt and pepper.
Stir in cilantro before serving.
notes: Ensure beans are fully tender before adding the acidic tomato mixture.
Use a high-quality smoked sausage like Chorizo or Longaniza for authentic flavor.
The broth should be thick but not dry; add a splash of water if it reduces too much.

recipes.recipe_name: Pork in Salsa Roja
recipes.visual_description: A deep, wide terracotta bowl holds the Cerdo en Salsa Roja. The pork appears as large 3cm tender chunks, thoroughly coated in a thick, vibrant crimson sauce made from blended tomatoes and guajillo chilies. The sauce has a glossy, rich texture with visible specks of oregano. The dish is garnished with a sprig of fresh cilantro and a few rings of raw white onion. Beside the bowl sits a small stack of warm, folded corn tortillas on a linen napkin. The setting is a dark wood table under soft, natural light. A single portion is shown, emphasizing the rustic yet clean presentation with ample space around the bowl.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Warm corn tortillas
Mexican red rice
Refried beans
Lime wedges

ingredients.name: Guajillo chilies, stems and seeds removed

instructions: Cut pork into 3cm cubes and season with salt.
Toast guajillo chilies in a dry skillet over medium heat for 2 minutes.
Soak toasted chilies in hot water for 15 minutes until soft.
Boil tomatoes and onion in water for 10 minutes.
Blend boiled tomatoes, onion, garlic, and soaked chilies until completely smooth.
Heat oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat.
Sear pork cubes in batches until browned on all sides.
Pour the blended salsa over the pork.
Add cumin and oregano.
Reduce heat to low and simmer for 45 minutes until meat is tender.
Adjust salt to taste before serving.
notes: Ensure the sauce is blended very smooth to achieve a professional texture.
Sieve the sauce before adding to the meat if the chili skins remain coarse.
Use a heavy-bottomed pot to prevent the sauce from scorching during the braise.

recipes.recipe_name: Tartiflette Savoyarde
recipes.visual_description: A single individual portion served in a small, round white ceramic gratin dish. The dish sits on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The top features two large, thick chunks of Reblochon cheese with the characteristic orange-pink rind facing upward. The cheese is melted and bubbling, with charred golden-brown spots. Visible underneath are one centimeter thick potato rounds and small cubes of browned smoked lardons. Golden caramelized onion strips peek through the creamy sauce. A small sprig of fresh flat-leaf parsley provides a green accent. The setting is a modern bistro with a light oak wood table. A glass of white wine and a linen napkin are nearby. Natural side lighting highlights the creamy texture and bubbling surface.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a crisp green salad tossed in a sharp vinaigrette
Pair with a chilled Apremont or Roussette de Savoie white wine
Serve with cornichons and pickled onions on the side
instructions: Boil potatoes in salted water for 15 minutes until tender but firm.
Drain potatoes and allow to cool slightly.
Peel potatoes and cut into 1 cm thick rounds.
Sauté lardons in a large pan over medium heat until fat renders and they turn golden.
Add sliced onions to the pan with the lardons.
Cook onions until soft and lightly caramelized.
Pour in white wine to deglaze the pan.
Simmer wine until the liquid is reduced by half.
Preheat oven to 200°C.
Rub a ceramic baking dish with the garlic clove and butter.
Layer half of the potato rounds in the bottom of the dish.
Spread half of the onion and lardon mixture over the potatoes.
Repeat layers with remaining potatoes and onion mixture.
Spoon crème fraîche evenly over the top.
Season with black pepper.
Slice the Reblochon cheese in half horizontally to create two circles.
Place cheese halves crust-side up on top of the potatoes.
Bake for 20 minutes until the cheese is melted, bubbling, and golden brown.
notes: Do not remove the rind from the Reblochon as it provides essential flavor
Ensure potatoes are waxy varieties to prevent them from turning to mash
The dish should be served immediately while the cheese is fluid

recipes.recipe_name: Cantonese Claypot Rice with Chinese Sausage
recipes.visual_description: The dish is served in a traditional dark-textured ceramic claypot set on a rustic wooden table. The focal point is a mound of fluffy jasmine rice, featuring visible mahogany streaks from the dark soy sauce. Thick 1cm diagonal chunks of reddish-pink Chinese sausage are distributed across the surface, showing a glossy, rendered fat sheen. Fine 2cm julienne strips of pale yellow ginger and translucent softened shallots are scattered over the meat. Along the edges of the pot, a golden-brown, crispy rice crust is clearly visible. The composition is clean and centered, showing the entire pot. Natural side-lighting emphasizes the steam and the contrast between the white rice and dark sauce. A pair of dark wood chopsticks sits on a ceramic rest nearby.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve directly in the cooking claypot to maintain heat
Scrape the crispy rice crust (guo ba) from the bottom to share
Pair with blanched gai lan or bok choy
Serve with a side of chili oil or soy-marinated bird's eye chilies
instructions: Rinse rice until water runs clear. Drain well.
Cut Chinese sausage into 1cm thick diagonal chunks.
Peel ginger and cut into fine julienne strips.
Peel and thinly slice shallots. Mince garlic cloves.
Heat oil in a heavy-bottomed pot or claypot over medium heat.
Sauté shallots and garlic for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add rice to the pot. Stir to coat with oil for 1 minute.
Pour in chicken stock. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 10 minutes.
Place sausage chunks and ginger strips on top of the rice.
Cover and continue cooking for 8 minutes.
Increase heat to medium-high for 2 minutes to crisp the bottom rice.
Mix dark soy sauce, light soy sauce, and sugar in a small bowl.
Drizzle sauce over the rice and sausage. Cover for 2 minutes.
Remove from heat. Let stand for 5 minutes before serving.
notes: The high sugar content in Chinese sausage helps create the caramelized crust.
Do not stir the rice during the final high-heat phase to ensure the crust forms properly.

recipes.recipe_name: Mimicry Crab Egg Whites with Tomato Reduction
recipes.visual_description: A single portion features a central mound of velvetted egg whites, cooked into soft, pillowy white clouds with a delicate matte texture. Interspersed throughout the whites are fine, golden-brown threads of shredded dried scallops. A vibrant, translucent red tomato-ginger reduction is pooled around the base of the egg whites, creating a sharp color contrast against the white porcelain plate. The arrangement is organic and free-flowing with moderate negative space. A small garnish of julienned ginger batons sits atop the whites. The dish is set on a dark wood table with bamboo chopsticks on a ceramic rest and a small side bowl of steamed jasmine rice. Natural side lighting highlights the soft textures.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a small side dish of extra Chinkiang vinegar and ginger slivers
Accompany with a bowl of steamed jasmine rice
Present with traditional ceramic spoons and bamboo chopsticks
instructions: Rehydrate dried scallops in hot water for 30 minutes. Shred into fine threads.
Score tomato skins. Blanch in boiling water. Peel and remove seeds.
Dice tomatoes into 5mm pieces.
Sauté minced ginger in 10ml oil. Add diced tomatoes.
Stir in black vinegar and sugar. Simmer 10 minutes. Strain through a fine mesh sieve to create a smooth reduction.
Whisk egg whites, milk, and salt in a bowl until combined. Do not create foam.
Heat remaining 30ml oil in a wok over medium-low heat.
Pour egg mixture into the wok. Stir slowly and continuously in one direction.
Cook until whites form soft, opaque, pillowy clouds.
Fold in the shredded scallop threads. Remove from heat immediately.
Divide the egg whites into four portions. Pour tomato reduction around the base of each.
notes: Maintain low heat for the egg whites to prevent any browning or toughness
The addition of milk is essential for the snowy white color and tender mouthfeel
Ensure the tomato reduction is strained well for a professional restaurant finish

recipes.recipe_name: Vietnamese Shaking Beef (Bo Luc Lac)
recipes.special_requests: beef protein full meal without much carbs but with veggies cuisine
recipes.visual_description: The dish features seared 2.5cm beef sirloin cubes, glistening with a dark soy glaze and showing deep caramelized edges from the high-heat wok sear. The beef is piled naturally in the center of a clean white porcelain plate, mixed with softened red onion wedges. It rests atop a vibrant bed of fresh, bright green watercress and halved ruby-red cherry tomatoes. The arrangement is organic and uncrowded, leaving white space around the perimeter. Beside the plate sits a small ceramic ramekin containing a clear lime juice and coarse black pepper dipping sauce. The setting is a modern bistro with a dark wood table, a folded white cotton napkin, and dark wooden chopsticks. Natural side lighting highlights the succulent meat and crisp greens.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with Muoi Tieu Chanh (salt, pepper, and lime dipping sauce)
Use chopsticks for dining
Can be accompanied by pickled daikon and carrots

ingredients.name: Red onion, cut into thin wedges

instructions: Pat beef cubes dry with paper towels.
Marinate beef with garlic, soy sauce, fish sauce, oyster sauce, and sugar for 30 minutes.
Whisk lime juice and black pepper in a small bowl for the dipping sauce.
Arrange watercress and cherry tomatoes on a large platter or individual plates.
Heat oil in a wok over high heat until smoking.
Add beef cubes in a single layer to ensure a hard sear.
Sear without moving for 2 minutes until a dark crust forms.
Add red onion wedges to the wok.
Shake the wok vigorously to sear all sides of the beef for 2 minutes.
Remove from heat immediately to keep the beef medium-rare.
Tumble the beef and onions directly onto the bed of watercress and tomatoes.
notes: Ensure the wok is smoking hot before adding meat to achieve authentic wok hei flavor.
Do not overcrowd the pan; cook in batches if necessary to maintain high heat.
The residual heat from the beef will slightly wilt the watercress, creating a warm salad effect.

recipes.recipe_name: Dark Chocolate and Beef Tallow Tart with Candied Beef Crumble
recipes.visual_description: A single 8cm tart sits off-center on a matte black designer plate. The tart shell is golden and crisp, filled with a glass-like, dark chocolate ganache. A textured mound of candied beef brisket, cut into precise 2mm cubes, is placed organically on one side of the ganache surface. Three flakes of Maldon sea salt catch the light. The plate rests on a grey-veined white Carrara marble surface. A single, heavy silver dessert spoon is placed to the right. The lighting is dramatic and directional, casting soft shadows that emphasize the architectural edges of the tart and the rugged texture of the beef crumble. Minimalist negative space surrounds the dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a small glass of aged Pedro Ximénez sherry
Present on a chilled marble plinth for temperature contrast
instructions: Pulse flour, 50g sugar, and 80g chilled tallow in a food processor until sandy.
Add egg yolk and 20ml cold water. Process until dough forms.
Chill dough for 30 minutes. Roll to 3mm thickness.
Line four 8cm tart rings. Blind bake at 180°C for 15 minutes.
Simmer diced brisket in 100g sugar and 30ml water until syrup thickens.
Drain beef. Spread on parchment. Bake at 150°C until crisp and dark brown.
Bring cream to a simmer. Pour over chopped chocolate and 40g tallow.
Whisk gently from the center to create a smooth emulsion.
Pour ganache into tart shells. Set at room temperature for 2 hours.
Top with candied beef crumble and sea salt before serving.
notes: Ensure beef tallow is highly filtered for a neutral, creamy profile
The brisket must be diced extremely fine to ensure a pleasant texture when candied
Do not refrigerate the tart to maintain the gloss of the ganache

recipes.recipe_name: Pollo alla Cacciatora
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Pollo alla Cacciatora is presented on a wide, matte white porcelain plate. Two whole, bone-in chicken thighs are stacked slightly in the center, featuring deeply browned, caramelized skin. A thick, rustic sauce covers the base of the plate, filled with visible small cubes of orange carrots, green celery, and translucent onions. Whole, dark purple kalamata olives are nestled within the vibrant red tomato sauce. A light dusting of bright green chopped parsley and a single fresh rosemary sprig garnish the top. Two thick batons of grilled sourdough bread lean against the side of the chicken. The lighting is natural and soft, emphasizing the glossy texture of the braised sauce and the crispness of the chicken skin.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with toasted sourdough bread to soak up the sauce
Accompany with a glass of medium-bodied Italian red wine
Place on a bed of soft, buttery polenta
instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a wide braising pan over medium-high heat.
Place chicken skin-side down in the pan.
Sear for 6 minutes until the skin is deep golden and crisp.
Flip chicken and cook for 2 minutes.
Remove chicken from pan and set aside.
Add onion, carrot, and celery to the remaining fat.
Sauté vegetables for 8 minutes until softened.
Stir in garlic, rosemary, and sage. Cook for 1 minute.
Pour in red wine. Scrape the bottom of the pan to deglaze.
Simmer wine for 3 minutes until reduced by half.
Add crushed tomatoes and stir to combine.
Place chicken thighs back into the sauce.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 25 minutes.
Check internal temperature of chicken reaches 75°C.
Stir in olives and simmer uncovered for 5 minutes.
Remove rosemary sprigs before serving.
Garnish with chopped parsley.
notes: Always use a meat thermometer to ensure chicken reaches the safe internal temperature of 75°C
Browning the skin thoroughly at the start is essential for the final texture
The sauce should be thick and chunky, not watery

recipes.recipe_name: Sichuan Minced Chicken with Pickled Long Beans
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented as a single portion in a shallow, matte-white ceramic bowl. The primary focus is a mound of savory stir-fry featuring minced chicken cut into uniform 5mm pieces. This is mixed with vibrant green 5mm rounds of pickled long beans. Small cubes of bright red chili add contrast throughout. The chicken appears well-seared with a light, glossy soy glaze. A scattering of fresh green onion batons garnishes the top. The bowl sits on a dark walnut table next to a small porcelain bowl of steamed white jasmine rice. Dark bamboo chopsticks rest on a small stone holder. The lighting is soft and natural, highlighting the textures of the finely diced ingredients.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed jasmine rice
Accompany with a side of plain congee
Pair with a light clear vegetable soup

ingredients.name: Fresh red bird's eye chilies, diced

instructions: Finely chop chicken breast into small 5mm pieces.
Rinse pickled long beans and dice into 5mm rounds.
Heat vegetable oil in a wok over high heat until smoking.
Add minced chicken to the wok.
Stir-fry chicken until white and opaque.
Add ginger, garlic, and red chilies.
Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add pickled long beans and stir-fry for 2 minutes over high heat.
Pour in Shaoxing wine, light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, and sugar.
Toss ingredients continuously for 2 minutes to develop wok hei.
Verify chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Drizzle with sesame oil and toss to combine.
Remove from heat and garnish with green onion batons.
notes: Ensure the wok is extremely hot before adding oil to achieve wok hei flavor.
If pickled long beans are very salty, soak them in fresh water for 10 minutes before dicing.
Do not overcook the beans to maintain their crunchy texture.

recipes.recipe_name: Cantonese Soy Sauce Chicken (Shi Yao Gai)
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Soy Sauce Chicken presented as large, bone-in chunks on a clean white porcelain plate. The chicken skin is a deep, glossy mahogany brown with a mirror-like sheen from the soy glaze. The meat is ivory and moist. The chunks are stacked naturally in a loose mound in the center of the plate, showing the clean cuts of the bone. A small amount of the dark, viscous poaching liquid is drizzled over the top. Garnish with a few fresh cilantro sprigs and thin julienne strips of ginger. Beside the plate sits a small dipping bowl of bright green ginger-scallion oil and a pair of dark wood chopsticks on a ceramic rest. The background is a minimalist modern bistro table with a neutral cotton napkin.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed jasmine rice
Accompany with ginger-scallion dipping oil (Min Jiang)
Include a side of blanched bok choy
Provide hot oolong tea
instructions: Clean chicken and pat skin dry with paper towels.
Heat oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot over medium heat.
Sauté ginger and scallions until fragrant.
Add light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, rice wine, rock sugar, water, star anise, and cinnamon.
Bring liquid to a boil then reduce to a simmer.
Lower chicken into the liquid breast-side down.
Simmer for 15 minutes while frequently ladling hot liquid over exposed parts.
Flip chicken and simmer for another 15 minutes.
Check internal temperature reaches 75°C at the thickest part of the thigh.
Turn off heat and let chicken soak in liquid for 15 minutes.
Remove chicken and let rest for 20 minutes.
Chop chicken into large bite-sized bone-in chunks for serving.
notes: The poaching liquid can be strained and frozen for future use as a master stock.
Rock sugar provides a superior glossy finish compared to granulated sugar.
Ensure the chicken rests before chopping to retain juices.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Chicken with Potatoes
recipes.special_requests: 简单的家常菜比较容易做,用鸡腿带骨带皮
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of braised chicken and potatoes is served in a shallow, rustic blue-rimmed ceramic bowl. The dish features four large, bone-in chicken thigh chunks with deeply caramelized, mahogany-colored skin. Beside the chicken are several 3cm cubes of soft potato, their edges slightly rounded from braising, heavily coated in a thick, glossy brown sauce. Slices of ginger and whole star anise are visible among the ingredients. The bowl sits on a dark wood table next to a small bowl of steamed white rice and dark wood chopsticks. Lighting is warm and natural, highlighting the reflective sheen of the savory sauce. The entire plate is visible against a simple, lived-in kitchen background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed white jasmine rice
Accompany with a side of smashed cucumber salad
Place serving bowl in the center of the table for family-style sharing

ingredients.name: bone-in skin-on chicken thighs, cut into large chunks
potatoes, peeled and cut into 3cm cubes

instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 3-4 large chunks each.
Heat oil in a wok or deep pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down until golden brown.
Add ginger, garlic, and scallions. Stir for 1 minute.
Add potatoes, light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, wine, sugar, and star anise.
Pour in water. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 25 minutes.
Verify chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove lid. Increase heat to high.
Reduce sauce for 5 minutes until thick and glossy.
notes: Use waxy potatoes to ensure they hold their shape during braising
Adjust dark soy sauce quantity to achieve a deeper or lighter mahogany color
Keep the bone in for more flavorful sauce and tender meat

recipes.recipe_name: Three-Cup Chicken (San Bei Ji)
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented in a dark ceramic vessel. It features 4cm chunks of chicken coated in a thick, dark-amber glaze. Whole, toasted garlic cloves and 3cm squares of red bell pepper provide textural contrast. The chicken skin is deeply caramelized. Bright green Thai basil leaves are scattered across the top. The arrangement is natural and centered with moderate negative space around the rim. The setting includes a bowl of white rice and bamboo chopsticks on a clean wooden surface. Natural side lighting emphasizes the glossy texture of the reduction. No meat is sliced; all pieces remain as hearty, rustic chunks. The color palette is rich mahogany, vibrant red, and deep green.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed jasmine rice
Pair with pickled daikon radish
Accompany with a clear vegetable broth
instructions: Cut chicken into 4cm chunks.
Cut bell peppers into 3cm squares.
Slice ginger into thin rounds.
Heat sesame oil in a wok over medium heat.
Fry ginger slices until edges turn brown and crispy.
Add whole garlic cloves. Cook until golden on all sides.
Add chicken chunks. Sear until skin is browned.
Pour in soy sauce and Shaoxing wine. Add rock sugar.
Cover and simmer for 15 minutes.
Check chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Add bell pepper squares.
Remove lid. Increase heat to high.
Stir-fry until sauce reduces to a thick, dark glaze.
Turn off heat. Fold in Thai basil leaves until wilted.
Serve immediately.
notes: Use bone-in chicken for more authentic flavor and juiciness.
Do not substitute Thai basil with sweet basil as the anise flavor is critical.
The 'three cups' refers to the equal ratio of oil, soy, and wine.

recipes.recipe_name: Arroz con Pollo
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Arroz con Pollo presented on a clean white porcelain plate. Two whole, bone-in chicken thighs with deeply browned, crispy skin sit atop a bed of golden, saffron-stained rice. The rice grains are plump and distinct, interspersed with fine bits of softened onion and concentrated red tomato. The dish shows vibrant yellow and orange hues from the saffron and paprika. A generous sprinkle of bright green, finely chopped parsley is scattered over the top. A single lemon wedge is placed neatly on the side. The plate sits on a light oak wooden table with a folded white cotton napkin. Lighting is bright, natural, and even, highlighting the textures of the crispy skin and the moist rice grains.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of Alioli (garlic mayonnaise)
Accompany with crusty bread and a glass of chilled white wine
Present in a traditional terracotta cazuela for family-style dining
instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a wide shallow pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down until golden and crispy.
Flip and brown the other side. Remove chicken from pan.
Add onion to the same pan. Sauté until translucent.
Stir in garlic and grated tomato. Cook until liquid evaporates and mixture darkens.
Add smoked paprika and rice. Stir to coat rice in oil for 2 minutes.
Pour in white wine. Deglaze the pan. Simmer until wine reduces by half.
Add hot stock and saffron. Stir once to distribute.
Place chicken thighs back into the pan on top of the rice.
Simmer undisturbed over medium-low heat for 18-20 minutes.
Ensure chicken reaches internal temperature of 75°C.
Remove from heat. Cover with a clean cloth. Rest for 5 minutes.
Garnish with fresh parsley before serving.
notes: Do not stir the rice once the stock is added to allow a crust to form on the bottom.
Use a wide pan to ensure even rice cooking.

recipes.recipe_name: Sichuan Cumin Pork Skewers (Chuan'er)
recipes.visual_description: A professional presentation of eight skewers arranged on a matte black ceramic rectangular platter. The pork shoulder is cut into uniform 2cm cubes, showing deep caramelization and charred edges from high-heat roasting. A thick, textured crust of toasted whole cumin seeds and vibrant red chili flakes coats each piece of meat. The skewers are placed at a slight diagonal across the plate, leaving clean negative space at the corners. Fresh, bright green scallion curls and white sesame seeds are scattered over the center. The scene is set on a dark walnut bistro table with a folded grey linen napkin. Natural side lighting highlights the glistening fat and coarse spice texture.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with chilled Tsingtao beer
Accompany with pickled garlic cloves
Provide a side of extra spice mix for dipping
instructions: Place pork cubes in a large bowl.
Add soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, and 15ml oil.
Marinate for 30 minutes at room temperature.
Thread 4 to 5 pork cubes onto each bamboo skewer.
Preheat grill or oven to 220°C.
Mix cumin, chili flakes, Sichuan pepper, and salt in a small bowl.
Brush skewers with remaining oil.
Grill skewers for 4 minutes per side until charred.
Sprinkle spice mix heavily over both sides of the meat.
Grill for 1 more minute to toast the spices.
Garnish with sesame seeds and scallions.
notes: Soak bamboo skewers in water for 30 minutes before use to prevent burning.
Ensure a mix of fat and lean meat on each skewer for maximum juiciness.
Adjust chili flakes to control heat level.

recipes.recipe_name: Beef and Mushroom Ragù with Penne
recipes.visual_description: Serve the dish in a clean white porcelain pasta bowl on a light oak bistro table. The base consists of ridged penne pasta thoroughly coated in a thick, savory red tomato sauce. Large 3cm chunks of seared beef are distributed across the top, showing a dark browned exterior and tender interior. Quartered cremini mushrooms and 2cm diced red bell peppers are visible within the sauce. On the side of the bowl, four bright green, steamed broccoli florets are arranged neatly. The plating is professional with moderate negative space. Natural side-lighting highlights the glossy sauce and the textures of the vegetables. A grey cotton napkin and a single fork rest beside the plate.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with freshly grated Parmesan cheese
Accompany with crusty sourdough bread
Pair with a medium-bodied Italian red wine
instructions: Cut beef into 3cm chunks.
Season beef with salt and pepper.
Dice bell pepper into 2cm pieces.
Quarter the mushrooms.
Heat oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat.
Sear beef chunks until browned on all sides. Remove beef.
Add mushrooms and peppers to the pot. Sauté for 5 minutes.
Stir in minced garlic and oregano. Cook for 1 minute.
Pour in crushed tomatoes and beef stock. Return beef to pot.
Simmer on low heat for 45 minutes until beef is tender.
Boil salted water in a large pot.
Cook penne until al dente. Drain and reserve 100ml pasta water.
Steam broccoli florets for 4 minutes until bright green.
Toss pasta with beef ragù. Add pasta water to emulsify sauce.
Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure the beef is seared in batches to maintain high heat.
Use the reserved pasta water to achieve a silky sauce consistency.
Do not overcook the broccoli to maintain its vibrant color and snap.

recipes.recipe_name: Gong Bao Beef and Chicken
recipes.visual_description: The dish features uniform 2cm cubes of seared beef and chicken, glistening in a dark, translucent mahogany glaze. The meats are piled naturally in the center of a wide, shallow celadon-green porcelain bowl. Bright red pieces of snapped dried chilies and whole toasted golden peanuts are scattered throughout the meat. Pale green scallion batons provide a fresh color contrast. The meat surfaces show visible wok-searing marks and a glossy texture. The arrangement is clean, showing the entire bowl with moderate negative space. The bowl sits on a dark wood table next to dark wood chopsticks on a ceramic rest. A small bowl of fluffy white rice is positioned slightly out of focus in the background. Natural side lighting emphasizes the steam and the rich sauce.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed jasmine rice
Pair with a light stir-fried leafy green vegetable
Use chopsticks and individual rice bowls

ingredients.name: Dried red chilies, deseeded and snapped

instructions: Mix meats with 10ml soy sauce, 10ml Shaoxing wine, and 5g cornstarch. Marinate for 20 minutes.
Whisk remaining soy sauce, vinegar, sugar, wine, and cornstarch in a bowl for the sauce.
Heat 30ml oil in a wok over high heat until smoking.
Sear beef cubes until browned. Remove and set aside.
Add chicken cubes to the wok. Cook until the internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove.
Wipe wok. Add 15ml oil. Fry chilies and peppercorns until dark red and fragrant.
Add ginger, garlic, and scallions. Stir-fry for 30 seconds.
Return beef and chicken to the wok. Toss to combine.
Pour in the sauce mixture. Stir-fry rapidly until the sauce thickens and coats the meat.
Fold in roasted peanuts. Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure the wok is extremely hot before adding meat to achieve 'wok hei' flavor.
Do not burn the dried chilies; they should turn dark red, not black.
Velveting the meat with cornstarch ensures a tender texture.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Dopiaza
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Chicken Dopiaza served in a traditional hammered copper kadai bowl. The dish features 4cm chunks of tender braised chicken coated in a thick mahogany-colored onion gravy. Translucent, slightly softened white onion petals are scattered throughout, providing a structural contrast. The surface shows a light sheen of oil from the bhuna technique. A vibrant garnish of coarsely chopped fresh cilantro and julienned ginger sits on top. The bowl rests on a dark wooden table next to a small stainless steel bowl of cucumber raita and a folded piece of charred garlic naan. Warm natural lighting highlights the rich textures of the sauce and the whole chicken pieces.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm garlic naan or basmati rice
Accompany with a side of cooling cucumber raita
Provide a fresh lime wedge and raw onion rings on the side

ingredients.name: Chicken thighs, boneless, cut into 4cm chunks

instructions: Heat oil in a heavy pot over medium heat.
Add cumin seeds and fry until they sizzle.
Add diced red onions to the pot.
Sauté onions until they reach a deep golden brown color.
Stir in the ginger-garlic paste for 1 minute.
Add chicken chunks to the pot.
Brown the chicken on all sides.
Lower the heat and stir in turmeric, coriander, and chili powder.
Add the whisked yogurt slowly while stirring constantly.
Cover and simmer for 15 minutes.
Add the white onion petals and salt.
Cook for 10 minutes until chicken reaches 75°C.
Stir in garam masala and remove from heat.
Garnish with fresh cilantro before serving.
notes: Ensure red onions are deeply caramelized for the authentic base flavor
Do not overcook the second batch of onions to maintain their petal shape
Always use a heavy-bottomed pot to prevent the yogurt from scorching

recipes.recipe_name: Chongqing Spicy Chicken (Laziji)
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Chongqing Spicy Chicken served on a clean white porcelain plate atop a dark walnut wood table. The dish features golden-brown, crispy 2cm cubes of chicken thigh nestled within a vibrant mound of glossy, deep red whole dried chilis and fragrant Sichuan peppercorns. Bright green scallion batons provide a fresh color contrast. The chicken looks crunchy and succulent. Beside the plate sits a small ceramic bowl of fluffy white jasmine rice and a pair of dark bamboo chopsticks resting on a ceramic holder. The lighting is natural and soft, highlighting the textures of the crispy chicken skin and the oily sheen of the chilis. The arrangement is organic and centered with balanced negative space.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of steamed jasmine rice
Pairs well with a cold lager or herbal tea
Pick chicken pieces out from the chilis using chopsticks
instructions: Marinate chicken cubes with soy sauce, wine, and salt for 20 minutes.
Toss chicken with cornstarch to coat evenly.
Heat 500ml oil in a wok to 180°C.
Fry chicken in batches until golden brown. Remove.
Increase oil temperature to 200°C.
Flash-fry chicken for 30 seconds until very crispy.
Ensure chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C. Drain.
Remove all but 2 tbsp of oil from wok.
Sauté ginger and garlic for 30 seconds.
Add dried chilis and Sichuan peppercorns.
Stir-fry on low heat until chilis darken and smell fragrant.
Return chicken to wok.
Add sugar and scallion batons.
Toss quickly on high heat to combine.
Garnish with toasted sesame seeds.
notes: Do not eat the whole dried chilis
Adjust chili quantity to preference
Use high-quality Sichuan peppercorns for the numbing effect

recipes.recipe_name: Kashmiri Dum Aloo
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Kashmiri Dum Aloo served in a traditional hammered copper kadhai. Six whole, golden-brown baby potatoes are submerged in a thick, vibrant deep-red gravy. The gravy has a glossy finish from the mustard oil. The potatoes show a slight textural crust from deep frying. Fresh green cilantro leaves and thin julienne strips of ginger are scattered on top. The kadhai sits on a dark wooden bistro table. A side of charred garlic naan is placed in a small basket lined with a linen cloth. A small brass bowl of cooling cucumber raita and a wedge of lemon accompany the dish. The lighting is warm and natural, highlighting the rich spice colors and the matte texture of the potatoes.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed Basmati rice or Garlic Naan
Accompany with a side of onion laccha salad and lemon wedges
Traditionally served in a copper or brass Kadhai
instructions: Boil baby potatoes in salted water until 70% cooked.
Peel potatoes and prick all over with a toothpick.
Heat mustard oil in a heavy-bottomed pan until smoking, then cool slightly.
Fry potatoes in hot oil until golden brown and crisp on the outside.
Remove potatoes and set aside.
Reduce oil in pan to 2 tablespoons.
Add cumin, cinnamon, cardamom, and cloves to the oil.
Mix chili powder with 2 tablespoons of water to prevent burning.
Pour chili paste into the oil and stir for 30 seconds.
Lower heat and gradually whisk in yogurt to avoid curdling.
Add ginger powder, fennel powder, and salt.
Add fried potatoes and 200 ml water.
Cover with a tight lid and simmer on low heat for 15 minutes.
Garnish with chopped cilantro before serving.
notes: Mustard oil provides the authentic pungent flavor; ensure it reaches smoking point before use.
Pricking the potatoes is essential for the gravy to penetrate the core.
The gravy should be thick and coat the potatoes generously, not watery.

recipes.recipe_name: Mustard-Oregano Roasted Chicken with Parmesan Potato Pavé
recipes.visual_description: A single portion served on a matte white porcelain plate. The focal point is a whole, golden-brown roasted chicken thigh with a visible mustard glaze and flecks of dried oregano. Beside the chicken sits a perfectly square-cut potato pavé block, showing distinct, thin horizontal layers of potato and melted parmesan with crispy browned edges. A neat pile of vibrant, steam-glistening green peas is positioned to the side. A light, translucent mustard-colored jus is drizzled around the base of the chicken. The scene is set on a dark oak wooden table with a folded grey cotton napkin and a silver fork and knife. Natural side-lighting highlights the textures of the crispy chicken skin and the layered potato.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a glass of dry white wine such as Chardonnay
Provide a side of crusty baguette to soak up the mustard jus
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C.
Slice potatoes into 2mm rounds using a mandoline.
Toss potato slices with melted butter, parmesan, half the oregano, salt, and pepper.
Layer potatoes tightly in a lined baking dish. Press down firmly.
Bake potatoes for 45 minutes until tender. Let cool, then cut into 4 large rectangular blocks.
Increase oven temperature to 200°C.
Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper.
Heat oil in an oven-proof skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down for 6 minutes until skin is crisp and golden.
Flip chicken. Brush the skin generously with Dijon mustard.
Add onion, garlic, and remaining oregano to the skillet.
Transfer skillet to the oven. Roast until chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove chicken and onions from the pan. Keep warm.
Place skillet on stovetop. Add chicken stock and deglaze over medium heat for 3 minutes.
Blanch green peas in boiling salted water for 2 minutes. Drain.
Sear the potato pavé blocks in a separate buttered pan until edges are crispy.
Plate one potato block, one whole chicken thigh, and a portion of peas.
notes: Ensure the potato pavé is pressed weighted down while cooling for cleaner edges when cutting
Use a meat thermometer to ensure chicken reaches exactly 75°C for safety and juiciness

recipes.recipe_name: Cantonese Steamed Fish with Ginger and Scallions
recipes.visual_description: A whole steamed sea bass sits centered on a clean, white oval porcelain platter. The fish skin is silver-grey and intact, with white flesh visible through diagonal scores. A vibrant nest of bright green shredded scallions and thin yellow ginger batons sits atop the fish. Fresh green cilantro sprigs are scattered naturally over the aromatics. A dark, translucent soy-based sauce pools at the base of the fish, shimmering with droplets of clear oil. The setting features a dark wood table with a pair of bamboo chopsticks resting on a ceramic holder. A small bowl of fluffy white jasmine rice sits to the side. The lighting is soft and natural, highlighting the moist texture of the fish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as a central shared dish in a multi-course meal
Accompany with steamed jasmine rice
Provide a communal spoon and chopsticks for portioning
Pair with a light green tea or Oolong tea

ingredients.name: Whole sea bass, cleaned and scaled
Scallions, cut into 5cm batons and shredded

instructions: Rinse the fish and pat dry with paper towels.
Make three shallow diagonal slashes on both sides of the fish.
Place half of the ginger batons inside the fish cavity.
Place the fish on a heatproof oval ceramic platter.
Scatter the remaining ginger batons over the top of the fish.
Set up a steamer over boiling water.
Place the platter inside the steamer.
Steam the fish over high heat for 10 to 12 minutes.
Ensure the internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Carefully remove the platter from the steamer.
Drain and discard any liquid collected on the platter.
Combine soy sauce, sugar, hot water, and white pepper in a small bowl.
Pour the sauce mixture around the base of the fish.
Place the shredded scallions and cilantro directly on top of the fish.
Heat peanut oil in a small saucepan until it begins to smoke.
Pour the hot oil over the scallions and cilantro to sizzle.
Serve immediately with steamed rice.
notes: Use the freshest fish possible with clear eyes for best results.
Do not overcook the fish; the flesh should just turn opaque and flake easily.
The sizzling oil is essential to release the aroma of the ginger and scallions.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Saltimbocca with Fettuccine
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of glossy fettuccine is nested in the center of a clean white porcelain plate. The pasta is coated in a pale gold, translucent butter sauce. Three thick chunks of golden-seared chicken are placed naturally on top of the pasta. Each chicken piece displays a crisp, mahogany-colored prosciutto wrap and a visible sage leaf. Two thick wedges of toasted ciabatta with dark grill marks lean against the side of the pasta nest. The dish is finished with a fine dusting of Parmigiano-Reggiano and small torn sage leaves. The plate sits on a rustic dark wood table in a modern bistro setting, illuminated by soft natural side light. A folded white cotton napkin and a polished silver fork are placed to the right.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a glass of crisp Frascati or Pinot Grigio.
Present with additional Parmigiano-Reggiano on the side for guests to add.
Include a small bowl for discarded toothpicks if used during cooking.

ingredients.name: Chicken breast, halved into thick chunks
Ciabatta loaf, cut into thick wedges

instructions: Boil a large pot of salted water.
Cook fettuccine until al dente.
Press one sage leaf and one prosciutto slice onto each chicken chunk.
Secure with a toothpick if necessary.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken prosciutto-side down for 3 minutes until crispy.
Flip chicken and cook until the internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove chicken from the pan and keep warm.
Add garlic to the skillet and sauté for 30 seconds.
Deglaze the pan with white wine, scraping the bottom.
Add chicken stock and simmer until reduced by half.
Whisk in cold butter until the sauce is glossy and emulsified.
Stir in lemon juice.
Toss the cooked pasta into the sauce until well coated.
Brush ciabatta wedges with olive oil and toast until golden.
Plate the pasta immediately and top with chicken chunks.
notes: Ensure the butter is cold when whisking into the sauce to create a proper emulsion.
Do not over-salt the chicken, as the prosciutto provides significant saltiness.
Save 50ml of pasta water to loosen the sauce if it becomes too thick.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Dopiaza
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Chicken Dopiaza served in a traditional hammered copper kadai bowl. The dish features 4cm chunks of tender braised chicken coated in a thick mahogany-colored onion gravy. Translucent, slightly softened white onion petals are scattered throughout, providing a structural contrast. The surface shows a light sheen of oil from the bhuna technique. A vibrant garnish of coarsely chopped fresh cilantro and julienned ginger sits on top. The bowl rests on a dark wooden table next to a small stainless steel bowl of cucumber raita and a folded piece of charred garlic naan. Warm natural lighting highlights the rich textures of the sauce and the whole chicken pieces.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm garlic naan or basmati rice
Accompany with a side of cooling cucumber raita
Provide a fresh lime wedge and raw onion rings on the side

ingredients.name: Chicken thighs, boneless, cut into 4cm chunks

instructions: Heat oil in a heavy pot over medium heat.
Add cumin seeds and fry until they sizzle.
Add diced red onions to the pot.
Sauté onions until they reach a deep golden brown color.
Stir in the ginger-garlic paste for 1 minute.
Add chicken chunks to the pot.
Brown the chicken on all sides.
Lower the heat and stir in turmeric, coriander, and chili powder.
Add the whisked yogurt slowly while stirring constantly.
Cover and simmer for 15 minutes.
Add the white onion petals and salt.
Cook for 10 minutes until chicken reaches 75°C.
Stir in garam masala and remove from heat.
Garnish with fresh cilantro before serving.
notes: Ensure red onions are deeply caramelized for the authentic base flavor
Do not overcook the second batch of onions to maintain their petal shape
Always use a heavy-bottomed pot to prevent the yogurt from scorching

recipes.recipe_name: Rigatoni with Salami and Whipped Ricotta
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of rigatoni is presented in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl on a light oak table. The ridged pasta tubes are coated in a glossy, translucent sauce. Thick 1cm cubes of seared salami are nestled between the pasta, showing a deep mahogany crust. Strips of bright red sun-dried tomatoes and dark green wilted spinach leaves are distributed evenly throughout the bowl. Three large, soft dollops of snowy white whipped ricotta are placed on top, finished with fresh lemon zest and cracked black pepper. The lighting is natural and soft from the side. A crisp white linen napkin and a polished silver fork sit to the right. The arrangement is clean with ample negative space.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty ciabatta bread
Pair with a dry red wine like Chianti
Present in shallow ceramic bowls
instructions: Boil a large pot of salted water.
Cook rigatoni until al dente.
Reserve 200ml of pasta cooking water.
Whisk ricotta with lemon zest and black pepper until smooth.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Sauté salami cubes until edges are crisp and browned.
Add minced garlic and julienned sun-dried tomatoes.
Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add cooked pasta and 100ml of reserved pasta water to the skillet.
Toss in baby spinach.
Stir until spinach is just wilted.
Add Pecorino Romano and remaining water as needed to create a glossy sauce.
Remove from heat.
Plate pasta and top with three large dollops of whipped ricotta.
notes: Ensure the pasta water is very salty like the sea.
Do not overcook the spinach; it should remain vibrant green.
Whipping the ricotta adds a professional, airy texture to the final dish.

recipes.recipe_name: Pollo alla Cacciatora con Pasta
recipes.special_requests: Italian cuisine, appropriate for an older person with high cholesterol
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Pollo alla Cacciatora served on a rustic, off-white ceramic plate. Large, succulent chunks of golden-browned chicken breast are nestled among al dente penne pasta. The sauce is a chunky, vibrant red tomato base featuring softened strips of red bell pepper, earthy sliced mushrooms, and small diced orange carrots. Fresh green basil leaves are torn and scattered across the top, adding a pop of color. To the side, a small pile of crisp, dark green salad leaves offers a fresh contrast. The plate sits on a weathered wooden kitchen table next to a simple stainless steel fork and a textured linen napkin. Soft, natural morning light illuminates the textures of the braised vegetables and the steam rising from the dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve in a shallow bowl to capture the rustic sauce
Accompany with a glass of room-temperature water or a light red wine
Enjoy as a 'piatto unico' (complete single-course meal)

ingredients.name: Red bell pepper, cut into thin strips

instructions: Boil pasta in salted water until al dente. Drain and set aside.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat.
Brown chicken chunks until golden on all sides. Remove from pan.
Add remaining oil, onion, and carrot to the same pan. Sauté 5 minutes.
Add bell pepper strips, mushrooms, garlic, and chili. Cook for 3 minutes.
Pour in crushed tomatoes. Simmer for 10 minutes until sauce thickens.
Return chicken to the pan. Simmer until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C.
Toss the cooked pasta into the sauce. Stir in fresh basil.
Serve immediately with a side of fresh salad greens.
notes: Using chicken breast and extra virgin olive oil makes this dish heart-healthy and lower in saturated fat.
Whole wheat pasta can be substituted for extra fiber to further manage cholesterol levels.
Do not overcook the pasta; 'al dente' texture is essential for authentic Italian preparation.

recipes.recipe_name: Pollo en Salsa de Chiles Fermentados
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of two whole, skin-on chicken pieces sits centered in a handmade, shallow matte-terracotta cazuela. The chicken is smothered in a thick, vibrant deep-red salsa roja, showing visible charred specks from the tatemado process. To the side, three thick carrot batons and several golden-brown sautéed mushroom quarters are neatly placed. A small, separate mound of vibrant salad greens mixed with fresh basil leaves and carrot-top fronds provides a bright green contrast. The dish is presented on a dark, reclaimed wood table with a hand-woven linen napkin. Natural afternoon light creates soft shadows, highlighting the glossy texture of the sauce and the rustic finish of the pottery.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas kept in a cloth-lined basket
Accompany with a small bowl of fermented vegetable pickles
Provide a traditional spoon for the rich salsa

ingredients.name: Fermented chili and garlic paste (prepared 1 week prior)

instructions: Pat chicken dry and season with salt.
Heat oil in a heavy cazuela or pot over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken pieces until skin is golden. Remove chicken.
Place tomatoes, half the onions, and bell peppers on a dry comal or cast-iron pan.
Char vegetables until skins are blackened and flesh is soft (tatemado).
Blend charred vegetables with fermented chili paste and 100ml water until smooth.
Return sauce to the pot. Add chicken pieces.
Simmer covered until chicken reaches internal temperature of 75°C.
Sauté mushrooms and carrot batons in a separate pan until tender.
Toss salad greens and basil with carrot tops for a zero-waste side.
Serve chicken whole in the sauce with mushrooms and carrots arranged alongside.
notes: Use chicken carcasses and vegetable scraps to create a stock for future use.
Fermented chili paste is made by brining chilies and garlic in 3% salt water for 7 days.
Ensure the sauce reaches a simmer before adding chicken to maintain food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Greek Braised Chicken with Tomato and Peppers
recipes.visual_description: A single whole braised chicken thigh sits centered on a wide, white porcelain plate. The chicken skin is deeply browned and glossy, coated in a thick, rich tomato-based sauce. Surrounding the chicken are large chunks of softened red bell peppers and thick orange carrot rounds. Diced onions and minced garlic are visible within the rustic, textured sauce. A small, vibrant pile of fresh green salad leaves is placed neatly on the side of the plate for contrast. The dish is finished with a light sprinkle of dried oregano and a drizzle of olive oil. The plate is set on a light wood table with a linen napkin and a piece of crusty bread nearby. Natural lighting emphasizes the rich reds and deep browns of the braise.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty sourdough bread to soak up the sauce
Accompany with a side of Greek feta cheese
Pair with a glass of Agiorgitiko red wine

ingredients.name: Bell peppers, cut into large chunks

instructions: Heat 30 ml olive oil in a heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat.
Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper.
Brown chicken for 5 minutes per side until skin is crisp.
Remove chicken and set aside on a plate.
Add remaining olive oil to the pot.
Sauté diced onion, carrot rounds, and bell pepper chunks for 8 minutes.
Stir in minced garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add crushed tomatoes, water, oregano, and cinnamon.
Return chicken thighs to the pot, skin side up.
Reduce heat to low and cover with a lid.
Simmer for 35 minutes.
Check chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Serve chicken with the vegetable sauce and fresh salad greens.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C for safety
Cinnamon is a traditional Greek addition to tomato-based stews
The sauce should be thick and reduced, not watery

recipes.recipe_name: Beef and Mushroom Mole Estofado
recipes.visual_description: The dish features large 4cm chunks of tender braised beef and halved cremini mushrooms, heavily coated in a glossy, deep mahogany-colored chocolate-infused sauce. Served in a traditional rustic matte-black clay bowl, the beef chunks are piled naturally in the center, showing a moist, fibrous texture. The sauce is thick and velvety, clinging to the meat. Garnishes include a sprinkle of vibrant green chopped cilantro and thin rings of crisp white onion for contrast. Beside the bowl sits a small stack of warm, hand-pressed corn tortillas wrapped in a clean white cloth napkin. The setting is a dark wood table under soft, natural light, emphasizing the rich, earthy textures and deep colors of the stew.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Warm corn tortillas
Fresh lime wedges
Pickled red onions
instructions: Cut beef into 4cm chunks. Pat dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat oil in a heavy-based pot over medium-high heat.
Sear beef chunks in batches until deep brown on all sides. Remove beef.
Dice onions into 1cm pieces. Halve the mushrooms.
Add onions and mushrooms to the pot. Sauté for 8 minutes until browned.
Add minced garlic, chili powder, and cinnamon. Stir for 1 minute.
Pour in beef stock. Return beef to the pot.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 90 minutes or until beef is tender.
Finely chop the dark chocolate. Stir into the pot until melted.
Simmer uncovered for 10 minutes to thicken the sauce. Adjust salt.
notes: Use 70% cocoa dark chocolate for a savory depth without excess sweetness.
Do not boil the sauce vigorously after adding chocolate to maintain a smooth texture.

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Braised Lentils with Roasted Peppers
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of braised brown lentils served in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl. The lentils are glossy and moist, arranged in a natural mound in the center. Interspersed throughout the lentils are thick batons of roasted red and yellow bell peppers, showing distinct charred edges and softened texture. Large, rustic chunks of creamy white feta cheese are scattered on top, not crumbled finely. A vibrant green herb oil drizzle circles the lentils. Fresh flat-leaf parsley leaves provide a final garnish. The background features a light oak wood table with a linen napkin and a silver spoon. The lighting is bright and natural, highlighting the contrast between the dark lentils and bright peppers.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm sourdough or pita bread
Accompany with Kalamata olives
Pair with a crisp Assyrtiko white wine

ingredients.name: red bell peppers, deseeded and cut into thick batons
yellow bell peppers, deseeded and cut into thick batons
feta cheese, broken into large chunks

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Toss bell pepper batons with 15ml olive oil and salt.
Spread peppers on a baking sheet.
Roast for 20 minutes until edges are charred.
Heat remaining olive oil in a heavy pot.
Sauté onion and garlic until translucent.
Stir in lentils, bay leaf, and thyme.
Add vegetable stock and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer for 25 minutes.
Cook until lentils are tender but retain their shape.
Drain any excess liquid if necessary.
Whisk lemon juice and smoked paprika together.
Fold roasted peppers and lemon dressing into the warm lentils.
Season with salt and black pepper.
Top with large feta chunks and fresh parsley.
notes: Do not overcook the lentils to prevent a mushy texture.
Use high-quality Greek feta stored in brine for best flavor.

recipes.recipe_name: Beef and Mushroom Donburi
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Beef and Mushroom Donburi served in a deep, textured indigo ceramic bowl. The base is a fluffy mound of steamed white short-grain rice. Atop the rice, glossy 3cm chunks of simmered beef are clustered with thick-sliced earthy shiitake mushrooms and soft, translucent onion wedges. The ingredients are coated in a dark, shimmering savory glaze. A small, vibrant mound of bright red julienned pickled ginger sits to one side. Finely chopped green onion rings provide a fresh green contrast. The bowl sits on a light oak wood table. A pair of dark wooden chopsticks rests on a ceramic holder to the right. Natural, soft window light highlights the moist textures of the meat.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of miso soup
Accompany with hot green tea
Provide chopsticks and a deep ceramic spoon
instructions: Rinse rice until water runs clear. Cook rice with 360ml water until tender.
Heat oil in a large deep skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear beef chunks until browned on all sides. Remove beef from pan.
Add sliced onions and mushrooms to the same pan. Sauté for 4 minutes.
Pour in dashi, soy sauce, mirin, and sugar. Bring to a simmer.
Return beef to the pan. Reduce heat to medium-low.
Simmer for 10 minutes until the sauce reduces slightly and onions are translucent.
Divide steamed rice into four deep ceramic bowls.
Top each bowl with beef chunks, mushrooms, and onions.
Ladle remaining simmering liquid over the beef and rice.
Garnish with green onions and a small mound of pickled ginger.
notes: Ensure the beef is not overcooked during the initial sear to keep the chunks tender during simmering.
Use high-quality dashi for a deeper umami profile.

recipes.recipe_name: New England Lobster Roll
recipes.visual_description: A single portion featuring a golden-brown, butter-toasted split-top brioche bun resting on a clean white porcelain plate. The bun is packed with large, succulent chunks of red-tipped white lobster meat. The meat is coated in a light, glossy mayonnaise dressing that does not drip. Visible specks of finely diced green celery are mixed throughout. The top is garnished with bright green chopped chives and a subtle sprinkle of red smoked paprika. The plate sits on a rustic light wood bistro table. A side of thick-cut kettle chips and a single lemon wedge provide contrast. The lighting is natural and soft, highlighting the textures of the crusty bread and tender seafood.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of kettle-cooked potato chips
Include a crisp dill pickle spear
Accompany with a side of creamy coleslaw
Serve with a cold craft lager or sparkling water
instructions: Cut lobster meat into large 2cm chunks.
Whisk mayonnaise, lemon juice, salt, and pepper in a bowl.
Fold lobster meat and diced celery into the dressing.
Melt butter in a skillet over medium heat.
Toast the sides of the brioche buns until golden brown.
Fill each bun generously with the lobster mixture.
Garnish with chopped chives and a light dusting of paprika.
Serve immediately while the bun is warm and lobster is chilled.
notes: Ensure the lobster meat is thoroughly chilled before mixing with mayonnaise.
Do not over-mix the lobster to keep the chunks intact.
Use high-quality brioche for the best buttery flavor and soft texture.

recipes.recipe_name: Pasta e Patate con Provola
recipes.visual_description: A deep white porcelain bowl holds a thick, creamy pasta and potato stew. The pasta consists of mixed short shapes coated in a rich, glossy starch emulsion. Small 1cm cubes of tender yellow potato are distributed evenly throughout the dish. Halved cherry tomatoes provide bright red accents against the golden-hued sauce. Strands of melted smoked provola cheese are visible, stretching through the mixture. A single whole sprig of fresh basil sits as a central garnish. The dish is presented on a rustic dark wood table. A folded white cotton napkin and a polished silver spoon lie beside the bowl. Natural daylight highlights the creamy, velvety texture of the sauce. The plate remains clean with ample negative space around the rim.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with toasted sourdough bread for scarpetta
Pair with a chilled glass of Gragnano or light red wine
Serve in wide, shallow ceramic bowls

ingredients.name: Starchy yellow potatoes, peeled and cut into 1cm cubes
Mixed short pasta shapes (Pasta Mista) or Ditalini
Smoked Provola or Scamorza cheese, diced small
Celery, carrot, and onion, finely diced

instructions: Heat olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot.
Sauté celery, carrot, onion, and garlic over medium heat for 5 minutes.
Add cherry tomatoes and cook until they release their juices.
Stir in potato cubes and cook for 5 minutes until edges soften.
Add enough hot stock to cover potatoes and simmer for 15 minutes.
Add pasta directly into the pot with the potatoes.
Cook pasta until al dente, stirring frequently and adding stock as needed to maintain a creamy consistency.
Turn off heat when pasta is cooked and most liquid is absorbed.
Stir in smoked cheese and Parmigiano vigorously to create a creamy emulsion.
Fold in fresh basil and season with black pepper.
notes: The consistency should be 'azzeccato' (thick and creamy), not a liquid soup.
Stirring the pasta frequently releases starches necessary for the sauce texture.

recipes.recipe_name: Latin-Style Braised Chicken and Annatto Rice
recipes.visual_description: The dish features a generous portion of vibrant golden-yellow annatto rice mixed with bright yellow corn kernels, served on a rustic, off-white ceramic plate. Next to the rice, a whole braised chicken thigh sits submerged in a rich, red-orange tomato sauce. Thick chunks of tender potato and cubes of soft eggplant are scattered throughout the stew. Sliced mushrooms and red beans add varied textures. The arrangement is casual and home-style, with the sauce slightly bleeding into the rice. Freshly torn green basil leaves and sliced pickled jalapeños provide a vibrant garnish. The entire plate is visible on a worn wooden table, illuminated by warm, soft kitchen light, creating a cozy, authentic atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of sliced avocado
Accompany with extra hot sauce on the table
Pair with the remaining cold lager beer
instructions: Heat oil and annatto seeds in a heavy pot.
Strain and discard seeds once oil turns bright orange.
Brown chicken pieces in 2 tablespoons of annatto oil.
Remove chicken and set aside.
Sauté onion, garlic, chili, mushrooms, and eggplant in the same pot.
Add tomatoes, oregano, and cayenne pepper.
Pour in beer and add potatoes and beans.
Return chicken to the pot and cover.
Simmer for 30 minutes until chicken reaches 75°C internally.
Boil rice with remaining annatto oil, corn, and 800ml water in a separate pot.
Cover rice and simmer on low for 15 minutes.
Serve chicken stew directly over a bed of yellow rice.
Garnish with hot sauce, fresh basil, and pickled jalapeños.
notes: Do not boil the annatto seeds too long or they become bitter.
Ensure chicken reaches the safe internal temperature of 75°C.
The eggplant absorbs the braising liquid, adding richness to the sauce.

recipes.recipe_name: Lomo Saltado
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Lomo Saltado presented on a clean white porcelain plate. The dish features 3cm chunks of seared beef sirloin with a deep brown crust. These are mixed with thick, glossy wedges of purple red onion and bright red Roma tomatoes. Golden, thick-cut potato batons are scattered through the beef mixture, all coated in a dark, shimmering sauce. A neat, molded dome of fluffy white rice sits on the side of the plate. Fresh green cilantro leaves garnish the top. The scene is set on a light wooden bistro table with a white cotton napkin and a small side bowl of spicy green aji sauce. The lighting is natural and even.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of Aji Verde (green chili sauce)
Accompany with Inca Kola or a glass of red wine
Traditionally eaten with both rice and potatoes in the same meal

ingredients.name: Red onions, cut into thick wedges
Roma tomatoes, cut into thick wedges

instructions: Season beef chunks with salt and pepper.
Heat 2 tablespoons of oil in a wok over high heat until smoking.
Sear beef in batches until browned and medium-rare.
Remove beef from wok and set aside.
Add remaining oil to the wok.
Stir-fry onion wedges for 2 minutes until slightly charred but crisp.
Add garlic and aji amarillo paste. Stir for 30 seconds.
Return beef to the wok.
Pour in soy sauce and red wine vinegar. Toss quickly.
Add tomato wedges. Stir for 30 seconds to warm through.
Fold in the cooked potato fries and half the cilantro.
Remove from heat immediately.
Serve with white rice.
notes: Ensure the wok is extremely hot before adding beef to achieve a smoky flavor.
Do not overcook the tomatoes; they should be warm but hold their shape.
The potatoes should be added at the very last second to maintain some crispness.

recipes.recipe_name: Vanilla-Poached Potato Pavé with White Chocolate Miso Crémeux
recipes.visual_description: A single 4cm golden-brown caramelized potato pavé cube sits off-center on a matte charcoal designer plate. The pavé shows distinct, paper-thin horizontal layers. Three spherical, velvet-textured dollops of ivory-colored miso crémeux are placed in an organic curve following the pavé. A fine, sandy brown butter soil is scattered at the base of the pavé, suggesting a natural landscape. The lighting is dramatic and directional, casting soft shadows across a white Carrara marble surface. A pristine white linen napkin is folded into a precise triangle in the background. The composition uses significant negative space to emphasize the architectural precision of the potato cube and the smooth texture of the crémeux.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as a final course with a glass of Sauternes or late-harvest Riesling.
Present on warmed bone china to maintain the temperature contrast between the warm pavé and cold crémeux.
instructions: Slice potatoes into 1mm translucent rounds using a mandoline.
Whisk clarified butter with 50g sugar and vanilla seeds.
Line a rectangular terrine mold with parchment paper.
Layer potato slices tightly, brushing each layer with the vanilla butter.
Cover with parchment and bake at 150°C for 90 minutes under a heavy weight.
Chill the pavé for 12 hours while compressed.
Bring cream and miso to a simmer. Pour over white chocolate and whisk until smooth.
Blend 100g of cooked potato scraps into the chocolate mixture until emulsified. Chill until firm.
Rub almond flour, all-purpose flour, remaining sugar, and brown butter into crumbs.
Bake crumbs at 160°C for 12 minutes until golden to create the soil.
Unmold pavé and trim into 4cm x 4cm cubes.
Sear pavé cubes in a hot pan with a small amount of butter until all sides are caramelized.
Place one pavé cube on a plate. Pipe three precise dots of crémeux alongside.
Scatter brown butter soil around the base and garnish with a touch of sea salt.
notes: Ensure the potato layers are pressed firmly during chilling to prevent the pavé from separating during searing.
Use Yukon Gold potatoes for their high starch content and buttery flavor profile.

recipes.recipe_name: Beef and Mushroom Arroz Meloso
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented in a shallow white porcelain bowl. The rice has a fluid, glossy meloso consistency, spreading naturally across the plate. Large 3cm chunks of seared beef and quartered golden-brown mushrooms sit prominently on the surface. Bright green peas and 1cm red bell pepper cubes are distributed evenly, providing vibrant color contrast. The sauce is a rich, translucent reddish-brown from the tomato and paprika. The plate is clean with moderate negative space around the edges. It is set on a light oak wood table. A folded white cotton napkin and a polished silver spoon lie to the right. Natural side lighting highlights the steam and the moist texture of the rice.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty rustic bread
Pair with a medium-bodied Spanish red wine
Garnish with a sprig of fresh parsley
instructions: Cut beef into 3cm chunks and season with salt.
Heat oil in a wide pan over medium-high heat.
Sear beef chunks until browned on all sides. Remove beef from pan.
Sauté quartered mushrooms in the same pan until golden. Remove mushrooms.
Add finely diced onion and 1cm diced bell pepper. Cook until softened.
Stir in minced garlic and smoked paprika. Cook for 30 seconds.
Add pureed tomatoes. Cook until the liquid evaporates and the mixture darkens.
Add rice to the pan. Toast for 2 minutes while stirring constantly.
Pour in 1 liter of warm chicken stock.
Simmer over medium heat for 15 minutes. Stir occasionally.
Return beef and mushrooms to the pan. Add green peas.
Add remaining stock to achieve a fluid, honey-like consistency.
Cook for 3 minutes until rice is tender but firm.
Rest for 2 minutes. Serve immediately in shallow bowls.
notes: Ensure the stock is warm before adding to the rice to maintain cooking temperature.
The rice should be 'al dente' with a slight bite in the center.
Do not let the rice dry out; the consistency should be fluid and free-flowing.

recipes.recipe_name: Casarecce with Gorgonzola, Pear, and Lemon
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean white porcelain plate centered on a rustic oak table. The Casarecce pasta is coated in a glossy, pale ivory Gorgonzola sauce, showing a fluid, silky consistency. Interspersed throughout the pasta are 1.5cm cubes of sautéed pear, appearing slightly translucent with golden edges. Toasted walnut pieces are scattered over the top, providing a dark brown textural contrast. Bright yellow threads of fresh lemon zest and tiny green thyme leaves are sprinkled across the surface. The arrangement is natural and free-flowing, filling the center of the plate while leaving a clear margin. A single linen napkin and a stainless steel fork sit beside the dish under natural light.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve in a shallow pasta bowl
Pair with a crisp glass of Pinot Grigio or Soave
Follow with a light arugula salad

ingredients.name: firm-ripe Pears (Abate or Bosc), diced into 1.5cm cubes

instructions: Boil a large pot of salted water.
Cook pasta until al dente.
Toast walnuts in a dry pan until fragrant.
Melt butter in a large skillet over medium heat.
Sauté shallots for 2 minutes until translucent.
Add pear cubes to the skillet.
Sauté pears for 3 minutes until slightly softened.
Pour in heavy cream and crumbled Gorgonzola.
Stir gently until cheese melts and sauce thickens.
Reserve 100ml pasta water and drain the pasta.
Add pasta to the skillet with the sauce.
Add lemon juice and half the lemon zest.
Toss pasta and add reserved water for a fluid consistency.
Fold in half the walnuts, Parmigiano-Reggiano, and thyme.
Season with salt and cracked black pepper.
Plate immediately.
notes: Use Gorgonzola Dolce for a creamier, milder flavor profile.
Ensure pears are firm so they maintain their shape during sautéing.
Do not overcook the pasta as it will continue to cook in the sauce.

recipes.recipe_name: Casarecce with Gorgonzola, Pear, and Lemon
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean white porcelain plate centered on a rustic oak table. The Casarecce pasta is coated in a glossy, pale ivory Gorgonzola sauce, showing a fluid, silky consistency. Interspersed throughout the pasta are 1.5cm cubes of sautéed pear, appearing slightly translucent with golden edges. Toasted walnut pieces are scattered over the top, providing a dark brown textural contrast. Bright yellow threads of fresh lemon zest and tiny green thyme leaves are sprinkled across the surface. The arrangement is natural and free-flowing, filling the center of the plate while leaving a clear margin. A single linen napkin and a stainless steel fork sit beside the dish under natural light.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve in a shallow pasta bowl
Pair with a crisp glass of Pinot Grigio or Soave
Follow with a light arugula salad

ingredients.name: firm-ripe Pears (Abate or Bosc), diced into 1.5cm cubes

instructions: Boil a large pot of salted water.
Cook pasta until al dente.
Toast walnuts in a dry pan until fragrant.
Melt butter in a large skillet over medium heat.
Sauté shallots for 2 minutes until translucent.
Add pear cubes to the skillet.
Sauté pears for 3 minutes until slightly softened.
Pour in heavy cream and crumbled Gorgonzola.
Stir gently until cheese melts and sauce thickens.
Reserve 100ml pasta water and drain the pasta.
Add pasta to the skillet with the sauce.
Add lemon juice and half the lemon zest.
Toss pasta and add reserved water for a fluid consistency.
Fold in half the walnuts, Parmigiano-Reggiano, and thyme.
Season with salt and cracked black pepper.
Plate immediately.
