recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Creamy Dijon Sauce and Roasted Asparagus
recipes.visual_description: A golden-brown, pan-seared chicken breast, cooked whole, rests centrally on a clean white porcelain plate. Its exterior boasts a beautiful, even crust, while the interior promises succulence. Alongside, a vibrant cluster of roasted asparagus spears, tender-crisp with slightly caramelized tips, adds a striking green contrast. These spears are presented as whole pieces. A creamy Dijon mustard sauce, rich and glistening, is spooned gracefully around the chicken, enhancing its appeal without overwhelming the plate. The dish is finished with a light sprinkle of fresh, chopped parsley for a touch of herbaceousness and color. The presentation is balanced and organized, allowing moderate negative space. Served on a simple wooden table, with natural lighting, reflecting a modern bistro style.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Pat chicken breasts dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat 1 tbsp olive oil in an oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken breasts for 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown.
Transfer skillet to preheated oven. Roast for 10-12 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken, let rest.
While chicken roasts, trim woody ends from asparagus. Toss with 1 tbsp olive oil, salt, and pepper.
Roast asparagus on a baking sheet for 8-10 minutes until tender-crisp.
Return skillet to stovetop over medium heat. Add butter. Sauté shallot until softened, about 2 minutes.
Add garlic and thyme. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Deglaze with chicken broth, scraping up browned bits. Simmer for 2 minutes.
Stir in Dijon mustard and heavy cream. Bring to a gentle simmer. Cook until slightly thickened, about 3-4 minutes.
Stir in lemon juice. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Serve whole chicken breasts with creamy Dijon sauce and roasted asparagus. Garnish with fresh parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Rustic Chicken and Root Vegetable Soup with Savory
recipes.visual_description: The Rustic Chicken and Root Vegetable Soup is presented in a deep, clean white porcelain bowl. The rich, golden-brown broth is clear, with visible chunks of uniformly diced carrots, celery, onion, and potatoes. Tender, shredded chicken pieces are interspersed throughout the soup, showcasing its hearty texture. Thinly sliced leeks add a delicate green and white contrast. The soup is garnished generously with vibrant, freshly chopped parsley scattered over the surface, providing a pop of bright green color and freshness. The arrangement is natural and inviting, with moderate negative space in the bowl. The setting features a simple wooden table surface, a standard European soup spoon, and a crisp cotton napkin, creating a modern bistro atmosphere with natural, even lighting. The entire bowl is visible, displaying a single, balanced individual portion.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty artisanal bread for dipping.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs 4 minutes per side until golden brown. Remove chicken. Set aside.
Dice carrots, celery, and onion into 1 cm cubes. Thinly slice leek. Mince garlic.
Add diced onion, carrots, celery, and sliced leek to the pot. Sauté 8-10 minutes until softened. Stir in minced garlic. Cook 1 minute more.
Pour in a splash of chicken broth. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot.
Add remaining chicken broth, diced potatoes, and fresh savory to the pot. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared chicken thighs to the pot. Ensure chicken is fully submerged. Simmer 20-25 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C.
Remove chicken from the pot. Shred chicken using two forks.
Return shredded chicken to the soup. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Chop fresh parsley. Ladle soup into bowls. Garnish with fresh parsley before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Beef and Mushroom Stuffed Bell Peppers
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Beef and Mushroom Stuffed Bell Peppers is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Two vibrant bell pepper halves, one red and one yellow, are generously filled with a rich, savory ground beef and mushroom mixture. The topping of melted mozzarella cheese is golden-brown and bubbly, with slight charring at the edges. A scattering of fresh green basil leaves and a light dusting of grated Parmesan cheese garnish the dish. The peppers are arranged organically, allowing the textures and colors of the filling and cheese to be prominent. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple wooden table surface, a neatly folded cotton napkin beside the plate, and traditional Italian flatware. Natural, even lighting highlights the appealing colors and textures.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty Italian bread to soak up the savory sauce.
Pair with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C (375°F).
Halve bell peppers lengthwise. Remove seeds and membranes. Place cut-side up in a baking dish.
Bring a pot of water to a boil. Blanch bell pepper halves for 3 minutes. Drain and set aside.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add diced onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add ground beef to the skillet. Cook, breaking it apart, until browned. Drain excess fat.
Stir in finely diced mushrooms. Cook until mushrooms soften and release their liquid, about 5 minutes.
Pour in crushed tomatoes and beef stock. Add dried oregano. Season with salt and black pepper.
Simmer for 10 minutes, allowing flavors to meld and sauce to thicken slightly.
Remove from heat. Stir in breadcrumbs, chopped fresh basil, and half of the grated Parmesan cheese.
Spoon the beef mixture generously into each blanched bell pepper half.
Top each stuffed pepper with shredded mozzarella cheese.
Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until peppers are tender and cheese is melted and bubbly golden brown.
Serve immediately, garnished with remaining fresh basil and Parmesan.

recipes.recipe_name: Poulet Braisé au Vin Blanc avec Champignons et Légumes
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of French braised chicken is presented in a deep, clean white porcelain bowl. A golden-brown, crisp-skinned chicken thigh (whole, not sliced) is nestled prominently. Surrounding the chicken are tender, creamy white halved new potatoes, earthy brown quartered cremini mushrooms, and vibrant orange thick-cut carrot chunks. The rich, amber-hued braising sauce coats the ingredients with a glossy sheen. A generous sprinkle of bright green chopped fresh parsley adds a final touch of color and freshness. The dish is set on a simple wooden table, accompanied by classic silver flatware and a neatly folded white cotton napkin, evoking a modern bistro atmosphere with natural, even lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a crusty baguette to soak up the delicious sauce
Pair with a glass of the same dry white wine used in the dish
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Lightly dredge chicken thighs in flour, shaking off excess.

Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat. Sear chicken skin-side down for 5-7 minutes until golden brown and crispy. Flip chicken. Sear other side for 3-4 minutes. Remove chicken from pot and set aside.
Quarter mushrooms. Roughly chop onion. Cut carrots into thick rounds or chunks. Mince garlic.
Add chopped onion and carrot to the pot. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened.
Add quartered mushrooms. Cook for 5 minutes until browned.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in dry white wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot (deglazing). Simmer for 2 minutes.
Add chicken broth, halved or quartered new potatoes, fresh thyme sprigs, and bay leaf. Bring the liquid to a gentle simmer.
Return seared chicken thighs to the pot, nestling them among the vegetables and liquid. Ensure chicken is partially submerged.
Cover the pot. Reduce heat to low. Braise for 30-40 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) and potatoes are tender.
Remove chicken, potatoes, and vegetables from the pot. Discard thyme sprigs and bay leaf. Keep warm.
Increase heat to medium-high. Reduce the braising liquid for 5-10 minutes, until it slightly thickens to a desired consistency. Stir in unsalted butter until melted and incorporated.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Return chicken and vegetables to the sauce. Chop fresh parsley.
Garnish with chopped parsley. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Apple and Cinnamon Bread Pudding
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous square portion of warm Apple and Cinnamon Bread Pudding is presented on a simple, round white ceramic dessert plate. The pudding has a rich, golden-brown crust on top, lightly dusted with powdered sugar, offering a subtle contrast. The interior reveals a soft, custardy texture with tender, cooked apple cubes interspersed throughout, showing natural shades of creamy yellow and pale red. The bread pieces are visibly plump from absorbing the custard. The pudding sits naturally in the center of the plate, with no rigid edges, conveying a homemade feel. The plate rests on a well-used wooden dining table, with a casually placed cloth napkin and a simple dessert fork beside it, under warm, cozy kitchen lighting.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Grease a 20x20 cm baking dish with 5g butter.
Cut stale bread into 2-3 cm cubes. Peel, core, and dice apples into 1 cm cubes.
Melt 15g butter in a large pan over medium heat. Add diced apples. Cook 5-7 minutes until slightly softened.
Stir in 10g sugar and half of the cinnamon with the apples. Remove from heat.
In a large bowl, whisk eggs, remaining sugar, milk, cream, vanilla, and lemon zest until well combined.
Add bread cubes and sautéed apples to the egg mixture. Gently fold to coat all bread pieces.
Let the mixture stand for 10 minutes. This allows bread to absorb liquid.
Pour mixture into the prepared baking dish.
Bake 30-35 minutes, or until golden brown and set. A knife inserted into the center should come out mostly clean.
Let cool slightly before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Smoked Salmon Benedict with Verjus Cream Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Smoked Salmon Benedict is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate. A golden-brown toasted bagel half forms the base, providing a rustic texture. Over this, thin, delicate sheets of vibrant pink smoked salmon are artfully folded, creating soft waves. A perfectly poached egg, with its creamy white exterior and potential for a rich, flowing yellow yolk, sits atop the salmon. A glossy, pale yellow Verjus Cream Sauce is elegantly drizzled over the egg and salmon, catching the light. Fresh green sprigs of dill and finely chopped chives are scattered for a pop of color and freshness. The arrangement is balanced, with moderate negative space. The setting features a simple wooden table, a silver fork and knife rest beside the plate, and a folded cotton napkin, all under natural, even lighting for a modern bistro feel.
instructions: Prepare Verjus Cream Sauce: Melt 100 g butter in a small saucepan over low heat. Keep warm. In a separate bowl, whisk 2 egg yolks. In a heatproof bowl set over a saucepan of simmering water (bain-marie), combine cream cheese and verjus. Whisk until smooth and warm.

Remove bowl from heat. Gradually whisk in the egg yolks until fully incorporated and sauce thickens slightly. Slowly drizzle in the warm melted butter, whisking constantly until the sauce is emulsified and smooth. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm, stirring occasionally.

Poach Eggs: Fill a large saucepan with water to a depth of 10 cm. Add 30 ml white vinegar and a pinch of salt. Bring to a gentle simmer. Crack remaining 4 eggs individually into small bowls or ramekins.
Carefully slide each egg into the simmering water. Cook for 3-4 minutes until whites are set and yolks are still runny. Remove eggs with a slotted spoon. Drain excess water on paper towels.
Toast Bagels: Slice bagels in half horizontally. Toast until golden brown and slightly crispy.
Assemble: Place a toasted bagel half on each plate. Arrange 50 g of smoked salmon in elegant folds over each bagel.
Carefully place one poached egg on top of the smoked salmon.
Spoon a generous amount of the warm Verjus Cream Sauce over the egg and salmon.
Garnish with fresh dill sprigs and finely chopped chives. Serve immediately.
notes: For best results, use fresh, high-quality smoked salmon.
Ensure the water for poaching eggs is simmering gently, not boiling rapidly, to keep the eggs intact.

Remove bowl from heat. Gradually whisk in the egg yolks until fully incorporated and sauce thickens slightly. Slowly drizzle in the warm melted butter, whisking constantly until the sauce is emulsified and smooth. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm, stirring occasionally.

Poach Eggs: Fill a large saucepan with water to a depth of 10 cm. Add 30 ml white vinegar and a pinch of salt. Bring to a gentle simmer. Crack remaining 4 eggs individually into small bowls or ramekins.
Carefully slide each egg into the simmering water. Cook for 3-4 minutes until whites are set and yolks are still runny. Remove eggs with a slotted spoon. Drain excess water on paper towels.
Toast Bagels: Slice bagels in half horizontally. Toast until golden brown and slightly crispy.
Assemble: Place a toasted bagel half on each plate. Arrange 50 g of smoked salmon in elegant folds over each bagel.
Carefully place one poached egg on top of the smoked salmon.
Spoon a generous amount of the warm Verjus Cream Sauce over the egg and salmon.
Garnish with fresh dill sprigs and finely chopped chives. Serve immediately.
notes: For best results, use fresh, high-quality smoked salmon.
Ensure the water for poaching eggs is simmering gently, not boiling rapidly, to keep the eggs intact.

recipes.recipe_name: Smoked Salmon Benedict with Verjus Cream Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Smoked Salmon Benedict is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate. A golden-brown toasted bagel half forms the base, providing a rustic texture. Over this, thin, delicate sheets of vibrant pink smoked salmon are artfully folded, creating soft waves. A perfectly poached egg, with its creamy white exterior and potential for a rich, flowing yellow yolk, sits atop the salmon. A glossy, pale yellow Verjus Cream Sauce is elegantly drizzled over the egg and salmon, catching the light. Fresh green sprigs of dill and finely chopped chives are scattered for a pop of color and freshness. The arrangement is balanced, with moderate negative space. The setting features a simple wooden table, a silver fork and knife rest beside the plate, and a folded cotton napkin, all under natural, even lighting for a modern bistro feel.
instructions: Prepare Verjus Cream Sauce: Melt 100 g butter in a small saucepan over low heat. Keep warm. In a separate bowl, whisk 2 egg yolks. In a heatproof bowl set over a saucepan of simmering water (bain-marie), combine cream cheese and verjus. Whisk until smooth and warm.

Remove bowl from heat. Gradually whisk in the egg yolks until fully incorporated and sauce thickens slightly. Slowly drizzle in the warm melted butter, whisking constantly until the sauce is emulsified and smooth. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm, stirring occasionally.

Poach Eggs: Fill a large saucepan with water to a depth of 10 cm. Add 30 ml white vinegar and a pinch of salt. Bring to a gentle simmer. Crack remaining 4 eggs individually into small bowls or ramekins.
Carefully slide each egg into the simmering water. Cook for 3-4 minutes until whites are set and yolks are still runny. Remove eggs with a slotted spoon. Drain excess water on paper towels.
Toast Bagels: Slice bagels in half horizontally. Toast until golden brown and slightly crispy.
Assemble: Place a toasted bagel half on each plate. Arrange 50 g of smoked salmon in elegant folds over each bagel.
Carefully place one poached egg on top of the smoked salmon.
Spoon a generous amount of the warm Verjus Cream Sauce over the egg and salmon.
Garnish with fresh dill sprigs and finely chopped chives. Serve immediately.
notes: For best results, use fresh, high-quality smoked salmon.
Ensure the water for poaching eggs is simmering gently, not boiling rapidly, to keep the eggs intact.

recipes.recipe_name: Five-Spice Braised Chicken with Caramelized Fennel and Parmesan Crisp
recipes.visual_description: The dish presents a single, whole braised chicken thigh, skin-on, deeply caramelized and glistening with a rich, dark brown five-spice glaze, centered on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The chicken is tender and succulent. Alongside, several thick-cut caramelized fennel wedges, golden-brown with softened edges, are arranged neatly, providing lighter color and distinct texture. A delicate, golden-brown Parmesan crisp, irregular and airy, leans against the chicken, adding a crisp textural contrast. The plate is lightly drizzled with glossy, reduced braising sauce, pooling subtly. Vibrant green, finely chopped fresh coriander provides a fresh counterpoint. The setting is a modern bistro: a simple wooden table, a white cotton napkin, natural lighting. The entire plate is visible, with moderate negative space. Traditional chopsticks rest beside the plate, acknowledging the Modern Asian influence.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.

Heat 15ml oil in a large oven-safe pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs, skin-side down, until golden brown and crispy, about 8 minutes. Flip and sear other side for 3 minutes. Remove chicken from pan.
Reduce heat to medium. Add grated ginger and minced garlic to the pan. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add soy sauce and rice wine vinegar to the pan. Scrape up any browned bits.
Pour in chicken stock. Add star anise, cinnamon stick, cloves, Sichuan peppercorns, and fennel seeds. Bring to a simmer.
Return chicken thighs to the pan, skin-side up. Ensure liquid comes halfway up the chicken. Cover pan and transfer to a preheated oven at 180°C. Braise for 30 minutes.
Remove from oven. Check internal temperature of chicken; it should be 75°C. If not, return to oven for 5-10 more minutes.

While chicken braises, slice fennel bulbs into 1 cm thick wedges. Heat remaining 15ml oil in a separate pan over medium heat. Add fennel wedges. Cook, turning occasionally, until tender and caramelized, about 10-12 minutes. Season with salt and pepper.

Heat a non-stick pan over medium-low heat. Sprinkle small mounds of grated Parmesan (approx. 20g each) into the pan, forming circles. Cook until golden and crispy, about 2-3 minutes. Carefully remove with a spatula and let cool on a wire rack. Make 4 crisps.
Remove chicken from braising liquid. Strain braising liquid into a small saucepan. Skim off excess fat. Reduce sauce over medium-high heat until slightly thickened, about 5-7 minutes.
Plate: Place a braised chicken thigh on each plate. Arrange caramelized fennel wedges alongside. Drizzle with reduced braising sauce. Garnish with chopped fresh coriander and a Parmesan crisp.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Classic Yangzhou Fried Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of Classic Yangzhou Fried Rice is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The rice is mounded slightly in the center, showcasing individual golden grains. Visible throughout are small, evenly diced pieces of vibrant red char siu, bright green peas, orange carrots, and fluffy yellow scrambled egg. The dish has a slightly glossy sheen from the stir-frying. A sprinkle of freshly chopped green scallions provides a final burst of color and freshness on top. The plate rests on a simple wooden table surface. A pair of elegant wooden chopsticks are placed neatly beside the plate. Natural, soft, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and colors without harsh shadows. The background is minimal, suggesting a modern bistro setting with a casual atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a small side dish of chili oil or soy sauce for additional seasoning.
Traditionally accompanied by a light soup, such as a clear broth.
instructions: Prepare all ingredients: Dice char siu, onion, and carrots. Mince garlic. Chop scallions.
Whisk egg with a pinch of salt. Heat 5 mL vegetable oil in a wok or large frying pan over medium-high heat.
Pour in whisked egg. Scramble until just set. Remove egg from wok and set aside.
Add remaining 10 mL vegetable oil to the wok. Heat until shimmering.
Add diced onion, minced garlic, and diced carrots. Stir-fry for 2 minutes until fragrant and slightly softened.
Add diced char siu and frozen peas. Stir-fry for 1 minute.
Add cooked day-old jasmine rice to the wok. Break up any clumps with the back of your spatula. Stir-fry for 3-4 minutes, ensuring rice is heated through and slightly toasted.
Pour in soy sauce and sesame oil. Sprinkle with white pepper and sugar. Toss vigorously to coat all ingredients evenly. Continue to stir-fry for 1-2 minutes.
Return scrambled egg to the wok. Gently toss to combine.
Taste and adjust seasoning if needed. Remove from heat.
Serve immediately, garnished with fresh chopped scallions.
traditional_techniques: Wok Hei (achieving a 'breath of the wok' smoky aroma through high-heat stir-frying)

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Broccoli Stir-fry Noodles
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, showcasing a vibrant medley of colors and textures. Tender, golden-brown chicken slices are interspersed among bright green, tender-crisp broccoli florets. The cooked egg noodles are glistening with a rich, savory stir-fry sauce, which provides a glossy coating. Thinly sliced, slightly caramelized onions are visible throughout, adding subtle sweetness and depth. The overall arrangement is organic and flowing, with noodles forming the base, topped with chicken and broccoli, and a sprinkle of fresh, thinly sliced spring onions for a contrasting green garnish. Moderate negative space surrounds the central mound of food. The setting is a modern bistro with a simple wooden table, a single set of chopsticks resting beside the plate, and a crisp white cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's appealing textures and colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of chili garlic sauce for added heat.
Offer small bowls of soy sauce or vinegar for dipping.
Traditionally eaten with chopsticks.
instructions: Cut chicken breast into 2 cm thick slices. Toss with 5g cornstarch, 15ml soy sauce, and 5ml sesame oil. Set aside.
Cut broccoli into florets. Thinly slice onion. Mince garlic and ginger.
Boil noodles according to package directions until al dente. Drain and rinse with cold water. Toss with a little vegetable oil to prevent sticking.
Heat 15ml vegetable oil in a large wok or pan over high heat. Add chicken. Stir-fry until browned and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes. Remove chicken and set aside.
Add remaining 15ml vegetable oil to the wok. Add minced garlic, ginger, and sliced onion. Stir-fry for 2 minutes until fragrant. Add broccoli florets. Stir-fry for 3-4 minutes until tender-crisp.
In a small bowl, whisk together remaining 45ml soy sauce, oyster sauce, chicken stock, remaining 10g cornstarch, sugar, and white pepper.
Add cooked noodles and chicken back to the wok with the vegetables. Pour in the sauce. Toss everything together for 2-3 minutes until sauce thickens and coats all ingredients.
Garnish with thinly sliced spring onions. Serve immediately.
notes: Adjust spice level by adding dried chili flakes during stir-frying.
Ensure the wok is very hot for proper stir-frying technique.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Fajitas with Mixed Bell Peppers
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of vibrant Chicken Fajitas is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The plate holds a generous mound of sizzling chicken batons, seared to a golden-brown, interspersed with colorful strips of red, green, and yellow bell peppers and translucent, tender onion slices. The vegetables retain a slight crispness and show subtle charring. A scattering of freshly chopped green cilantro garnishes the top, adding a fresh contrast. Beside the main dish, a stack of two warm, pliable corn tortillas is neatly arranged. Small, culturally authentic ceramic bowls containing bright red salsa and creamy white sour cream are placed adjacent to the plate. A fresh lime wedge sits on the plate, ready to be squeezed. The setting is a modern bistro: a simple wooden table surface, a neutral cotton napkin, and even natural lighting create an inviting, authentic atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn or flour tortillas for self-assembly.
Offer traditional accompaniments like salsa, guacamole, and sour cream (or Mexican crema).
Provide fresh lime wedges for squeezing over the fajitas.
instructions: Slice chicken breasts into 1 cm thick batons. Place in a bowl.
Mince garlic. Add minced garlic, chili powder, cumin, paprika, oregano, salt, pepper, and juice of one lime to the chicken. Mix well to coat. Marinate for at least 15 minutes.
Slice all bell peppers into 1 cm thick strips. Slice onion into thick half-moon pieces.
Heat 30 ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering.
Add bell peppers and onion to the skillet. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until tender-crisp and slightly charred. Remove vegetables from skillet and set aside.
Add remaining 30 ml olive oil to the same skillet. Increase heat if needed.
Add marinated chicken to the skillet in a single layer. Cook for 6-8 minutes, stirring occasionally, until chicken is cooked through and lightly browned (internal temperature 75°C).
Return cooked vegetables to the skillet with the chicken. Toss to combine and heat through for 1-2 minutes.
Warm tortillas according to package instructions. Slice remaining lime into wedges.
Chop fresh cilantro for garnish.
Serve fajita mixture hot with warm tortillas, lime wedges, salsa, and sour cream.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Ricotta Pasta with Crispy Pancetta
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented in a clean, white porcelain bowl, showcasing a generous individual portion of pasta. The pasta, such as rigatoni, is al dente, thoroughly coated in a smooth, creamy, off-white ricotta sauce. Scattered throughout and atop the pasta are golden-brown, irregular chunks of crispy pancetta, providing a textural contrast. Freshly chopped green oregano leaves are sprinkled generously, adding vibrant color and herbaceous aroma. A light dusting of finely grated Parmigiano Reggiano cheese adds a subtle finish. The overall composition is natural and inviting, with moderate negative space. It sits on a simple wooden table, accompanied by traditional Italian flatware and a white cotton napkin.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread to sop up the sauce
Pair with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and vinegar
instructions: Boil 4 litres of salted water in a large pot. Add 400g pasta. Cook according to package directions until al dente.

While pasta cooks, heat 15ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add 200g diced pancetta. Cook until crispy and golden. Remove pancetta with a slotted spoon. Set aside. Leave rendered fat in skillet.
Add 2 minced garlic cloves to the skillet with rendered fat. Sauté for 30 seconds until fragrant. Do not brown.
In a bowl, combine 250g ricotta, 50g grated Parmigiano Reggiano, and 5g freshly ground black pepper. Mix well.

Drain pasta, reserving 250ml pasta cooking water. Add drained pasta to the skillet with garlic. Pour in the ricotta mixture. Add 150ml reserved pasta water. Stir continuously over low heat until sauce is creamy and coats pasta. Add more pasta water if needed for desired consistency.
Stir in most of the crispy pancetta and 10g chopped fresh oregano. Taste and adjust salt if necessary.
Serve immediately. Garnish each portion with remaining crispy pancetta and 5g chopped fresh oregano.

recipes.recipe_name: Tofu and Vegetable Donburi
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Tofu and Vegetable Donburi is presented in a traditional glazed ceramic donburi bowl. Fluffy white Japanese short-grain rice forms the base. Neatly arranged on top are golden-brown pan-fried tofu rectangles, vibrant green tender-crisp broccoli florets, earthy sliced shiitake mushrooms, julienned bright orange carrots, and translucent slivers of sautéed onion. A glistening savory amber sauce lightly coats the ingredients. The dish is garnished with finely sliced green onions and a sprinkle of toasted sesame seeds, adding fresh color and texture. The bowl sits on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a pair of elegant wooden chopsticks resting beside it on a ceramic chopstick rest, and a crisp white cotton napkin. Natural, soft light illuminates the dish, highlighting the varied textures and rich colors, creating an inviting and authentic Japanese dining experience.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Served with a side of miso soup
Accompanied by a small dish of pickled ginger (gari)
instructions: Rinse rice. Cook rice according to package directions. Keep warm.
Press tofu to remove excess water. Cut tofu into 2 cm x 3 cm rectangles.
Slice mushrooms. Thinly slice onion. Cut broccoli into small florets. Julienne carrot.
Heat 15 ml vegetable oil in a large non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Pan-fry tofu until golden brown and crispy on all sides. Remove tofu from pan. Set aside.
Add remaining 15 ml oil to the pan. Sauté onion until softened, about 3 minutes. Add mushrooms and carrot. Cook for 5 minutes until tender-crisp. Add broccoli florets. Cook for 3 minutes more.
In a small bowl, combine soy sauce, mirin, sake, sugar, and dashi stock.

Pour sauce mixture into the pan with vegetables. Bring to a simmer. Return cooked tofu to the pan. Cook for 2-3 minutes, allowing tofu to absorb sauce. Ensure tofu internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).
Divide cooked rice among 4 donburi bowls. Arrange tofu and vegetable mixture over the rice.
Garnish with thinly sliced green onions and toasted sesame seeds. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Cultured Cocoa Apple Dessert Bowls
recipes.visual_description: A single portion is presented in a handcrafted, unglazed ceramic bowl with an organic, slightly irregular rim, in an earthy cream or beige tone. The base features a generous scoop of rich, deep brown cocoa cottage cheese, its creamy texture visible. On top, a vibrant mound of golden-yellow fermented apple cubes, each precisely 1 cm, is artfully arranged. Their slightly translucent, firm appearance provides a textural contrast. A delicate dusting of cocoa powder lightly coats the apple cubes. The bowl rests on a light-colored reclaimed wood table. A folded, undyed linen napkin in natural beige is placed beside it. Soft, natural daylight illuminates the scene, highlighting the dish's natural colors and textures against a clean, minimalist background.
instructions: Wash apples thoroughly. Cut apples into 1 cm cubes, discarding cores.
Prepare a 2% brine solution: Dissolve 10 g sea salt in 500 ml water.
Place apple cubes into a clean glass jar. Pour brine over apples, ensuring all cubes are submerged. Use a fermentation weight if necessary.
Cover the jar loosely with a lid or cloth. Let ferment at room temperature (20-24°C) for 3-5 days. Taste daily for desired tanginess.
Once fermented, refrigerate the apples.
In a mixing bowl, combine cottage cheese, cocoa powder, and maple syrup. Mix until smooth and well incorporated.
Taste the cocoa cottage cheese. Adjust sweetness with more maple syrup if desired.
To serve, divide the cocoa cottage cheese among 4 individual serving bowls.
Drain the fermented apple cubes. Spoon a generous portion of fermented apples over the cocoa cottage cheese in each bowl.
notes: Fermentation time for apples can vary based on room temperature and desired sourness. Start tasting on day 3.
Ensure apples remain submerged in brine during fermentation to prevent mold.

recipes.recipe_name: Potato Gnocchi with Fava Beans and Brown Butter Sage Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of golden-brown potato gnocchi is artfully arranged on a clean, round white porcelain plate. The gnocchi, irregular in shape from hand-rolling, exhibit a slightly crisp exterior from being pan-tossed in brown butter, revealing a soft, pillowy interior. Bright green blanched fava beans are scattered among the gnocchi, adding vibrant color and a fresh texture contrast. A glistening brown butter and sage sauce coats the gnocchi, with crispy sage leaves visible throughout, imparting an aromatic herbaceousness. A light dusting of finely grated Pecorino Romano cheese adds a subtle white counterpoint. The plate is presented on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a folded linen napkin and a fork, embodying a modern bistro aesthetic with Italian charm. The lighting is natural and even, highlighting the dish's warm tones and inviting textures.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately with a generous grating of Pecorino Romano or Parmigiano Reggiano cheese.
A glass of crisp Italian white wine, such as Pinot Grigio or Vermentino, complements the dish.
Offer fresh, crusty Italian bread on the side for dipping into the remaining sauce.

ingredients.name: Pecorino Romano or Parmigiano Reggiano, grated

instructions: Boil potatoes in their skins until very tender. Drain and cool slightly. Peel potatoes while still warm.
Pass warm potatoes through a potato ricer or mash thoroughly until smooth. Spread mashed potato on a clean surface to cool completely.
Form a well in the center of the cooled potato. Add flour, egg, a pinch of salt, and pepper to the well.
Gently mix ingredients with hands until a soft, cohesive dough forms. Do not overmix.
Divide dough into four portions. Roll each portion into a long rope, approximately 2 cm thick. Cut ropes into 2 cm pieces.
Gently roll each gnocchi piece over the back of a fork or a gnocchi board to create ridges. Place formed gnocchi on a floured tray.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil. Add fava beans and blanch for 2 minutes. Drain and immediately plunge into ice water. Peel the outer skin from each fava bean; set aside.
In a large pan, melt butter over medium heat. Cook until butter turns golden brown and smells nutty. Add sage leaves and minced garlic. Cook until sage is crispy and garlic is fragrant.
Boil gnocchi in batches in the same pot of salted water until they float to the surface, about 2-3 minutes. Remove with a slotted spoon.
Transfer cooked gnocchi directly to the pan with brown butter sauce. Add blanched fava beans. Toss gently to coat.
Season with additional salt and pepper if needed. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Turkey Roulade with Lemon-Herb Orzo
recipes.visual_description: The dish presents sliced turkey roulade, golden-brown and seared, with a visible vibrant green spinach and white feta filling. Three thick medallions of turkey are arranged against a central mound of bright yellow lemon-herb orzo, which has flecks of green parsley. Halved and slightly burst roasted cherry tomatoes are scattered around the plate, adding pops of red. A light drizzle of pan sauce from the turkey glistens on the plate. Textures are varied: tender turkey, creamy filling, al dente orzo, and soft tomatoes. A sprig of fresh oregano garnishes the turkey. Plated on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, set on a simple wooden table with a folded cotton napkin and standard flatware, under natural, even lighting. The background features a subtle, casual bistro ambiance.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and lemon.
Offer crusty bread for dipping in any remaining pan juices.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Butterfly turkey breasts. Pound each to 1 cm thickness. Season with salt and pepper.
Sauté spinach in 5 ml olive oil until wilted. Squeeze out excess water.
Crumble feta cheese. Mince 1 clove garlic. Chop fresh oregano and thyme.
Combine spinach, feta, minced garlic, and herbs in a bowl.
Spread filling evenly over turkey cutlets. Roll tightly. Secure with toothpicks or butcher's twine.
Heat 15 ml olive oil in an oven-safe pan over medium-high heat. Sear turkey roulades 3 minutes per side until golden.
Transfer pan to preheated oven. Roast 20-25 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Meanwhile, cook orzo according to package directions. Drain well.
Halve cherry tomatoes. Toss with 5 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Roast in oven alongside turkey for the last 15 minutes.
Zest and juice half a lemon. Mince remaining garlic clove. Chop fresh parsley.
Toss cooked orzo with remaining 5 ml olive oil, lemon zest, lemon juice, minced garlic, and chopped parsley. Season with salt and pepper.
Remove turkey from oven. Let rest 5 minutes. Remove twine or toothpicks. Slice each roulade into 3-4 thick medallions.

recipes.recipe_name: Tempeh, Kale, and Potato Curry
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Tempeh, Kale, and Potato Curry is presented in a rustic, deep ceramic bowl with natural imperfections. The curry features rich, reddish-brown sauce enveloping tender, diced potatoes, vibrant green wilted kale, and golden-brown seared tempeh cubes. The ingredients are naturally arranged, slightly overlapping. A small pile of fluffy basmati rice sits to the side of the curry within the same bowl, demonstrating a homely plating style. Fresh, roughly chopped coriander leaves are sprinkled over the curry as a functional garnish, adding a pop of green. The bowl rests on a well-used wooden dining table. A simple, folded cloth napkin and a traditional metal spoon are casually placed alongside. Warm, cozy lighting illuminates the scene, creating a comforting, lived-in family kitchen atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve hot with freshly cooked basmati rice.
Accompany with warm naan bread or roti for scooping the curry.
Offer a side of simple cucumber raita (vegan version with plant-based yogurt) or a fresh kachumber salad.
instructions: Cut tempeh into 2 cm cubes. Dice potatoes into 2 cm cubes. Roughly chop kale.
Finely dice onion. Mince garlic. Grate ginger.
Heat vegetable oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add tempeh cubes. Sear until golden brown on all sides. Remove tempeh from pot. Set aside.
Add onion to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and grated ginger. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in cumin powder, coriander powder, turmeric powder, and chili powder. Cook for 30 seconds, stirring constantly.
Add diced potatoes and canned tomatoes. Stir well to combine.
Pour in water or vegetable broth. Bring to a simmer. Cover and cook for 10-15 minutes, until potatoes are nearly tender.
Add kale and coconut milk. Stir until kale begins to wilt. Return seared tempeh to the pot.
Simmer uncovered for 5-7 minutes, until kale is tender and sauce has thickened slightly.
Stir in garam masala. Season with salt to taste.
Garnish with fresh coriander before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Gochujang Dak Bokkeum with Kimchi Fried Rice and Egg Ribbons
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Gochujang Dak Bokkeum with Kimchi Fried Rice is presented on a clean white porcelain plate. The vibrant red-orange gochujang-glazed chicken chunks, approximately 3cm, are arranged neatly beside a mound of glossy, reddish-orange kimchi fried rice. The rice is studded with darker kimchi pieces and bright green onion bits, offering a textural contrast. Thin, golden-yellow egg ribbons are artfully draped over a portion of the rice and chicken. Fresh green onion slices garnish the dish, adding a pop of color. A warm, golden-brown scallion flatbread, approximately 15cm, rests beside the plate. The setting is a modern bistro with a simple wooden table, natural even lighting. Traditional Korean metal chopsticks are placed to the right.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with small side dishes (banchan) like pickled radish or cucumber.
Eat with metal chopsticks and a spoon for the rice.
Rip the flatbread to scoop up chicken and rice.
instructions: In a bowl, combine gochujang, gochugaru, soy sauce, mirin, 1 tbsp sesame oil, minced garlic, grated ginger, and brown sugar. Add chicken chunks (cut into 3cm pieces). Mix well. Marinate for at least 30 minutes, or up to 4 hours in the refrigerator.

Whisk eggs with a pinch of salt. Heat a lightly oiled non-stick pan over medium-low heat. Pour a thin layer of egg mixture to make thin omelets. Cook until set. Flip once. Remove. Stack omelets. Roll tightly. Slice into thin ribbons. Set aside.

For scallion flatbread: In a bowl, combine flour and 1/2 tsp salt. Gradually add warm water. Mix until a dough forms. Knead on a floured surface for 5 minutes until smooth. Divide dough into 4 equal pieces. Roll each piece into a thin circle. Brush with 1 tbsp sesame oil. Sprinkle with sliced green parts of green onions. Roll up each circle into a log. Coil the log into a spiral. Flatten the spiral slightly. Roll out again into a flatbread about 15cm in diameter.
Heat a lightly oiled pan over medium heat. Cook flatbreads for 2-3 minutes per side, until golden brown and cooked through. Keep warm.

Heat 1 tbsp cooking oil in a large wok or skillet over medium-high heat. Add marinated chicken. Stir-fry for 8-10 minutes. Cook until chicken reaches 75°C (167°F) internal temperature. Remove chicken from wok. Set aside.

Add remaining 1 tbsp cooking oil to the same wok. Add white parts of green onions. Stir-fry for 1 minute. Add chopped kimchi. Stir-fry for 3 minutes. Add cooked rice. Break up any clumps. Stir-fry for 5-7 minutes, until rice is heated through and slightly crisp.

Divide kimchi fried rice among 4 plates. Arrange cooked gochujang chicken next to the rice. Garnish with egg ribbons and remaining green parts of green onions. Serve immediately with warm scallion flatbread on the side.
traditional_techniques: Making thin egg omelets (jidan) for garnishing

recipes.recipe_name: Goat Cheese Stuffed Chicken Breast with Beet Risotto and Pomelo Gremolata
recipes.visual_description: A refined individual portion is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, set against a simple wooden table surface in a modern bistro style. The centerpiece is a golden-brown, oven-roasted chicken breast, sliced diagonally in half, revealing a creamy, melted goat cheese filling. Beside the chicken rests a vibrant, smooth quenelle of deep purple beet risotto, its al dente grains visible, offering a striking color contrast. A generous sprinkle of bright green, finely chopped parsley and pale yellow diced pomelo gremolata adorns both the chicken and the risotto, adding fresh texture and zesty highlights. The plating is balanced, with moderate negative space, showcasing the distinct elements without overcrowding. Standard silver flatware rests beside the plate, complementing the modern bistro aesthetic. The scene is bathed in natural, even lighting, emphasizing the dish's appealing colors and textures.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C. Wrap beets in foil. Roast for 45-60 minutes until tender. Peel and roughly chop beets. Puree beets with 50 ml of broth until smooth. Set aside.
Butterfly each chicken breast. Season inside with salt and pepper. Spread 25 g of goat cheese inside each. Fold chicken breasts to enclose cheese. Secure with toothpicks if needed.

Heat 15 ml olive oil in an oven-safe pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken breasts for 3 minutes per side until golden brown. Transfer pan to oven. Roast for 15-20 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken, let rest 5 minutes.

While chicken roasts, prepare risotto. Heat remaining 15 ml olive oil and 10 g butter in a separate pot over medium heat. Sauté shallots until softened, about 3 minutes. Add garlic. Cook for 1 minute.
Add Arborio rice. Stir for 2 minutes until translucent. Pour in white wine. Cook until absorbed.

Add beet puree to rice. Stir well. Begin adding hot broth, one ladle at a time. Stir continuously. Wait for each addition to be absorbed before adding more. Continue for 18-20 minutes until rice is creamy and al dente.
Stir in remaining 20 g butter and Parmesan cheese. Season risotto with salt and pepper. Keep warm.
For gremolata, segment pomelo. Remove all pith and membrane. Dice pomelo segments finely. Combine diced pomelo, chopped parsley, and lemon zest in a small bowl.
Slice each chicken breast in half diagonally. Remove toothpicks. Serve a portion of beet risotto. Place chicken breast halves beside risotto. Garnish generously with pomelo gremolata.

recipes.recipe_name: Individual Coffee Soufflé
recipes.visual_description: A single, perfectly risen coffee soufflé in a classic white ceramic ramekin sits centrally on a simple round white ceramic plate. The soufflé has a golden-brown, slightly cracked crust, indicating its airy texture, and has risen significantly above the rim of the ramekin. A light dusting of powdered sugar subtly highlights its contours. A small, creamy pool of warm vanilla sauce is gently poured beside the ramekin on the plate. The colors are warm: the rich brown of the soufflé top, creamy white interior (peeking slightly), and the pale beige of the vanilla sauce. The scene is set on a well-used wooden dining table in a homely kitchen, illuminated by warm, inviting light. A simple silver dessert spoon rests beside the plate, ready for enjoyment. The overall presentation is natural and unpretentious, reflecting home-style French dessert plating.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately from the oven to appreciate its full height and airy texture.
Traditionally enjoyed as a light, elegant dessert.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Butter a 150ml soufflé ramekin. Dust inside with 10g granulated sugar. Set aside.
In a small saucepan, melt 10g butter over medium heat.
Stir in cake flour. Cook, stirring, for 1 minute to form a roux.
Gradually whisk in 50ml milk until smooth. Cook until mixture thickens.
Remove from heat. Stir in 15g granulated sugar, brewed coffee, 2ml vanilla extract, and egg yolk. Mix until smooth.
In a clean, dry bowl, whisk egg whites with a pinch of salt until soft peaks form.
Gradually add remaining 20g granulated sugar. Continue whisking until stiff, glossy peaks form.
Fold one-third of the whisked egg whites into the coffee base mixture to lighten it.
Gently fold in the remaining egg whites until just combined. Do not overmix.
Spoon the soufflé mixture into the prepared ramekin. Level the top gently.
Bake for 12-15 minutes, or until soufflé is well-risen and golden brown on top.

While soufflé bakes, prepare vanilla sauce: Heat remaining 50ml milk, 2ml vanilla extract, and 5g granulated sugar in a small saucepan over low heat. Stir until sugar dissolves and milk is warm. Do not boil.
Serve soufflé immediately, with warm vanilla sauce poured alongside or gently drizzled over.
traditional_techniques: Making a roux for the soufflé base
Whipping egg whites to stiff peaks

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Stuffed Potato with Cheesy Mushroom, Tomato, and Rice
recipes.visual_description: The baked potato is split lengthwise, presenting a generous, mounded filling. The top is a golden-brown, bubbly crust of melted cheddar cheese. Beneath, the hearty stuffing reveals a mix of creamy mashed potato, soft rice grains, thinly sliced browned mushrooms, small red tomato cubes, and small bread cubes, all integrated into a rich texture. The rustic potato skin provides a natural vessel, slightly crisped from baking. It is served on a simple, everyday ceramic plate with natural imperfections. A fork and knife are placed casually beside the plate. The setting is a well-used wooden dining table in a cozy kitchen, illuminated by warm, inviting light. A casually placed cloth napkin and perhaps a small, unassuming glass of water complete the homely scene. The portion is substantial for one person.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Served hot directly from the oven.
Often accompanied by a simple side salad.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Pierce potato several times with a fork. Bake for 50-60 minutes until very tender.
While potato bakes, prepare filling. Dice onion finely. Mince garlic. Slice mushrooms thinly. Dice tomato into small cubes. Cut stale bread into 1cm cubes.
Heat olive oil in a pan over medium heat. Add diced onion. Sauté until softened, about 3 minutes.
Add minced garlic and sliced mushrooms. Cook until mushrooms release their liquid and brown, about 5-7 minutes.
Stir in diced tomato. Cook for 2 minutes until slightly softened. Remove from heat.
Once potato is baked, carefully cut it in half lengthwise. Scoop out most of the flesh into a bowl, leaving a 1cm border in the skin.
Add butter, milk, salt, and pepper to the scooped potato flesh. Mash until smooth.
Grate half of the cheddar cheese (25g). Add grated cheese, cooked rice, bread cubes, and the mushroom-tomato mixture to the mashed potato. Mix well.
Spoon the potato filling back into the potato skins, mounding it slightly.
Grate remaining cheddar cheese (25g) over the top of the stuffed potatoes.
Return stuffed potatoes to the oven. Bake for 15-20 minutes, or until cheese is melted and golden brown.
Garnish with fresh chopped chives or parsley before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Roasted Chicken with Bell Pepper & Tomato Relish
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of golden-brown roasted boneless chicken thigh, tender and succulent, sits prominently on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Alongside, a vibrant relish of finely diced red and yellow bell peppers, sautéed until tender-crisp, and halved cherry tomatoes, lightly cooked to burst with flavor, is artfully spooned. The relish offers a rich tapestry of red, yellow, and green hues from fresh parsley. A small, neat mound of fresh, crisp mixed salad greens, lightly dressed, provides a refreshing contrast in texture and color. The dish is garnished with a fresh sprig of flat-leaf parsley and a bright yellow lemon wedge. The setting is a modern bistro: a simple wooden table surface, with traditional silver flatware and a folded white cotton napkin placed beside the plate, all under natural, even lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm, crusty bread to sop up the relish juices.
Pair with a glass of light-bodied regional white wine.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt, pepper, and 3g dried oregano.

Heat 15ml olive oil in an oven-safe pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown. Transfer pan to oven. Roast for 15-20 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C.
While chicken roasts, dice red and yellow bell peppers. Halve cherry tomatoes. Mince garlic. Finely dice red onion.
For the relish, heat 30ml olive oil in a separate pan over medium heat. Sauté diced red onion for 3 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic and sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.

Add diced bell peppers to the pan. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until tender-crisp. Add halved cherry tomatoes, remaining 2g dried oregano, and 5ml red wine vinegar. Cook for 3-4 minutes until tomatoes slightly soften. Season relish with salt and pepper. Stir in half of the chopped fresh parsley.
For the salad dressing, whisk together remaining 15ml olive oil, 10ml red wine vinegar, juice from half a lemon, salt, and pepper in a small bowl.
Toss mixed salad greens with the prepared dressing just before serving.
Remove chicken from oven. Let rest for 5 minutes.

To plate, place one roasted chicken thigh on each plate. Spoon a generous portion of the bell pepper and tomato relish alongside. Arrange a small mound of dressed salad greens next to the relish. Garnish with a sprig of fresh parsley and a lemon wedge.

recipes.recipe_name: Arroz con Cerdo
recipes.visual_description: The dish features a vibrant, orange-hued rice known as Arroz con Cerdo, served on a clean white porcelain plate. Large, golden-brown seared pork chunks are distributed throughout the fluffy medium-grain rice. Visible pieces of translucent diced onions, minced garlic, green olives, and small capers add textural variety. The rice is garnished with fresh, bright green chopped cilantro. A side of thick-cut fried sweet plantains rests beside the rice. The setting is a modern bistro with a light wood table and a neutral cotton napkin. Lighting is natural and even, highlighting the moist texture of the meat and individual grains. The entire plate is visible, showing a balanced restaurant portion.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with fried sweet plantains (amarillos)
Accompany with thick slices of fresh avocado
Serve with a side of crispy tostones
instructions: Season pork chunks with salt, pepper, and oregano.
Heat olive oil in a heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat.
Brown pork chunks on all sides until golden. Remove pork from pot.
Sauté diced onion and minced garlic in the same pot until translucent.
Stir in tomato sauce, sazón, green olives, and capers.
Return pork to the pot. Add rice and stir to coat grains.
Pour in water. Bring the mixture to a boil.
Reduce heat to low. Cover the pot with a tight-fitting lid.
Simmer for 20 minutes until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed.
Fluff rice gently with a fork. Rest for 5 minutes before serving.
notes: Use a caldero for the most authentic rice texture.
Do not stir the rice while simmering to allow a crust (pegao) to form at the bottom.
Ensure pork reaches an internal temperature of 75°C.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Pork Medallions with Habanero-Mango Glaze and Lime Rice
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, set on a simple wooden table. A bed of fluffy white jasmine rice, infused with bright green flecks of lime zest, forms the base. Three to four golden-brown seared pork medallions, cooked to a tender finish, are arranged organically on the rice. The pork exhibits a beautiful caramelized crust. A vibrant, chunky habanero-mango glaze, showcasing hues of orange and subtle red from the chili, is generously drizzled over the pork. Fresh, bright green chopped cilantro is scattered over the glaze, adding a pop of color and freshness. The arrangement is balanced, with moderate negative space, allowing each component to stand out. A simple cotton napkin rests beside the plate. The lighting is natural and even, highlighting the dish's fresh ingredients and appealing textures.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of fried plantains (tostones or maduros).
instructions: Rinse jasmine rice. Combine rice with 150 ml stock, a pinch of salt, and the juice of 1/4 lime in a small saucepan. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until liquid is absorbed and rice is tender. Remove from heat, let stand covered for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork and stir in the zest of 1/2 lime.
Slice pork tenderloin into 2-3 cm thick medallions. Season generously with salt and black pepper.

Heat 10 ml olive oil in a small pan over medium-high heat. Sear pork medallions for 3-4 minutes per side, until golden brown and cooked to an internal temperature of 75°C. Remove pork from pan and set aside to rest.

In the same pan, add remaining 5 ml olive oil. Sauté minced garlic and minced habanero for 30 seconds until fragrant. Add diced mango and the juice of 1/4 lime. Simmer for 3-5 minutes, mashing mango gently with a spoon, until the sauce thickens slightly. Season with salt to taste. This is your habanero-mango glaze.

Plate the lime-infused rice as a base. Arrange the seared pork medallions on top of the rice. Spoon the habanero-mango glaze over the pork. Garnish generously with fresh chopped cilantro and the remaining lime zest.
notes: Adjust habanero chili quantity to personal spice preference.
For a smoother glaze, blend the sauce after simmering.

recipes.recipe_name: Smoked Tofu and Trumpet Mushroom Steaks with Green Chili-Pumpkin Seed Gremolata and Paprika Yogurt
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of the dish is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. A thick, golden-brown seared smoked tofu rectangle, approximately 2 cm thick, is the central focus. Alongside it are several deeply caramelized trumpet mushroom medallions, showcasing their earthy brown hues and appealing texture. A vibrant green gremolata, featuring finely chopped cilantro, visible pumpkin seeds, and a hint of red chili, is generously sprinkled over the tofu and mushrooms. A creamy, pale orange swirl of paprika yogurt sauce anchors the dish, providing a soft contrast. The plate is moderately spaced, allowing each element to stand out. The setting is a modern bistro, with a simple wooden table surface, a grey cotton napkin, and silver flatware placed beside the plate, all under natural, even lighting.

ingredients.name: Yogurt cheese (labneh or strained Greek yogurt)

instructions: Press tofu for 30 minutes to remove excess water. Slice into four equal thick rectangles, approximately 2 cm thick.
Slice trumpet mushrooms lengthwise into 1 cm thick medallions.
For the Paprika Yogurt: Combine yogurt cheese and smoked paprika in a small bowl. Season with a pinch of salt. Mix well. Refrigerate until serving.

For the Gremolata: Finely chop pumpkin seeds, Thai green chilies (deseed for less heat), and garlic. Roughly chop cilantro or parsley. Combine all in a bowl. Add lemon zest and 15 ml olive oil. Season with salt and pepper. Mix well.
Heat remaining 45 ml olive oil in a large non-stick pan over medium-high heat.
Sear tofu 'steaks' for 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown and crispy. Remove from pan and set aside.
Add mushroom medallions to the same pan. Sear for 3-4 minutes per side until deeply caramelized and tender. Season with salt and pepper.
To plate, spread a dollop of Paprika Yogurt on each plate. Place one seared tofu 'steak' and several mushroom medallions on top or beside the yogurt.
Spoon a generous amount of Green Chili-Pumpkin Seed Gremolata over the tofu and mushrooms.
Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken Breast with Brown Rice Risotto, Roasted Squash & Carrots, and Sweet Corn Nage
recipes.visual_description: A single pan-seared chicken breast, golden-skinned, anchors the plate as a whole piece. It rests atop a free-flowing mound of creamy brown rice risotto. Around the risotto, artfully arranged 2 cm cubes of roasted butternut squash and 1 cm thick rounds of caramelized carrots add vibrant orange and earthy tones. Sautéed cremini mushrooms, quartered and deeply browned, are nestled alongside. A rich, golden-yellow sweet corn nage is elegantly spooned around the central components, forming a delicate pool. The plate is garnished sparingly with fresh thyme leaves and finely chopped green chives, providing freshness and verdant color. Presentation is organic and flowing, emphasizing natural shapes and abundant negative space on an expensive bone china plate.

ingredients.name: Butternut Squash
ingredients.quantity: 300 g, peeled, seeded, cut into 2 cm cubes

ingredients.name: Carrots
ingredients.quantity: 2 medium, peeled, cut into 1 cm thick rounds

instructions: Prepare Vegetables: Peel and finely dice the onion. Mince garlic. Peel, seed, and cut butternut squash into 2 cm cubes. Peel carrots and slice into 1 cm thick rounds. Quarter mushrooms. Strip leaves from 4 thyme sprigs.

Roast Vegetables: Preheat oven to 200°C. Toss squash and carrots with 15 ml olive oil, stripped thyme leaves, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking tray. Roast for 20-25 minutes, until tender and slightly caramelized.

Start Brown Rice Risotto: Heat 15 ml olive oil and 10 g butter in a heavy-bottomed pot over medium heat. Add half of the diced onion. Sauté until translucent, about 5 minutes. Add brown rice. Toast for 2 minutes, stirring constantly. Deglaze with white wine. Cook until wine is absorbed.

Cook Risotto: Add hot chicken stock, 150 ml at a time, stirring frequently. Allow each addition to absorb before adding more. Continue for 35-45 minutes, until rice is creamy and tender but still has a slight bite. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.

Sear Chicken: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and pepper. Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Place chicken skin-side down. Sear for 6-8 minutes, until skin is golden and crispy. Flip chicken.
Finish Chicken: Transfer skillet to preheated oven (200°C) for 10-12 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Let rest 5 minutes before serving.

Sauté Mushrooms: While chicken rests, heat remaining 10 g butter in a separate pan over medium-high heat. Add quartered mushrooms. Sauté until golden brown and tender, about 5-7 minutes. Season with salt and pepper.

Prepare Corn Nage: In a small saucepan, combine fresh corn kernels, remaining half of diced onion, and 100 ml chicken stock. Simmer for 5 minutes. Stir in heavy cream and Worcestershire sauce. Simmer gently for another 2 minutes. Blend with an immersion blender until smooth. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve for a refined texture. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.

Plate: Spoon a generous portion of brown rice risotto onto the center of each plate. Arrange roasted squash and carrots artfully around the risotto. Place a seared chicken breast on top of the risotto. Spoon corn nage around the chicken. Garnish with sautéed mushrooms, a few fresh thyme leaves, and finely chopped chives.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
For a smoother corn nage, pass through a fine-mesh sieve after blending.

recipes.recipe_name: Rustic Sausage and Potato Hash with Fried Egg
recipes.visual_description: On a clean white porcelain plate, the dish presents a rustic yet refined composition. A mound of golden-brown potato hash forms the base, showcasing irregularly shaped, pan-fried potato cubes with slightly crisped edges. Interspersed are caramelized diced onions, bright orange diced carrots, and vibrant green peas, all harmoniously mixed with thick, browned slices of savory pork sausage. A perfectly fried egg, with a glistening, runny yolk and crisp white edges, crowns the hash. Beside the hash, a dollop of creamy, pale green cucumber-dill relish adds a refreshing counterpoint, flecked with green dill and tiny white cucumber pieces. The overall color palette is warm and inviting, with rich browns, golden yellows, and fresh greens. A sprinkle of bright green chopped parsley provides a final touch of freshness and color. The plate is moderately filled, allowing for some negative space.
instructions: Boil potatoes. Place diced 1.5 cm potato cubes in a pot. Cover with cold salted water. Bring to a boil. Cook until tender, 8-10 minutes. Drain well.

Cook sausage. Heat 15ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add sausages. Brown on all sides. Cook until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove sausages. Slice into thick rounds or chunks.
Sauté aromatics. Add remaining 15ml olive oil and butter to the skillet. Add finely diced onion and 1 cm diced carrot. Sauté until softened, 5-7 minutes.

Prepare hash base. Add cooked potatoes and sliced sausage to the skillet with onion and carrot. Toss gently. Cook for 5-8 minutes, stirring occasionally, until potatoes are slightly browned. Season with salt and pepper. Add green peas. Cook for 2 minutes.
Make relish. In a small bowl, combine finely diced cucumber, mayonnaise, chopped dill, and white wine vinegar. Season with a pinch of salt and pepper. Mix well.
Fry eggs. While hash finishes, fry 4 eggs to your preferred doneness.

Plate dish. Divide hash among four plates. Place one fried egg on top of each hash portion. Serve with a generous spoonful of creamy cucumber-dill relish on the side. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Sichuan Black Bean Pork Udon Stir-fry
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented in a deep, clean white porcelain bowl, showcasing a generous single serving. Chewy udon noodles, coated in a rich, dark savory sauce, form the base. Tender pork, cut into irregular 2cm chunks, is nestled among the noodles, exhibiting a glossy, caramelized exterior. Vibrant green gai lan florets and 5cm batons are interspersed, maintaining their crisp-tender texture and bright color. A scattering of golden-brown toasted cashews adds textural contrast. The dish is garnished with thinly sliced spring onions and a light dusting of freshly ground Szechuan peppercorns. The overall composition is balanced, with moderate negative space. Chopsticks rest on a ceramic holder beside the bowl. A small, simple white side dish with pickled mustard greens sits adjacent, enhancing the authentic Sichuan dining experience. The setting is a modern bistro with a simple wooden table and natural, even lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately with chopsticks.
Offer a side of chili oil or pickled mustard greens.
instructions: Cut pork into irregular 2 cm chunks. Marinate pork with 1 tablespoon light soy sauce, 1 tablespoon Shaoxing wine, and cornstarch. Mix well. Set aside for 15 minutes.
Cut gai lan into 5 cm batons, separating florets. Blanch gai lan in boiling water for 2 minutes. Drain and set aside.
Mince garlic. Grate ginger. Rinse and roughly chop preserved black beans. Thinly slice spring onions for garnish.
Toast Szechuan peppercorns in a dry pan over medium heat for 2 minutes. Grind into a coarse powder.
In a small bowl, combine dark soy sauce, remaining 1 tablespoon light soy sauce, remaining 1 tablespoon Shaoxing wine, chicken stock, and sugar. Mix to create the sauce.
Heat 1 tablespoon vegetable oil in a large wok or pan over high heat. Stir-fry pork until browned and cooked through. Remove pork from wok and set aside.

Add remaining 2 tablespoons vegetable oil to the wok. Add minced garlic, grated ginger, chopped preserved black beans, chili pepper flakes, and half of the ground Szechuan peppercorns. Stir-fry for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add blanched gai lan to the wok. Stir-fry for 1 minute.
Add the prepared sauce mixture to the wok. Bring to a simmer.
Add udon noodles to the wok. Toss to coat noodles in sauce.
Return cooked pork to the wok. Add cashews. Toss everything together to combine.
Drizzle with sesame oil. Serve immediately, garnished with sliced spring onions and the remaining ground Szechuan peppercorns.

recipes.recipe_name: Pollo Asado con Frijoles y Salsa Fresca
recipes.visual_description: A single individual portion of Pollo Asado con Frijoles y Salsa Fresca is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate, set on a simple wooden table surface. The seared chicken chunks, exhibiting a rich golden-brown char, are arranged neatly on one side of the plate. Adjacent is a compact mound of creamy black beans, their dark color providing contrast. Thin strips of vibrant red and yellow bell peppers, sautéed to tender-crisp, are placed next to the beans. A small, rustic ceramic bowl holds the fresh, chunky Salsa Fresca, bursting with diced red tomatoes, red onion, and green coriander. A generous drizzle of white lime crema artistically cascades over the chicken and beans. Bright green pickled jalapeño slices and fresh coriander leaves garnish the dish, adding pops of color. Two warm corn tortillas are folded and stacked neatly beside the main components, ready to be filled. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and colors. The background is a subtly blurred modern bistro setting, with a cotton napkin and traditional flatware completing the authentic Mexican dining experience.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas for building individual tacos.
Offer fresh lime wedges on the side for added zest.
Pair with a traditional Mexican rice side dish.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Cut into 2 cm thick chunks. In a bowl, combine 15 mL olive oil, 2 minced garlic cloves, 5 mL dark soy sauce, 15 mL honey, juice of 1/2 lime, 5 g cumin, 5 g smoked paprika, 2 g dried oregano, salt, and pepper. Add chicken chunks. Mix well. Marinate for at least 30 minutes, or up to 4 hours in the refrigerator.
Prepare Salsa Fresca: Dice tomatoes, 1/4 red onion, and 1/2 fresh jalapeño. Finely chop 1/4 bunch fresh coriander. Combine in a bowl with juice of 1/2 lime and a pinch of salt. Mix. Set aside.

Prepare Black Beans: Finely dice remaining 1/4 red onion. Mince 2 garlic cloves. Heat 15 mL olive oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Sauté onion until soft, about 3 minutes. Add garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant. Add rinsed black beans. Add 60 mL water. Season with salt and a pinch of cumin. Simmer gently for 5-7 minutes, mashing some beans with a fork for a creamier texture. Keep warm.
Prepare Lime Crema: In a small bowl, combine sour cream with juice of 1/2 lime and a pinch of salt. Stir until smooth. Set aside.

Cook Chicken: Heat a large skillet or grill pan over medium-high heat. Add marinated chicken chunks. Cook for 6-8 minutes, turning occasionally, until cooked through and lightly charred. Internal temperature must reach 75°C (167°F).

Sauté Bell Peppers: While chicken cooks, slice bell peppers into thin strips. Heat a separate pan with 5 mL olive oil. Sauté bell pepper strips over medium-high heat until tender-crisp, about 4-5 minutes. Season with salt and pepper.
Warm Tortillas: Heat corn tortillas in a dry skillet over medium heat for 30 seconds per side, or wrap in foil and warm in oven.

To serve: Arrange chicken chunks, black beans, sautéed bell peppers, and Salsa Fresca on individual plates. Garnish with pickled jalapeño slices and fresh coriander leaves. Drizzle with Lime Crema. Serve with warm corn tortillas and lime wedges.

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish Garlic Chicken with Crispy Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Spanish Garlic Chicken with Crispy Potatoes is presented on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate. Two golden-brown, whole chicken thighs, rich with a glossy, savory garlic sauce, are positioned towards the plate's center. Beside them, a generous portion of roasted potato cubes, uniformly cut to 2-3 cm, exhibit a crispy, golden-brown exterior and fluffy interior. The sauce lightly coats the chicken, revealing bits of thinly sliced garlic. A sprinkle of vibrant green fresh parsley garnishes the dish, with a bright yellow lemon wedge placed on the side. The overall composition is balanced with moderate negative space. The setting features a simple wooden table surface, standard European flatware, and a cotton napkin, evoking a modern bistro atmosphere with natural, even lighting. A small piece of rustic bread is subtly placed nearby, honoring traditional Spanish serving.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread to soak up the sauce.
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and vinegar.
Pair with a glass of Spanish red or white wine.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Cut potatoes into 2-3 cm cubes. Toss with 30 ml olive oil, 4 crushed garlic cloves, salt, and pepper.
Spread potatoes in a single layer on a baking tray. Roast for 30-35 minutes, or until golden and crispy. Turn halfway through.
Season chicken thighs with salt, pepper, and smoked paprika.
Heat remaining 30 ml olive oil in a large oven-safe pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs for 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown. Remove chicken and set aside.
Add 8 thinly sliced garlic cloves to the pan. Sauté for 1-2 minutes until fragrant, do not burn.
Pour in white wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Reduce by half.
Stir in chicken stock and lemon juice. Bring to a simmer.
Return chicken thighs to the pan. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Simmer for 10-15 minutes until chicken is cooked through and sauce slightly thickens.
Stir in most of the chopped parsley.
Serve chicken with crispy potatoes. Garnish with remaining fresh parsley and a lemon wedge.

recipes.recipe_name: Thai Basil Chicken Stir-fry
recipes.visual_description: The Thai Basil Chicken Stir-fry is presented on a clean white porcelain plate, alongside a mound of fluffy white jasmine rice. The chicken mince, cooked to a rich brown, is mixed with vibrant green wilted basil leaves and flecks of red chili. A perfectly fried egg with a crisp edge and a glossy, runny yolk rests atop the rice. The dish displays a balanced composition of textures and colors: the tender chicken, fresh basil, and the golden egg. The plate is moderately spaced, allowing each element to stand out. A set of chopsticks rests beside the plate, on a simple wooden table, under natural, even lighting, evoking a modern bistro setting with an authentic Thai culinary touch.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of prik nam pla (fish sauce with sliced chilies) for extra seasoning.
Traditionally eaten with jasmine rice as a staple accompaniment.
A fried egg (kai dao) is a common and essential topping.
instructions: Prepare the sauce: In a small bowl, combine soy sauce, fish sauce, oyster sauce, and sugar. Mix well.
Heat vegetable oil in a large wok or frying pan over high heat until smoking.
Add minced garlic and sliced chilies. Stir-fry for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add chicken mince to the wok. Break up the chicken with a spatula. Stir-fry for 5-7 minutes until chicken is cooked through and lightly browned. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).
Pour the prepared sauce over the chicken. Stir quickly to coat all ingredients.
Add the basil leaves. Stir-fry for 30-60 seconds until basil wilts but retains vibrant green color.
Remove from heat immediately.
While chicken cooks, fry 4 eggs sunny-side up until whites are set and yolks are runny.
Serve the Thai Basil Chicken stir-fry immediately over individual portions of cooked jasmine rice, topped with a fried egg.

recipes.recipe_name: Orange Vanilla Delice with Ginger Sablé and Cinnamon Gel
recipes.visual_description: A single, elegantly composed dessert rests on a pristine white bone china plate with a subtle, modern rim. The focal point is a vibrant orange-hued Orange Vanilla Crémeux, piped in a graceful, organic swirl or teardrop shape, showcasing its smooth, glossy texture. Beside it, a golden-brown, irregular Ginger Sablé biscuit provides a crisp textural contrast, its edges subtly browned. Small, translucent dollops of amber Cinnamon Citrus Gel are artfully placed around the crémeux, catching the light and adding a jeweled quality. Thin, glistening strips of candied orange peel are arranged delicately on top of the crémeux or alongside, providing a final touch of intense orange color and chewy texture. A single, fresh green micro herb or small mint leaf offers a vibrant counterpoint. The composition emphasizes natural curves and abundant negative space on the polished white plate, set against a luxurious white Carrara marble surface. Elegant silver dessert cutlery rests on a precisely folded white linen napkin. Dramatic professional lighting creates soft shadows, enhancing depth and dimension.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a strong espresso or a delicate digestif such as Grand Marnier or Cointreau.

ingredients.name: Fresh mint leaves or micro herbs

instructions: Prepare Ginger Sablé: Combine flour, icing sugar, ground ginger, and salt in a bowl. Cut in 75g cold butter until crumbly. Form into a dough. Wrap and chill for 30 minutes. Roll dough to 3mm thick. Cut into desired shapes (e.g., 6cm rounds or irregular pieces). Bake at 170°C for 10-12 minutes until golden. Cool completely.

Prepare Candied Orange Peel: Peel orange into long strips. Blanch strips in boiling water for 5 minutes. Drain. Repeat blanching two more times. Combine 100g sugar and 100ml water in a saucepan. Bring to a boil. Add blanched orange peel. Simmer gently for 30 minutes until peel is translucent. Drain and cool on a wire rack.

Prepare Orange Vanilla Crémeux: Bloom gelatine leaves in cold water. Scrape vanilla seeds from bean into a saucepan. Add orange juice, lemon juice, orange zest, and 50g granulated sugar. Heat until sugar dissolves. In a separate bowl, whisk egg yolks with remaining 50g granulated sugar. Slowly temper hot juice mixture into egg yolks, whisking constantly. Return mixture to saucepan. Cook over medium-low heat, stirring continuously, until thickened (nappe consistency, 82-85°C). Remove from heat. Stir in bloomed gelatine until dissolved. Allow to cool to 40°C. Gradually whisk in 150g cold butter cubes until smooth and emulsified. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve. Pour into a shallow dish. Cover surface with plastic wrap. Chill for at least 4 hours, or until firm.

Prepare Cinnamon Citrus Gel: Combine 100ml orange juice, 20ml lemon juice, 20g granulated sugar, and cinnamon stick in a small saucepan. Bring to a simmer. Remove from heat and let infuse for 15 minutes. Remove cinnamon stick. Reheat liquid gently. Whisk in agar-agar powder. Bring to a boil for 1 minute, whisking. Pour into a shallow container. Chill until set. Once firm, cut into small cubes or blend until smooth, adding a tiny amount of water if needed to achieve a gel consistency.

Assemble Dessert: On each plate, place one Ginger Sablé. Using a piping bag or spoon, artfully pipe or dollop a generous amount of Orange Vanilla Crémeux onto the sablé or directly onto the plate next to it. Arrange small, organic dollops or cubes of Cinnamon Citrus Gel around the crémeux. Place a few thin strips of Candied Orange Peel on top or beside the crémeux. Garnish with a single fresh mint leaf or micro herb for a touch of green.
notes: Ensure all ingredients for the crémeux are at precise temperatures for optimal emulsion.
The sablé can be prepared a day in advance and stored in an airtight container.
For the gel, agar-agar provides a firmer, cleaner set than gelatine for a modern texture.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Cherry Tomato and Basil Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A single pan-seared chicken breast, golden-brown with a crisp exterior, is centered on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The chicken is presented as a whole piece, unsliced. It is generously topped with a vibrant cherry tomato and basil sauce. The sauce features burst red cherry tomatoes, some still whole, interspersed with bright green torn basil leaves and slivers of golden garlic. A rich, glossy pan sauce lightly coats the chicken and pools around its base. The overall color palette is warm reds, vibrant greens, and golden brown. Textures include the firm chicken, soft tomatoes, and delicate basil. The plate is set on a simple wooden table, with a neatly folded cotton napkin to the left and a simple metal fork. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, with a softly blurred modern bistro background suggesting a casual restaurant atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread to sop up the sauce.
Pair with a simple side salad dressed with vinaigrette.
Serve alongside pasta or polenta.
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken breasts for 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C).
