recipes.recipe_name: Lemon Herb Roasted Chicken with Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single individual portion of Lemon Herb Roasted Chicken with Potatoes is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. A golden-brown, crispy-skinned roasted chicken thigh is the centerpiece. Thick-cut potato wedges, roasted to a tender interior and crisp, golden exterior, are arranged organically around it. The potatoes exhibit varied shades of golden yellow. Bright green flecks of roasted oregano and thyme are visible on both chicken and potatoes. Vibrant yellow roasted lemon wedges are nestled among the components, adding color. A sprig of fresh oregano garnishes the dish. The overall impression is rustic yet refined, with natural colors and appealing textures. The plate sits on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin and traditional flatware. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish against a soft, restaurant-style background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of tzatziki sauce.
Offer a simple Greek salad.
Accompany with crusty bread for dipping in pan juices.

ingredients.name: Potatoes (e.g., Maris Piper or Yukon Gold)

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Pat chicken thighs dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Wash potatoes. Cut into thick wedges, approximately 2 cm thick.
Finely chop garlic. Zest one lemon, then cut both lemons into thick wedges.
Roughly chop fresh oregano and thyme.
In a large roasting pan, combine chicken, potato wedges, chopped garlic, lemon zest, chopped herbs, and olive oil. Toss well to coat everything evenly.
Arrange chicken and potatoes in a single layer in the roasting pan. Place lemon wedges among the ingredients.
Pour chicken stock into the bottom of the pan.
Roast for 40-50 minutes, or until chicken skin is golden brown and crispy.
Check internal temperature of chicken. It must reach 75°C.
If needed, return to oven for further cooking.
Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C for food safety.
For extra crispiness, broil for the last 5 minutes, watching carefully.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Chicken and Vegetable Pasta Bake
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, featuring a generous portion of the creamy chicken and vegetable pasta bake. The top crust is a rich golden-brown from the baked mozzarella, with bubbly, melted edges hinting at its creamy interior. Beneath the crust, tender chunks of pan-seared chicken, cut into 2-3 cm pieces, are nestled amongst al dente penne pasta. Small, evenly diced 1 cm cubes of tender potato and bright orange carrot are integrated throughout the creamy, tomato-infused sauce, which coats every element. A sprinkle of vibrant green fresh chopped parsley garnishes the top, adding a fresh contrast. The overall presentation is hearty and inviting, with a balanced composition of colors and textures. The plate sits on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by standard European flatware and a folded white cotton napkin.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette.
Offer crusty Italian bread for dipping in the sauce.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Cook pasta in salted boiling water according to package directions until al dente. Drain.

Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe pan or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Cut chicken breast into 2-3 cm chunks. Add chicken chunks to the pan. Sear until browned on all sides and cooked through, reaching an internal temperature of 75°C. Remove chicken from pan and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add butter to the same pan. Finely chop onion and add to the pan. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.

Mince garlic. Peel and dice carrot into 1 cm cubes. Peel and dice potato into 1 cm cubes. Add minced garlic, diced carrot, and diced potato to the pan. Sauté for 8-10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until vegetables begin to soften.
Stir in canned diced tomatoes, milk, salt, black pepper, and dried oregano. Bring the sauce to a simmer. Cook for 5 minutes, allowing it to thicken slightly.
Return cooked chicken to the pan. Add cooked pasta. Stir gently to combine all ingredients with the sauce.
Grate Parmesan cheese and stir into the mixture. Shred mozzarella cheese and spread evenly over the top of the mixture.
Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until the cheese is melted, bubbly, and golden-brown.
Remove from oven. Let rest for 5 minutes. Chop fresh parsley and garnish before serving.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
Adjust seasoning to taste.

recipes.recipe_name: Mustard-Crusted Beef Steaks with Cheddar-Tomato Gratin
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Mustard-Crusted Beef Steak and Cheddar-Tomato Gratin is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The beef steak, a thick, unsliced cut, exhibits a rich, dark golden-brown mustard crust, contrasting with its juicy, medium-rare interior. Adjacent to the steak, a generous square portion of the gratin displays vibrant red tomato slices peeking through a bubbling, golden-brown cheddar cheese topping, lightly speckled with toasted breadcrumbs. The textures are distinct: crispy crust on the beef, tender steak, and soft baked tomatoes with melted cheese. A fresh sprig of thyme rests on the steak. The plate sits on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by standard silver flatware and a folded white cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting highlights the food's colors and textures, with a soft, out-of-focus modern bistro background.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Slice tomatoes into 5mm thick rounds. Arrange half the slices in a single layer in a small ovenproof gratin dish (approx. 20x20cm).
Season tomatoes with salt and pepper. Sprinkle with half the minced garlic and half the grated cheddar.
Repeat layering with remaining tomato slices, garlic, and cheddar. Top with fresh breadcrumbs.
Bake gratin for 25-30 minutes, until bubbly and golden brown. Remove from oven and set aside.
Pat beef steaks dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and black pepper on both sides.
In a small bowl, combine Dijon mustard and whole grain mustard. Spread a thin, even layer of mustard mixture over one side of each steak.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe frying pan over medium-high heat until shimmering.
Place steaks mustard-side down in the hot pan. Sear for 3-4 minutes until a golden-brown crust forms.
Flip steaks. Add butter and 2 thyme sprigs to the pan. Baste steaks with melted butter and thyme for 2-3 minutes.
Transfer the pan to the preheated oven. Roast for 5-7 minutes for medium-rare, or until desired doneness (internal temperature 60-65°C).
Remove steaks from oven. Transfer to a cutting board. Let rest for 5-10 minutes.
Serve each steak with a portion of the cheddar-tomato gratin. Garnish with fresh thyme sprigs.

recipes.recipe_name: Coq au Vin Traditionnel
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Coq au Vin is elegantly presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. Two succulent chicken pieces, deeply browned from searing and braising, rest at the center. The rich, glossy dark red wine sauce generously coats the chicken and the accompanying vegetables. Whole, earthy button mushrooms and tender, glistening pearl onions are artfully arranged around the chicken, showcasing their distinct shapes and textures. A sprinkle of bright green, freshly chopped parsley adds a vibrant color contrast and freshness. The dish is arranged organically, allowing the natural shapes of the ingredients to shine, with moderate negative space. The setting features a simple wooden table, a folded white cotton napkin beside the plate, and traditional European flatware, all under soft, natural, even lighting in a modern bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty baguette to soak up the rich sauce.

ingredients.name: Chicken thighs and drumsticks, bone-in, skin-on

instructions: Pat chicken pieces dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Preheat oven to 160°C.
In a large Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot, cook bacon lardons over medium heat until crispy. Remove bacon; set aside. Leave rendered fat in pot.
Add olive oil to the pot. Sear chicken pieces, skin-side down first, until deeply golden brown. This takes about 5-7 minutes per side. Remove chicken; set aside.
Add whole pearl onions and whole button mushrooms to the pot. Sauté until lightly browned, about 5 minutes.
Stir in minced garlic and tomato paste. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Sprinkle flour over the vegetables. Cook, stirring constantly, for 2 minutes.
Pour in red wine. Scrape the bottom of the pot to deglaze. Bring to a simmer and cook until the wine reduces by half.
Add chicken stock, fresh thyme sprigs, and bay leaf. Bring the liquid back to a simmer.
Return the seared chicken pieces to the pot, ensuring they are partially submerged in the liquid.
Cover the pot tightly. Braise in the preheated oven for 1.5-2 hours, or until chicken is very tender and an internal temperature of 75°C is reached.
Carefully remove chicken pieces, thyme sprigs, and bay leaf from the pot. Keep chicken warm.
Place the pot on the stovetop over medium heat. Reduce the sauce to desired consistency if needed. Stir in the reserved crispy bacon lardons.
Taste the sauce and adjust seasoning as necessary.
Serve chicken with the rich sauce, mushrooms, and pearl onions. Garnish generously with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Apple & Glutinous Rice Sphere with Chili-Shallot Caramel and Sweet Sausage Crumble
recipes.special_requests: тайская cuisine, Make it without any additional ingredients, just the ones I chose
recipes.visual_description: The dish presents a single, perfectly formed sphere of glossy, sweetened glutinous rice, its pristine white surface subtly reflecting light, positioned elegantly off-center on a pristine white bone china plate. Around its base, a scattering of translucent, golden-brown caramelized apple cubes provides a gentle textural contrast. A fluid, glistening line of amber chili-shallot caramel sweeps across the plate, its delicate spice and sweetness suggested by the subtle flecks of red chili and translucent shallot. Tiny, dark golden crumbles of sweet sausage are sparingly placed near the apple, offering an unexpected savory-sweet crunch. The plate is adorned with a single, paper-thin apple slice, artfully placed to add a touch of fresh color and height. Abundant negative space surrounds the composition, emphasizing its refined elegance. The setting features a superpremium wooden table, a pristine white linen napkin folded into a precise triangle, and dramatic professional lighting with soft shadows, highlighting the dish's architectural precision.
cultural_serving_suggestions: This modern dessert is best enjoyed with a small dessert spoon, allowing each component to be savored individually or in combination.
instructions: Wash glutinous rice until water runs clear. Soak rice in water for 2 hours. Drain thoroughly.
Steam drained rice for 20 minutes until tender and cooked through.

In a small saucepan, combine coconut milk, 15 g palm sugar, and a pinch of salt. Heat gently until sugar dissolves. Add steamed rice. Stir until liquid is fully absorbed and rice is glossy. Keep warm.

Remove pork sausage from casing. Crumble into a hot pan with 2 ml neutral oil. Cook until deeply browned and crispy. Drain excess fat. Mince cooked sausage very finely. Return to pan. Add 5 g palm sugar and a tiny pinch of salt. Stir over low heat until sugar melts and coats sausage, forming a sweet-savory crumble. Set aside.

Finely mince shallot and deseeded bird's eye chili. In a small saucepan, combine 10 g palm sugar and 15 ml water. Bring to a simmer until sugar dissolves. Add minced shallot and chili. Cook over medium-low heat, stirring occasionally, until mixture thickens into a glossy, translucent caramel with a hint of spice. Set aside.

Peel and dice half of the apple into 5mm cubes. In a small pan, melt 3 g granulated sugar with a tiny splash of water to form a light caramel. Add diced apple. Cook until just tender-crisp and lightly caramelized. Set aside. From the remaining apple, use a mandoline to shave 2-3 very thin slices for garnish.
Using clean hands or a small spherical mold, gently compress the warm sweetened glutinous rice into a perfect sphere, approximately 4 cm in diameter.

Place the glutinous rice sphere slightly off-center on a pristine white bone china plate. Artistically arrange the caramelized apple cubes around the base of the sphere. Drizzle the chili-shallot caramel in a natural, flowing line across the plate, leading towards the sphere. Sprinkle a small amount of the sweet sausage crumble delicately around the apple cubes and caramel. Garnish with one or two delicate, very thin apple slices, gently folded or placed for height and texture.

recipes.recipe_name: Khao Niao Sphere with Apple-Chili Caramel, Pandan-Mung Bean Roulade, and Crispy Shallot Tuile
recipes.visual_description: A pristine white bone china plate features a perfectly spherical, glistening coconut sticky rice at its heart, exuding a subtle cream hue. Around it, precisely diced, golden-brown caramelized apple cubes, infused with a hint of red chili, form a delicate arc. Three vibrant green pandan-mung bean roulade medallions, sliced with precision, are artfully placed, showcasing their smooth texture. A translucent, amber-colored crispy shallot tuile stands elegantly, providing architectural height. Bright green dots of coconut-lime gel add pops of fresh color and a smooth texture. The dish is garnished with a single, delicate edible orchid and a few vibrant red candied chili threads. Abundant negative space surrounds the components, highlighting their individual beauty and contrasting textures on the minimalist, elegant plate.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as an individual portion on a small dessert plate.
Provide a delicate dessert spoon for consumption.
Pair with a light, fragrant Thai tea or a chilled jasmine-infused water.
instructions: Prepare Pandan-Mung Bean Roulade: Soak mung beans 4 hours. Drain. Steam until tender. Mash into a smooth paste. In a small pot, combine mashed mung beans, 15g palm sugar, and a small piece of pandan leaf. Cook over low heat, stirring constantly, until mixture thickens and pulls away from the sides. Remove pandan leaf. Roll mixture into a small 5 cm log. Chill until firm.

Prepare Coconut Sticky Rice Sphere: Rinse glutinous rice until water runs clear. Soak rice 30 minutes. Drain. Steam rice with pandan leaf until tender, about 15 minutes. In a separate pot, heat 80ml coconut milk, 10g palm sugar, and a pinch of salt until sugar dissolves. Remove pandan leaf. Stir coconut milk mixture into steamed rice. Cover. Let stand 10 minutes. Form rice into a smooth sphere using plastic wrap.

Prepare Apple-Chili Caramel: Dice apple into 5mm cubes. In a small pan, melt 5g palm sugar. Add diced apple. Cook until softened and lightly caramelized. Mince bird's eye chili very finely. Stir chili into apple caramel. Set aside.

Prepare Crispy Shallot Tuile: Slice shallot paper-thin. In a small bowl, toss shallot slices with 5g granulated sugar. Spread thinly on parchment paper. Bake at 150°C (300°F) until golden brown and crisp, about 10-15 minutes. Watch carefully to prevent burning. Cool completely.

Prepare Coconut-Lime Gel: In a small saucepan, combine 20ml coconut milk, 5g granulated sugar, lime juice, agar-agar powder, and optional green food coloring. Bring to a boil. Simmer 1 minute, stirring. Pour into a shallow dish. Chill until set. Cut into small cubes or blend into a smooth gel.

Assemble Dish: Place coconut sticky rice sphere slightly off-center on a bone china plate. Arrange caramelized apple-chili mixture around the sphere. Slice the chilled pandan-mung bean roulade into three 1.5 cm thick medallions. Place medallions artistically on the plate. Gently place the crispy shallot tuile standing upright or leaning against the rice sphere. Dot plate with small amounts of coconut-lime gel. Garnish with a single edible flower and a few candied chili threads (optional, made by blanching thin chili strips and simmering in sugar syrup).
traditional_techniques: Making mung bean paste (Kanom Tua Paep technique)

recipes.recipe_name: Spinach Salad with Grilled Chicken, Pineapple, and Feta
recipes.visual_description: A generous, home-style individual portion of Spinach Salad with Grilled Chicken, Pineapple, and Feta is presented in a shallow, everyday ceramic bowl. Vibrant green baby spinach forms the base, with small cubes of golden-brown grilled chicken, bright yellow diced pineapple, and creamy white crumbled feta cheese artfully distributed on top. Scattered among these are crisp red bell pepper diced into 1 cm pieces, refreshing cucumber diced similarly, and thinly sliced purple-red onion. The ingredients are casually arranged, touching and overlapping, showcasing natural textures and colors, lightly glistening with a vinaigrette dressing. The bowl sits on a well-used wooden dining table, beside a simple fork and a casually placed cloth napkin, bathed in warm, cozy kitchen lighting, creating a relaxed, lived-in atmosphere.
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season with salt, pepper, and garlic powder.
Heat a grill pan or skillet over medium-high heat. Grill chicken for 6-8 minutes per side, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove and let rest for 5 minutes. Dice into small cubes.
While chicken cooks, prepare vegetables. Wash spinach and pat dry. Dice red bell pepper into 1 cm pieces. Dice cucumber into 1 cm pieces. Thinly slice red onion.
Peel and core the pineapple. Dice into 1 cm pieces.
Crumble the feta cheese.
Prepare the dressing. In a small bowl, whisk together 45 ml olive oil, white wine vinegar, Dijon mustard, salt, and pepper.
In a large serving bowl, combine spinach, diced red bell pepper, diced cucumber, thinly sliced red onion, diced pineapple, and diced chicken.
Drizzle the dressing over the salad ingredients. Toss gently to coat.
Sprinkle crumbled feta cheese over the top just before serving.
notes: Ensure chicken is fully cooled before adding to the salad to prevent wilting the spinach.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Vanilla Yogurt Chicken with Minted Cucumber Yogurt Sauce
recipes.visual_description: The dish presents golden-brown pan-seared chicken thighs, either whole or in robust, irregular chunks, showcasing a crisp exterior and tender interior. The chicken is centered on a clean white porcelain plate. Beside it, a generous swirl of creamy, white minted cucumber yogurt sauce provides a fresh contrast, flecked with vibrant green mint and grated cucumber texture. A sprig of fresh mint rests atop the sauce, adding an aromatic touch. A bright yellow lemon wedge is placed near the chicken. The plate features moderate negative space, enhancing the visual appeal. The setting is a modern bistro: a simple wooden table, a white cotton napkin folded beside the plate, and traditional flatware. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its rich colors and textures against an understated restaurant background. The portion is a single, refined serving.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with fluffy couscous or rice pilaf.
Offer warm pita bread or flatbread for scooping the sauce.
A side of simple tomato and cucumber salad with olive oil.
instructions: In a bowl, combine 250 g Greek yogurt, vanilla extract, minced garlic, 15 ml lemon juice, cumin, coriander, paprika, salt, and pepper. Mix well.
Add chicken thighs. Ensure chicken is fully coated. Cover and refrigerate for at least 2 hours, or up to 8 hours.
In a separate bowl, combine 150 g Greek yogurt, grated cucumber, chopped fresh mint, 10 ml lemon juice, and optional minced garlic. Season with salt to taste. Stir well. Refrigerate until serving.
Remove chicken from marinade. Scrape off excess marinade, but do not rinse. Heat olive oil in a large non-stick pan over medium-high heat.
Place chicken thighs in the hot pan. Sear for 6-8 minutes per side, until golden brown and cooked through. Internal temperature should reach 75°C.
Remove chicken from pan. Let rest for 5 minutes.
Serve chicken warm, accompanied by the Minted Cucumber Yogurt Sauce. Garnish with fresh mint leaves and a lemon wedge.
notes: For best flavor, marinate the chicken overnight.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Savory Raspberry-Honey Glaze and Herb Yogurt
recipes.visual_description: A single pan-seared chicken breast, golden-brown and glistening, rests on a clean white porcelain plate. The chicken, presented as a whole piece, is generously coated with a glossy, deep crimson raspberry-honey glaze, showcasing its vibrant fruit and savory notes. Beside the chicken, a creamy, pale green swirl of herb yogurt sauce provides a cool, tangy contrast. The plate features moderate negative space, enhancing the visual appeal of the main components. The setting is a modern bistro, with the dish placed on a simple wooden table. A neatly folded cotton napkin and polished silver cutlery complement the presentation. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and rich colors of the dish. The background is subtly blurred, maintaining focus on the food while suggesting a casual restaurant atmosphere.
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper.

Prepare the herb yogurt sauce: In a small bowl, combine Greek yogurt, chopped fresh mint, chopped fresh parsley, 1 minced garlic clove, lemon juice, a pinch of salt, and black pepper. Stir well. Refrigerate until serving.
Prepare the raspberry-honey glaze: In a small saucepan, heat 15ml olive oil over medium heat. Add minced shallot and the remaining minced garlic. Sauté until fragrant, about 2 minutes.
Add fresh raspberries, honey, red wine vinegar, and optional red pepper flakes to the saucepan. Bring to a simmer.

Cook, stirring occasionally, for 8-10 minutes until raspberries break down and the sauce thickens slightly. Mash raspberries gently with a fork. Strain the glaze through a fine-mesh sieve into a clean bowl, pressing solids to extract all liquid. Discard solids. Keep glaze warm.
Heat the remaining 15ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken breasts.
Sear chicken for 5-7 minutes per side, until golden brown and cooked through. Internal temperature must reach 75°C (167°F).
Pour the warm raspberry-honey glaze over the cooked chicken in the skillet. Turn chicken to coat evenly. Cook for 1 minute to allow glaze to adhere.
Serve chicken immediately with a dollop of herb yogurt sauce.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken with Tomato Sauce, Tagliatelle, and Roasted Carrots
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Pollo al Sugo con Tagliatelle e Carote Arrosto is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, set on a simple wooden table. Golden tagliatelle, coated in rich, vibrant red tomato sauce, forms a loose nest. Two tender, pan-seared chicken thigh pieces, golden-brown, are placed atop the pasta. Bright orange roasted carrot batons are arranged alongside, showing slight caramelization. Fresh green basil leaves are scattered over the dish for color. The plate is moderately spaced, focusing on the food. A cotton napkin and traditional flatware are positioned beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene, highlighting textures and colors in a modern bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with freshly grated Parmigiano-Reggiano.
Offer crusty bread to sop up the delicious sauce.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Cut carrots into 5 cm batons. Toss with 15 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Roast for 20-25 minutes until tender and lightly caramelized.
Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat 30 ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown. Internal temperature must reach 75°C. Remove chicken from pan.
Add remaining 15 ml olive oil to pan. Sauté diced onion for 5 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic, cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in white wine. Scrape up browned bits from the pan. Cook 2 minutes until reduced.
Add crushed tomatoes and chicken stock. Bring to a simmer. Return chicken to pan. Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 15 minutes.
Meanwhile, cook tagliatelle in salted boiling water according to package directions until al dente. Drain pasta, reserving 125 ml pasta water.
Remove chicken from sauce. Shred or cut into large chunks. Stir pasta into sauce. Add reserved pasta water if needed for desired consistency.
Serve pasta in bowls. Top with chicken and roasted carrots. Garnish with fresh basil. Serve with grated Parmigiano-Reggiano.

recipes.recipe_name: 7 Up Lemon Mousse Parfait
recipes.visual_description: The 7 Up Lemon Mousse Parfait is presented in a clear, elegant stemmed glass, showcasing its pale yellow, airy texture. The mousse is light and cloud-like, filling the glass to about two-thirds. A single piece of translucent, golden candied lemon peel, cut into a thin round, is artfully placed on top, adding a delicate contrast in texture and a touch of refined sweetness. The glass sits on a clean white porcelain plate, with a simple cotton napkin folded beside it. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a light wooden table surface. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting the mousse's delicate sheen and the candied peel's subtle sparkle. The presentation is clean, professional, and inviting, with moderate negative space on the plate.
instructions: Prepare candied lemon peel: Slice lemons into very thin rounds. Blanch in boiling water for 2 minutes. Drain. Repeat blanching two more times to remove bitterness.

Combine 100g sugar and 200ml water in a small saucepan. Bring to a simmer. Add blanched lemon slices. Simmer gently for 45-60 minutes until translucent. Remove lemon slices. Let cool on parchment paper.
Bloom gelatin: Sprinkle gelatin powder over 60ml cold water in a small bowl. Let stand for 5 minutes until softened.
Make lemon syrup: In a saucepan, combine 7 Up, lemon juice, lemon zest, and 50g sugar. Heat gently until sugar dissolves. Do not boil.
Melt bloomed gelatin: Place the gelatin bowl over a pot of simmering water (bain-marie) or microwave for 10-15 seconds until fully dissolved.
Combine gelatin and syrup: Stir the melted gelatin into the warm lemon syrup until thoroughly combined. Let cool to room temperature.
Whip cream: In a cold bowl, whip heavy cream until soft peaks form.
Fold mousse: Gently fold the cooled lemon-gelatin mixture into the whipped cream until just combined.
Assemble parfaits: Spoon mousse into individual serving glasses or bowls. Chill for at least 4 hours, or overnight, until set.
Garnish: Before serving, top each parfait with a piece of candied lemon peel.
notes: Optionally, layer with fresh raspberries or blueberries for added color and tartness.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Chicken Thighs with Garlic Potatoes and Sautéed Mushrooms
recipes.visual_description: A single roasted chicken thigh, golden-brown and crispy-skinned, rests centrally on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Beside it, a generous pile of rustic 2 cm potato chunks, roasted to a deep golden hue with slightly crisp edges, is visible. The potatoes are speckled with dark green rosemary and thyme leaves. Adjacent to the chicken and potatoes, a vibrant mound of earthy brown cremini mushrooms and translucent caramelized onion slices is arranged, glossy from sautéing, with hints of minced garlic. The dish presents a balanced composition of warm, inviting colors and varied textures. The plate sits on a simple wooden table surface in a modern bistro setting. A neatly folded cotton napkin and standard restaurant flatware are placed beside the plate, with soft, natural lighting illuminating the food against a subtly blurred, casual restaurant background.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Line a large baking tray with parchment paper.
Wash potatoes. Cut potatoes into 2 cm chunks. Place in a large bowl.
Mince 3 garlic cloves. Strip rosemary and thyme leaves from stems. Add minced garlic, rosemary, thyme, 30 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper to potatoes. Toss to coat evenly.
Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper on all sides.
Arrange seasoned potatoes on one side of the prepared baking tray. Place chicken thighs skin-side up on the other side of the tray.
Roast for 30 minutes. Flip potatoes. Continue roasting for another 15-20 minutes, or until chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C and potatoes are tender and golden brown.
While chicken and potatoes roast, prepare mushrooms and onions.
Slice mushrooms thinly. Slice onion thinly. Mince remaining 3 garlic cloves.
Heat remaining 30 ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add sliced onions. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened and lightly caramelized.
Add sliced mushrooms to the skillet. Cook for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until mushrooms release their liquid and brown.
Stir in minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in chicken stock. Bring to a simmer. Cook until liquid reduces by half, about 3-5 minutes. Season with salt and pepper.
Remove chicken and potatoes from oven. Let chicken rest for 5 minutes.
Plate one chicken thigh with a portion of roasted potatoes and sautéed mushrooms and onions. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: Ensure chicken thighs are patted very dry for crispier skin.
Adjust roasting time based on chicken thigh size and oven calibration.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Apple & Spelt Cake with Apple Core Syrup
recipes.visual_description: A rustic round cake with a deeply golden-brown crust sits on a light bamboo table. The cake has a slightly irregular, wholesome texture from spelt flour and sourdough. A single, substantial slice is centered on a handcrafted, matte cream ceramic plate. The moist, open crumb of the slice reveals tender, spiced apple chunks. A glossy, amber apple core syrup is generously drizzled over the slice, pooling slightly at the base. It is garnished simply with a fresh sprig of thyme. The remainder of the cake rests on a natural wood board in the soft-focused background. An undyed linen napkin is folded beside the plate. Soft, natural light highlights the cake's textures and warm colors, emphasizing its natural ingredients and sustainable preparation, offering a warm, inviting aesthetic.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Grease and flour a 20 cm round cake tin.

Prepare apple core syrup: Combine apple cores, peels, 200 ml water, and 50 g granulated sugar in a small saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat. Simmer for 15-20 minutes until liquid reduces and flavors infuse. Strain the syrup through a fine-mesh sieve, pressing solids to extract all liquid. Discard solids. Set syrup aside.
Peel, core, and dice 400 g apples into small cubes.
In a large bowl, whisk together sourdough starter, eggs, melted butter, and yogurt.
In a separate bowl, combine spelt flour, brown sugar, baking soda, salt, cinnamon, and nutmeg.
Add dry ingredients to wet ingredients. Mix until just combined. Do not overmix.
Gently fold in the diced apples.
Pour batter into the prepared cake tin. Smooth the top.
Bake for 40-50 minutes, or until a skewer inserted into the center comes out clean. Ensure internal temperature reaches 95°C (203°F).
Cool cake in the tin for 10 minutes. Invert onto a wire rack to cool completely.
Serve slices of cake drizzled generously with the prepared apple core syrup.
notes: This recipe utilizes apple cores and peels, which are often discarded, to create a flavorful syrup, embodying zero-waste principles.
Using sourdough starter adds a subtle tang and contributes to a unique texture, while also being an eco-conscious way to use starter discard.
Spelt flour offers a nutty flavor and contributes to the cake's rustic charm and nutritional profile.

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean White Bean and Vegetable Bake
recipes.visual_description: The Mediterranean White Bean and Vegetable Bake is presented in a rustic, shallow ceramic baking dish, showcasing a vibrant medley of ingredients. Creamy white cannellini beans are interspersed with bright red halved cherry tomatoes and tender green diced zucchini. Finely diced red onion and minced garlic are visible, integrated into the savory base. The dish has a slightly saucy consistency from the vegetable broth, clinging to the vegetables. A generous topping of crumbled white feta cheese provides a stark contrast, and fresh, roughly chopped green parsley is scattered across, adding a burst of color and freshness. The dish is placed on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a clean white porcelain side plate and a folded cotton napkin. The setting is minimally styled with natural, even lighting to highlight the food's authentic colors and textures, evoking a casual bistro atmosphere. A single individual portion is served on the side plate, featuring a balanced scoop of beans, tomatoes, and zucchini, topped with feta and parsley.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Drain and rinse cannellini beans.
Halve cherry tomatoes. Dice zucchini into 2cm cubes. Finely dice red onion. Mince garlic.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe pan or Dutch oven over medium heat.
Sauté diced red onion for 5 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in diced zucchini, halved cherry tomatoes, drained cannellini beans, and dried oregano.
Pour in vegetable broth. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Bring the mixture to a gentle simmer.
Transfer the pan to the preheated oven. Bake for 20-25 minutes.
Remove from oven. Stir in the zest and juice of one lemon.
Crumble feta cheese over the top. Roughly chop fresh parsley and sprinkle over the dish.
Serve hot directly from the pan.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Chicken Ragu Orecchiette with Parmesan Crema and Chili Gremolata
recipes.visual_description: A single, refined serving of Orecchiette with Braised Chicken Ragu is elegantly composed on a round, deep bone china plate with a subtle, sophisticated rim. The orecchiette, tossed in a rich, deep red-brown ragu, forms a natural, flowing mound in the center. Substantial, irregularly pulled chunks of tender braised chicken are nestled within the pasta, showcasing their moist texture. A delicate quenelle of pale ivory Parmesan crema is positioned artfully beside the pasta. A vibrant sprinkle of green parsley, bright lemon zest, and fiery red chili gremolata adorns the top, providing a precise pop of color and fresh texture. The composition utilizes abundant negative space, highlighting the dish as the focal point. The setting features a premium white Carrara marble surface, with exquisite Italian silver flatware (fork and spoon) resting on a pristine white linen napkin, precisely folded into a triangle. Dramatic professional lighting casts soft shadows, enhancing depth and texture against an ultra-minimalist background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty artisanal bread to sop up the rich ragu.
Pair with a robust Italian red wine, such as a Chianti Classico or Primitivo.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat 30 ml olive oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs until deeply golden on all sides. Remove chicken. Set aside.
Add remaining 30 ml olive oil and butter to the Dutch oven. Add diced onion. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and half of the minced dried chilies. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Deglaze with white wine. Scrape up any browned bits. Reduce by half.
Stir in passata, chicken stock, and oregano sprigs. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared chicken thighs to the pot. Ensure chicken is mostly submerged. Cover. Reduce heat to low.
Braise for 1.5 to 2 hours, or until chicken is fork-tender. Internal temperature should reach 75°C (167°F).
Remove chicken from ragu. Shred chicken into irregular, substantial chunks using two forks. Discard oregano sprigs. Return shredded chicken to the ragu. Stir well. Keep warm.

For the Parmesan Crema: Heat heavy cream in a small saucepan over medium-low heat. Bring to a gentle simmer. Remove from heat. Whisk in 100 g grated Parmesan cheese until smooth. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.
For the Chili Gremolata: Combine chopped parsley, lemon zest, and remaining minced dried chilies in a small bowl. Mix well.
Cook orecchiette pasta according to package directions until al dente. Drain, reserving 100 ml pasta water.
Add drained pasta to the chicken ragu. Add a splash of reserved pasta water if needed to loosen the sauce. Toss to coat evenly.
Plate individual portions of orecchiette and chicken ragu in the center of deep plates.
Spoon a quenelle of Parmesan crema alongside the pasta. Garnish generously with chili gremolata. Sprinkle with remaining 50 g grated Parmesan cheese.

recipes.recipe_name: Stuffed Pimento Peppers with Savory Rice & Mushroom Filling
recipes.visual_description: Four vibrant red pimento pepper halves, generously stuffed with a savory, earthy mixture of diced onion, sliced mushrooms, small cubes of butternut squash, and rice, are arranged naturally in a rustic, oval ceramic baking dish. The filling peeks out, showcasing varying shades of brown, green, and red from the vegetables and beans. A golden-brown crust of melted Gruyere cheese and toasted breadcrumbs covers the top of each pepper, offering a contrasting texture. A sprinkle of fresh, vibrant green parsley adds a pop of color. The dish sits on a well-used wooden dining table, with a simple, slightly textured off-white linen napkin casually folded beside it. Warm, cozy kitchen lighting illuminates the scene, highlighting the natural colors and textures of the dish. A sturdy, antique silver fork rests nearby. The overall presentation is homely and inviting, focusing on abundant portions.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty artisan bread for dipping into any juices.
A simple green salad with a light vinaigrette makes a fresh accompaniment.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Halve pimento peppers lengthwise. Remove seeds and membranes. Place cut-side up in a baking dish.
Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium heat. Add diced onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic, sliced mushrooms, and small cubes of butternut squash. Sauté for 8-10 minutes until vegetables are tender.
Stir in cooked rice, drained cannellini beans, and diced tomatoes. Mix well.
Pour in vegetable stock, dark beer, and optional pastis. Add ground grains of paradise, salt, and black pepper. Bring to a simmer.
Cook for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until liquid is mostly absorbed and mixture thickens slightly.
Spoon the filling evenly into the pimento pepper halves in the baking dish.
Combine grated Gruyere cheese and breadcrumbs in a small bowl. Sprinkle generously over the stuffed peppers.
Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until peppers are tender and the topping is golden brown and bubbly.
Garnish with chopped fresh parsley before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Ginger Chicken and Broccoli Soup
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Ginger Chicken and Broccoli Soup is presented in a clean, white porcelain bowl, centrally placed on a natural wooden table. The clear, golden broth holds tender, diced chicken cubes and vibrant, tender-crisp broccoli florets. Thin julienned ginger strips and bright green scallion rings are scattered over the top, adding fresh color and texture. The chicken is diced into 2 cm cubes, and broccoli florets are small and uniform. A pair of dark wooden chopsticks rests on a small ceramic chopstick rest beside the bowl. A simple white ceramic soup spoon is placed opposite. A white cotton napkin is neatly folded to the side. The background is a softly blurred modern bistro setting, emphasizing the dish with natural, even lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with chopsticks and a ceramic soup spoon.
Offer a small side dish of chili oil or extra soy sauce for personal seasoning.
instructions: Dice chicken breast into 2 cm cubes. Cut broccoli into small, bite-sized florets. Peel and julienne 25 g of ginger. Mince remaining 25 g ginger and garlic.
Heat neutral cooking oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Add diced chicken. Sear for 2-3 minutes until lightly browned. Remove chicken and set aside.
Add minced ginger and garlic to the pot. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in chicken stock. Bring to a simmer. Return seared chicken to the pot. Simmer for 10 minutes, ensuring chicken reaches 75°C internal temperature.
Add broccoli florets. Cook for 3-5 minutes until tender-crisp.
Stir in soy sauce and sesame oil. Season with salt and white pepper to taste.
Slice scallions thinly on the bias for garnish.
Ladle hot soup into bowls. Garnish each serving with julienned ginger and sliced scallions. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Roasted Mushroom and Garlic Soup
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of rich, creamy Roasted Mushroom and Garlic Soup is presented in a pristine white porcelain bowl. The soup possesses a deep, earthy brown hue, indicating the roasted mushrooms, with a smooth, velvety texture. A delicate swirl of heavy cream adorns the surface, and a sprinkle of vibrant green, finely chopped fresh chives is centered on top, adding a fresh contrast. The bowl is set on a light, natural wood table, accompanied by a folded white cotton napkin and a simple, polished metal spoon. The lighting is soft and even, highlighting the soup's warm tones and inviting texture. The background is subtly blurred, suggesting a modern bistro environment, keeping the focus entirely on the elegantly presented soup.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Toss thickly sliced or quartered mushrooms and peeled garlic cloves with 15 ml olive oil, a pinch of salt, and pepper.
Spread ingredients on a baking sheet. Roast for 20-25 minutes until tender and lightly caramelized.
In a large pot, melt butter with remaining 15 ml olive oil over medium heat.
Add diced onion. Sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add roasted mushrooms and garlic to the pot. Stir for 2 minutes.
Pour in vegetable broth and chopped thyme. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 10 minutes.
Remove from heat. Use an immersion blender to blend the soup until smooth. Alternatively, carefully transfer to a regular blender and blend in batches.
Stir in heavy cream. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Heat gently without boiling.
Ladle into bowls. Garnish with finely chopped fresh chives or parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Banana Ricotta Tartlet with Walnut-Cinnamon Crumble
recipes.special_requests: For breakfast. Try to be maximum healthy. Good looking and good taste dish. You can use not full ingredients. Try to maximum synergy
recipes.visual_description: A single, beautifully baked individual tartlet rests centered on a clean, white porcelain dessert plate. The tartlet features a golden-brown, slightly rustic whole wheat crust with gently fluted edges. The creamy, pale yellow ricotta-banana filling peeks through a generous, golden-brown crumble topping. The crumble is textured with visible pieces of chopped walnuts and dark cacao nibs, offering a pleasing contrast. Thin, neatly cut rounds of fresh banana are artfully arranged on top of the crumble. A delicate dusting of powdered sugar lightly covers the banana slices and edges of the crumble. The plate is set on a simple wooden table, with a folded cotton napkin beside it. Natural, even lighting highlights the tartlet's warm colors and textures, creating an inviting, casual bistro atmosphere. The entire plate is visible, with moderate negative space surrounding the tartlet.
instructions: Prepare the tartlet dough: In a bowl, combine all-purpose flour, whole wheat flour, and a pinch of salt. Cut cold butter into small cubes and rub into the flour until crumbly.
Add egg yolk and milk. Mix until just combined to form a dough. Do not overmix. Wrap in cling film. Chill for 30 minutes.
Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F).
On a lightly floured surface, roll out the dough to 3 mm thickness. Line a 10 cm tartlet mold. Trim excess dough. Prick the bottom with a fork.
Blind bake the tartlet shell for 10 minutes. Remove weights and bake for another 5 minutes until lightly golden. Set aside.
Prepare the filling: Mash 100 g of banana. In a bowl, combine ricotta cheese, mashed banana, 10 g granulated sugar, and 1 g cinnamon. Mix until smooth.

Prepare the crumble: In a separate small bowl, combine chopped walnuts, cacao nibs, remaining 1 g cinnamon, 10 g granulated sugar, and 5 g all-purpose flour. Add 5 g cold butter, cut into small pieces. Rub with fingertips until a coarse crumble forms.
Pour the ricotta-banana filling into the pre-baked tartlet shell. Sprinkle the walnut-cinnamon crumble evenly over the filling.
Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until the filling is set and the crumble is golden brown.
Let the tartlet cool completely on a wire rack.
Slice the remaining 20 g banana into thin rounds for garnish. Arrange on top of the cooled tartlet. Dust lightly with powdered sugar before serving.
notes: Ensure ricotta cheese is well-drained for best results.
Do not overmix the dough to keep it tender.
Adjust sweetness based on banana ripeness and personal preference.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Beef Roulades with Sauerkraut, Asadero, and Dark Beer Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A single portion is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate. Two thick, oval-shaped braised beef roulades, golden-brown from searing and deeply rich in color from the braising, are positioned slightly off-center. Each roulade is cross-sectioned to reveal the vibrant green of the sauerkraut and the melted, creamy white of the asadero cheese, creating a visually appealing spiral. A generous pool of glossy, dark amber dark beer sauce surrounds the roulades, catching the light. The sauce has a moderate viscosity, flowing naturally. A sprinkle of bright green, finely chopped fresh parsley provides a pop of color and freshness against the dark sauce and rich beef. The plate rests on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface. A neatly folded, crisp white cotton napkin is placed to the left. Standard, polished silver flatware (fork and knife) is arranged to the right. The background is softly blurred, hinting at a modern bistro atmosphere with warm, natural, even lighting that highlights the textures and colors of the food without harsh shadows.

ingredients.name: Beef top round or sirloin, thinly sliced

instructions: Pound beef slices to 3-4 mm thickness. Season both sides with salt and pepper.
Spread a thin layer of Dijon mustard on each beef slice. Top with a portion of sauerkraut and shredded asadero cheese.
Tightly roll each beef slice. Secure with kitchen twine or toothpicks.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe pot over medium-high heat. Sear roulades on all sides until deeply browned. Remove from pot.
Add diced onion to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic; cook for 1 minute more.
Stir in flour; cook for 1 minute. Pour in dark beer, scraping up any browned bits. Add beef broth and Worcestershire sauce. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared roulades to the pot, ensuring they are partially submerged in the liquid. Cover the pot.
Transfer to a preheated oven at 160°C. Braise for 1.5 to 2 hours, or until beef is very tender.
Remove roulades from pot. Remove twine or toothpicks. Skim any excess fat from the sauce. Simmer sauce on stovetop until slightly reduced and thickened. Adjust seasoning.
Spoon sauce onto plates. Place two roulades per person. Garnish with fresh parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Beef Cheeks with Grains of Paradise
recipes.visual_description: A single, large, deeply browned braised beef cheek rests prominently on a clean white porcelain plate. The beef is fork-tender, glistening with a rich, dark, reduced sauce. Beside it, a generous quenelle of creamy, smooth mashed potatoes provides a soft counterpoint. The beef, with its rich brown hues, contrasts with the off-white potatoes. Freshly chopped vibrant green parsley is scattered delicately over the beef and sauce, adding a pop of color and freshness. The setting is a simple wooden table with natural, even lighting, featuring a cotton napkin placed beside the plate, creating a casual yet refined dining atmosphere. The entire plate is visible, with moderate negative space, showcasing a professional and approachable presentation. The beef is presented as a whole piece, reflecting its slow-cooked tenderness.
instructions: Preheat oven to 150°C.
Crush grains of paradise using a mortar and pestle or spice grinder.
Season beef cheeks generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear beef cheeks until deeply browned on all sides. Remove beef from pot.
Dice onion, carrots, and celery into small cubes. Add to the same pot. Sauté 8-10 minutes until softened.
Mince garlic. Stir in minced garlic and tomato paste. Cook 2 minutes.
Deglaze the pot with red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom. Reduce wine by half.
Add beef stock, crushed grains of paradise, thyme sprigs, and bay leaves to the pot. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared beef cheeks to the pot. Ensure beef is mostly submerged in liquid. If not, add a little more stock.
Cover the pot tightly. Transfer to the preheated oven. Braise for 3-4 hours, or until beef is fork-tender.
Remove beef from the pot. Set aside. Strain the braising liquid into a clean saucepan, discarding solids. Skim any excess fat.
Reduce the braising liquid over medium heat until slightly thickened to a sauce consistency. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
For mashed potatoes: Peel and cut potatoes into equal-sized chunks. Boil in generously salted water until very tender (about 15-20 minutes).
Drain potatoes thoroughly. Return to the hot pot. Mash thoroughly until smooth.
Add butter and milk to mashed potatoes. Stir until smooth and creamy. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Chop fresh parsley.
Serve each braised beef cheek with a portion of creamy mashed potatoes. Spoon the reduced sauce generously over the beef. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Horseradish Beef Roulades
recipes.visual_description: Substantial pieces of seared beef roulades, revealing a creamy, off-white fermented horseradish filling, are arranged artfully on a handcrafted ceramic plate in a natural beige tone. The beef exterior boasts a rich, deep brown crust from searing, contrasting with the lighter, pungent horseradish interior. Each roulade piece is a compact chunk, showcasing the natural texture of the meat and the smooth, almost fluffy horseradish. A scattering of bright green, finely chopped chives provides a fresh color accent and delicate texture against the robust beef. The presentation is clean and minimalist, allowing natural colors and textures to shine. The plate sits on a light reclaimed wood surface, with a simple, undyed linen napkin. Soft, natural light illuminates the scene, emphasizing the dish's organic appeal.
instructions: Pound beef slices between two sheets of parchment paper until very thin, about 2-3mm thick. Season lightly with salt and pepper.
Spread an even layer of fermented horseradish paste over each beef slice.
Tightly roll each beef slice into a compact roulade. Secure with a toothpick if needed.
Heat olive oil in a skillet over medium-high heat. Sear roulades for 2-3 minutes per side until browned and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C).
Remove roulades from the pan. Add apple cider vinegar to the hot pan, scraping up any browned bits. Simmer briefly.
Slice roulades into 2-3 pieces each. Arrange on a platter. Drizzle with pan sauce (if made). Garnish with fresh chives.
notes: To make fermented horseradish paste: Grate 1 large horseradish root (approx. 100g). Combine with 10g non-iodized salt, 200ml filtered water, 5-6 black peppercorns, 2-3 dill sprigs, and 2 crushed garlic cloves in a clean jar. Ensure horseradish is fully submerged. Seal loosely or use an airlock. Ferment at room temperature (18-22°C) for 7-14 days, burping daily. Taste for desired tanginess. Store refrigerated. Remove dill, peppercorns, and garlic before using, then blend to a paste.

recipes.recipe_name: Thai Red Sardine & Walnut Curry
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant, creamy Thai Red Sardine & Walnut Curry is presented in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl. The rich, orange-red curry base, infused with coconut milk, cradles tender chunks of sardine. Thin strips of red bell pepper and wilted green spinach add contrasting colors and textures. A generous sprinkle of roughly chopped, toasted walnuts provides a textural crunch on top. The dish is garnished with bright green fresh coriander leaves and delicate slices of red chili, adding freshness and a hint of spice. The curry has a fluid consistency, reflecting its saucy nature. The bowl sits on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a white porcelain plate with a mound of fluffy steamed jasmine rice and a metal spoon, enhancing the authentic Thai dining experience. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its rich colors and inviting texture.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm steamed jasmine rice.
Offer a side of nam pla prik (fish sauce with sliced chilies) for those who prefer extra spice.

ingredients.name: Red bell pepper, cut into thin strips

instructions: Heat coconut oil in a large pot or wok over medium heat.
Add sliced shallots. Sauté for 2 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and grated ginger. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in red curry paste. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour in coconut milk. Bring to a gentle simmer, stirring.
Add red bell pepper strips. Simmer for 5 minutes until slightly tender.
Stir in fish sauce, lime juice, and brown sugar. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Gently add drained sardines. Simmer for 3 minutes to heat through. Avoid breaking them too much.
Add spinach. Cook until wilted, about 1-2 minutes.
Remove from heat. Stir in half of the toasted walnuts.
Ladle curry into deep serving bowls.
Garnish with remaining toasted walnuts, fresh chopped coriander, and sliced red chili.
Serve immediately with steamed jasmine rice.
traditional_techniques: Phad Prik Gaeng (stir-frying curry paste with oil to release aromas)
Balancing the four fundamental Thai tastes: spicy, sour, sweet, and salty

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Chickpea and Vegetable Stew
recipes.visual_description: The Mediterranean Chickpea and Vegetable Stew is served in a wide, shallow white ceramic bowl, presenting a vibrant and comforting composition. Tender-crisp broccoli florets, uniformly diced red and yellow bell peppers, and finely diced celery pieces are distinctly visible, nestled among plump, creamy chickpeas. The stew boasts a rich, reddish-orange color from the spiced tomato base, with a natural sheen. It maintains a fluid, saucy consistency. A generous scattering of freshly chopped vibrant green parsley provides a fresh contrast. A bright yellow lemon wedge, ready for squeezing, rests on the bowl's rim. The bowl is placed on a light, rustic wooden table surface. Alongside, a folded off-white cotton napkin and modern, simple metal flatware complete the individual setting. The background is softly blurred, evoking a casual bistro atmosphere with natural, even lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm crusty bread for dipping.
Serve alongside a simple green salad with a lemon-herb vinaigrette.
Offer a side of couscous or rice.
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add diced onion. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic, diced celery, and diced bell pepper. Cook for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until vegetables start to soften.
Stir in ground cumin, ground coriander, smoked paprika, and turmeric. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add diced tomatoes and vegetable broth. Bring to a simmer.
Add drained chickpeas and broccoli florets. Stir well.
Cover and simmer for 15-20 minutes, or until broccoli is tender-crisp.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Stir in half of the fresh chopped parsley. Squeeze in juice from half a lemon.
Serve hot, garnished with remaining fresh parsley and a lemon wedge.

recipes.recipe_name: Moroccan Chicken Tagine with Preserved Lemon and Olives
recipes.visual_description: A single portion served in an authentic shallow ceramic tagine base on a rustic wooden table. Two whole, bone-in chicken thighs are positioned centrally, featuring golden-brown rendered skin coated in a thick, vibrant yellow saffron and turmeric sauce. The sauce contains visible softened diced onions. Scattered around the chicken are bright green whole cracked olives and thin yellow strips of preserved lemon peel. A cinnamon stick rests to the side of the meat. The dish is garnished with a generous amount of roughly chopped emerald-green cilantro and parsley. A side bowl of fluffy steamed couscous and a clean white cotton napkin are placed nearby. Lighting is natural and soft, highlighting the glossy texture of the braising liquid.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm khobz or crusty bread to soak up the sauce
Accompany with a side of steamed couscous
Serve with a traditional Moroccan mint tea

ingredients.name: Preserved lemon, peel only, sliced into strips

instructions: Pat chicken dry with paper towels.
Season chicken with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a tagine or heavy-bottomed pot over medium heat.
Sear chicken thighs skin-side down for 6 minutes until golden brown.
Turn chicken and sear for 3 minutes.
Remove chicken from the pot and set aside.
Add diced onions to the pot.
Sauté onions for 8 minutes until translucent and soft.
Stir in garlic, ginger, turmeric, cumin, and saffron.
Cook spices for 1 minute until fragrant.
Return chicken to the pot with the cinnamon stick.
Pour in chicken stock until chicken is half-submerged.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 35 minutes.
Verify chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Add preserved lemon strips and olives.
Simmer uncovered for 10 minutes to thicken the sauce.
Stir in cilantro and parsley before serving.
notes: Rinse preserved lemons under cold water to remove excess salt before slicing.
Use a diffuser if cooking in a clay tagine on a gas stove to prevent cracking.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Beef Tenderloin, Celery Root Puree, Compressed Apple, Apple Gastrique
recipes.visual_description: A single starter portion is presented on an elegant, round, matte white designer plate, set on a premium grey veined marble surface. The plate features abundant negative space, enhancing the architectural precision of the composition. A creamy, fluid smear of celery root puree anchors the dish, sweeping across one side. Nestled atop is a perfectly seared beef tenderloin chunk, boasting a rich, dark brown crust and a tender, rosy interior. Its natural form is preserved, not sliced. Around the beef, several translucent, pale green compressed apple batons are artfully scattered, catching the light. A glistening, dark amber apple gastrique is precisely drizzled over the beef and across the plate, creating delicate lines. A single, vibrant green microgreen sprig, such as chervil, adds a final delicate touch of color and height. The lighting is dramatic, casting soft shadows, highlighting textures. A pristine white linen napkin, precisely folded into a triangle, and elegant silverware are subtly present in the background, maintaining a minimalist, luxury Michelin setting.
instructions: Divide beef tenderloin into four 100g portions. Season generously with salt and pepper. Vacuum seal each portion individually. Cook in a water bath at 54°C for 2 hours.

Peel and dice celery root into 1cm cubes. Boil in heavily salted water until fork-tender, approximately 15-20 minutes. Drain thoroughly. Transfer to a blender. Add butter and heavy cream. Blend until perfectly smooth. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.

Peel and core one Granny Smith apple. Cut into precise 5mm x 5mm x 3cm batons. Place apple batons in a vacuum seal bag with a pinch of sugar and a few drops of apple cider vinegar. Vacuum seal tightly to compress the apples. Set aside.

Finely dice the shallot. In a small saucepan, heat a drizzle of olive oil over medium heat. Sauté diced shallot until translucent. Add sugar and caramelize lightly. Deglaze with apple cider vinegar. Reduce by half. Add beef stock and reduce until the gastrique is syrupy. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve. Keep warm.

Remove beef tenderloin from vacuum bags. Pat very dry with paper towels. Heat olive oil in a high-heat skillet. Sear beef tenderloin on all sides until a deep, golden-brown crust forms, about 1-2 minutes total. Rest for 5 minutes.

To plate, create an artistic smear of celery root puree across the plate. Place one seared beef tenderloin portion (as a whole chunk) on the puree. Artfully arrange a few compressed apple batons around the beef. Drizzle the apple gastrique over and around the beef. Garnish with a small sprig of microgreens or chervil.

recipes.recipe_name: Stuffed Manicotti with Spinach and Ricotta
recipes.visual_description: The dish features golden-baked manicotti, generously filled with creamy ricotta and vibrant green spinach. Three to four manicotti tubes, each approximately 10 cm long, are nestled on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. They are bathed in a rich, glossy red marinara sauce, with some tubes peeking through. A delicate sprinkle of grated Parmesan cheese lightly dusts the exposed pasta, adding a subtle golden hue. Fresh basil leaves, torn into small pieces, are scattered over the top, providing a pop of contrasting green and aromatic freshness. The pasta has a tender yet firm texture, with the sauce clinging invitingly. A simple wooden table surface and a cotton napkin complete the casual bistro setting. Traditional flatware is arranged beside the plate.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty ciabatta bread for dipping in sauce.
Offer extra grated Parmesan cheese at the table.
Pair with a light green salad dressed with vinaigrette.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Cook manicotti according to package directions. Cook until al dente. Drain and rinse with cold water. Set aside.
Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium heat. Add minced garlic. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add fresh spinach to the pan. Cook until wilted, about 3-5 minutes. Squeeze out excess water from the spinach. Chop roughly.
In a large bowl, combine ricotta cheese, chopped spinach, grated Parmesan, egg, nutmeg, salt, and pepper. Mix well.
Spoon or pipe the ricotta-spinach filling into each cooked manicotti tube.
Spread a thin layer of marinara sauce on the bottom of a 20x30 cm baking dish.
Arrange the filled manicotti tubes in a single layer over the sauce.
Pour remaining marinara sauce over the manicotti. Ensure tubes are covered.
Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until bubbling and heated through.
Garnish with fresh basil before serving.
notes: Ensure spinach is thoroughly drained to prevent a watery filling.
Do not overcook manicotti during initial boiling, as it will bake further.
traditional_techniques: Layering and baking of pasta dishes

recipes.recipe_name: Pollo alla Cacciatora
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Pollo alla Cacciatora is presented on a wide, matte white porcelain plate. Two whole, bone-in chicken thighs are stacked slightly in the center, featuring deeply browned, caramelized skin. A thick, rustic sauce covers the base of the plate, filled with visible small cubes of orange carrots, green celery, and translucent onions. Whole, dark purple kalamata olives are nestled within the vibrant red tomato sauce. A light dusting of bright green chopped parsley and a single fresh rosemary sprig garnish the top. Two thick batons of grilled sourdough bread lean against the side of the chicken. The lighting is natural and soft, emphasizing the glossy texture of the braised sauce and the crispness of the chicken skin.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with toasted sourdough bread to soak up the sauce
Accompany with a glass of medium-bodied Italian red wine
Place on a bed of soft, buttery polenta
instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a wide braising pan over medium-high heat.
Place chicken skin-side down in the pan.
Sear for 6 minutes until the skin is deep golden and crisp.
Flip chicken and cook for 2 minutes.
Remove chicken from pan and set aside.
Add onion, carrot, and celery to the remaining fat.
Sauté vegetables for 8 minutes until softened.
Stir in garlic, rosemary, and sage. Cook for 1 minute.
Pour in red wine. Scrape the bottom of the pan to deglaze.
Simmer wine for 3 minutes until reduced by half.
Add crushed tomatoes and stir to combine.
Place chicken thighs back into the sauce.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 25 minutes.
Check internal temperature of chicken reaches 75°C.
Stir in olives and simmer uncovered for 5 minutes.
Remove rosemary sprigs before serving.
Garnish with chopped parsley.
notes: Always use a meat thermometer to ensure chicken reaches the safe internal temperature of 75°C
Browning the skin thoroughly at the start is essential for the final texture
The sauce should be thick and chunky, not watery

recipes.recipe_name: Spiced Apple Crumble Cake
recipes.visual_description: A single generous slice of Spiced Apple Crumble Cake sits on a simple, off-white ceramic plate. The plate rests on a well-used wooden dining table. The cake slice shows a golden-brown, crumbly streusel topping. Beneath, a moist, light-brown cake holds soft, tender 1 cm diced apple cubes. Textures vary: crisp crumble, tender cake, yielding apple. A light dusting of powdered sugar covers the top. In the background, the remaining 6-inch round cake is visible on a simple cake stand. A casually placed linen napkin and a fork complete the homely scene. Lighting is warm, evoking a family kitchen.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Served warm
Pairs well with vanilla ice cream or whipped cream
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Grease and flour a 15 cm (6-inch) round cake pan.
Prepare crumble topping: Combine 50g flour, 30g sugar, and 1.25g cinnamon in a bowl. Cut in cold 30g butter cubes until mixture resembles coarse crumbs. Set aside.
For the cake: In a large bowl, cream softened 75g butter and 100g sugar until light and fluffy.
Beat in the egg until well combined.
In a separate bowl, whisk together 150g flour, 5g baking powder, 2.5g cinnamon, and 1.25g salt.
Gradually add dry ingredients to wet ingredients, alternating with 60ml milk. Mix until just combined. Do not overmix.
Fold in the 1 cm diced apples.
Pour batter into the prepared cake pan. Spread evenly.
Sprinkle the reserved crumble topping evenly over the cake batter.
Bake for 35-45 minutes, or until a wooden skewer inserted into the center comes out clean.
Cool cake in the pan for 10 minutes. Then invert onto a wire rack to cool completely.

recipes.recipe_name: Paella de Pollo y Pimientos
recipes.visual_description: A generous individual portion of golden-hued Paella de Pollo y Pimientos is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The saffron-infused rice is a vibrant orange-yellow. Visible are tender chunks of seared chicken, roasted red and green bell pepper diced into 2 cm squares, and finely diced tomatoes, creating rich texture contrast. A slight socarrat crust is visible at the bottom. A sprinkle of fresh chopped parsley adds aroma and color. A quartered lemon wedge sits to the side. The plate rests on a simple light wooden table. A folded cotton napkin is beside it. The background suggests a modern bistro, softly blurred, with warm, natural lighting. The paella is a cohesive, slightly mounded portion. Chicken pieces are whole chunks. Traditional Spanish flatware, fork and spoon, are arranged beside the plate.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve directly from the paella pan at the table for a communal experience.
Offer crusty bread to sop up the flavorful juices.
Pair with a dry white wine or sangria.
Eat with a fork, scooping the rice and ingredients together.
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large paella pan or wide, shallow skillet over medium-high heat.
Season chicken chunks with salt and pepper. Add chicken to the pan. Sear until golden brown on all sides. Remove chicken from pan.
Dice onion. Add to the pan. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Mince garlic. Dice red and green bell peppers. Add to the pan. Sauté for 7-8 minutes until peppers soften.
Stir in grated tomatoes and smoked paprika. Cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until sauce thickens slightly.
Return chicken to the pan. Stir in rice, ensuring it is well coated with the sofrito.
Steep saffron threads in a little warm broth. Pour in remaining chicken broth and saffron liquid. Bring to a simmer.
Arrange chicken and vegetables evenly in the pan. Do not stir the rice after this point.
Reduce heat to medium-low. Cook uncovered for 15-20 minutes, or until most liquid is absorbed and rice is tender. A crust (socarrat) should form at the bottom.
If rice is still firm, add a little more hot broth and continue cooking.
Remove paella from heat. Cover with foil or a clean kitchen towel. Let rest for 5-10 minutes.
Garnish with fresh parsley. Serve immediately with lemon wedges.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
Avoid stirring the rice once the broth is added to allow the socarrat to form.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Mushroom Risotto
recipes.visual_description: Serve the risotto on a flat white porcelain dinner plate. The consistency is fluid and spreads naturally across the plate, appearing free-flowing rather than molded. The rice grains are distinct, coated in a glossy, creamy sauce. Large 3cm chunks of golden-brown seared chicken thighs are distributed throughout the rice. Sliced cremini and shiitake mushrooms show deep caramelization and earthy brown tones. The dish features a pale golden hue. Finely minced flat-leaf parsley provides a vibrant green contrast. A light dusting of finely grated Parmesan cheese covers the surface. The arrangement is organic. Beside the plate sits a heavy silver spoon and a folded white cotton napkin on a light oak table. Natural side lighting highlights the creamy texture.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately while the consistency remains fluid
Accompany with a crisp dry white wine such as Pinot Grigio
Provide extra grated Parmesan at the table
instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 3cm chunks.
Dice onion into 5mm pieces.
Mince garlic cloves.
Slice mushrooms into 5mm thick pieces.
Heat 20ml olive oil in a wide pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken chunks until browned and internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove chicken from pan and set aside.
Add mushrooms to the same pan. Sauté until moisture evaporates and edges brown.
Remove mushrooms and set aside.
Melt 20g butter in the pan. Add onion and garlic.
Cook until softened but not browned.
Add rice. Stir 2 minutes to toast the grains until edges are translucent.
Pour in white wine. Stir until liquid is fully absorbed.
Add 200ml warm stock. Stir continuously until liquid is absorbed.
Repeat stock additions one ladle at a time, stirring constantly, until rice is tender but firm.
Return chicken and mushrooms to the pan.
Remove from heat.
Vigorously stir in remaining 30g butter and Parmesan cheese to create a creamy emulsion.
Season with salt and pepper. Fold in chopped parsley.
notes: Keep the chicken stock at a low simmer in a separate pot to maintain cooking temperature.
Stirring constantly is essential to release rice starches for a creamy texture.
Ensure chicken reaches the safety temperature of 75°C during the initial searing phase.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Crab Stuffed Mushrooms with Tomato Cream Sauce
recipes.visual_description: The dish features two generously stuffed, oven-baked cremini mushrooms, boasting a rich golden-brown topping of melted Parmesan and mozzarella, resting gracefully on a vibrant, creamy tomato-red sauce. The mushrooms, with their tender, earthy caps, are packed with a savory filling of finely diced chicken and delicate white crab meat, interspersed with sautéed onion and mushroom stem pieces. The sauce, smooth and glossy, forms an inviting base, its warm color contrasting with the mushrooms. A sprinkle of fresh, bright green chopped parsley adorns the top, adding a pop of color and freshness. The plate is clean white porcelain, centered on a light wooden table. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's textures and colors. Standard silver cutlery and a folded cotton napkin complete the casual bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a crisp green salad tossed in a light vinaigrette.
Offer crusty artisan bread for dipping in the sauce.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Clean mushrooms. Carefully remove stems. Finely chop mushroom stems.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a pan over medium heat. Sauté chopped mushroom stems and diced onion until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute more.

Transfer sautéed vegetables to a bowl. Add diced cooked chicken, flaked crab meat, 30g grated Parmesan, 30g shredded mozzarella, half of the chopped parsley, salt, and pepper. Mix well. Add 60ml chicken broth to moisten.
Stuff mushroom caps generously with the chicken and crab mixture. Place stuffed mushrooms on a baking sheet.
Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until mushrooms are tender and stuffing is heated through.
While mushrooms bake, prepare the sauce. Melt 30g butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Whisk in 30g flour. Cook 1 minute to form a roux.
Gradually whisk in warm milk until smooth. Cook, stirring constantly, until sauce thickens.
Stir in crushed tomatoes. Bring to a simmer. Add remaining 20g grated Parmesan and 20g shredded mozzarella. Stir until melted and smooth. Season with salt and pepper.
To serve, spoon a generous amount of tomato cream sauce onto each plate. Arrange two stuffed mushrooms per plate on the sauce.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley. Serve immediately.
notes: For best flavor, use fresh, good quality crab meat.
Ensure chicken is fully cooked to an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) before dicing and mixing into the stuffing.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Chicken and Vegetable Risotto with Parmesan
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of creamy Chicken and Vegetable Risotto is presented in a shallow, matte white porcelain bowl. The risotto, a pale golden hue from the saffron (if used) and Parmesan, flows naturally, not stiffly mounded. Visible throughout are vibrant orange small diced carrots and bright yellow corn kernels, offering pops of color. On top of the risotto, several golden-brown seared chicken chunks are arranged organically, showcasing their crispy exterior. A dusting of finely grated Parmesan cheese covers the chicken and risotto, with a sprinkle of fresh, bright green chopped parsley providing a final flourish. The bowl sits on a simple light wooden table, accompanied by traditional silver flatware and a folded white cotton napkin. Natural, even light illuminates the dish, highlighting its rich texture and inviting warmth against a subtly blurred, casual bistro background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately after preparation to enjoy its creamy texture.
Offer extra grated Parmesan cheese at the table.
Pair with a light, crisp white wine.
instructions: Pat chicken breast dry. Cut into 3 cm chunks. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken chunks for 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through to 75°C. Remove chicken and set aside.
In the same pan, melt 30 g butter with remaining 15 ml olive oil over medium heat. Add chopped onion. Sauté until translucent, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and diced carrots. Cook for 3 minutes until slightly softened.
Add Arborio rice. Stir constantly for 2 minutes until grains are translucent at the edges.
Pour in white wine. Stir until completely absorbed.

Add one ladle of warm chicken broth. Stir continuously until absorbed. Repeat this process, adding broth one ladle at a time, allowing each addition to be absorbed before adding the next. This takes about 18-20 minutes.
After 15 minutes of broth additions, stir in sweet corn kernels. Continue adding broth and stirring.
When rice is al dente and risotto is creamy, remove from heat. Stir in remaining 30 g butter and grated Parmesan cheese. The risotto should be fluid.
Gently fold in the cooked chicken chunks. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Serve immediately, garnished with fresh chopped parsley and extra Parmesan.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Veal Medallions with Chanterelle-Chestnut Ragout and Madeira-Truffle Jus
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate within a modern bistro setting. A single seared veal medallion, golden-brown with a delicate crust, is placed slightly off-center. Its interior reveals a tender, pale pink hue. Beside it, a generous mound of vibrant chanterelle and chestnut ragout creates a textural contrast. The chanterelles, some whole and some halved, exhibit rich golden-orange tones, interspersed with irregular chunks of light brown chestnuts. A glossy, dark Madeira-veal jus lightly coats the ragout and pools subtly around the veal. Delicate, translucent shavings of white truffle adorn the veal and ragout, adding an elegant touch. A sprinkle of bright green, finely chopped fresh parsley provides a final pop of color. The plate maintains ample negative space. A simple cotton napkin rests beside the plate, with classic European flatware. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and colors of the ingredients, creating an inviting, refined presentation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: A crusty baguette to sop up the sauce
A glass of full-bodied red wine
instructions: Pat veal medallions dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat 15ml olive oil and 20g butter in a large pan over medium-high heat. Sear veal medallions 3-4 minutes per side for medium-rare. Remove veal from pan. Keep warm.
In the same pan, add remaining 15ml olive oil. Sauté finely diced shallots until softened, about 2 minutes. Add minced garlic and sauté for 1 minute more.
Add cleaned chanterelle mushrooms to the pan. Sauté until softened and lightly browned, about 5-7 minutes. Add roughly chopped chestnuts.
Pour Madeira wine into the pan. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom. Reduce by half, about 3 minutes.
Pour in veal stock and add thyme sprigs. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to medium-low. Simmer until sauce slightly thickens, about 10-12 minutes. Remove thyme sprigs.
Stir in remaining 30g butter. Season sauce with salt and pepper to taste.
Spoon a generous amount of chanterelle-chestnut ragout onto each plate. Place a seared veal medallion on top or beside the ragout.
Shave fresh white truffle generously over the veal and ragout. Garnish with finely chopped fresh parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Pollo alla Cacciatora
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Pollo alla Cacciatora is presented on a wide, matte white porcelain plate.
