Two whole, bone-in chicken thighs are stacked slightly in the center, featuring deeply browned, caramelized skin. A thick, rustic sauce covers the base of the plate, filled with visible small cubes of orange carrots, green celery, and translucent onions. Whole, dark purple kalamata olives are nestled within the vibrant red tomato sauce. A light dusting of bright green chopped parsley and a single fresh rosemary sprig garnish the top. Two thick batons of grilled sourdough bread lean against the side of the chicken. The lighting is natural and soft, emphasizing the glossy texture of the braised sauce and the crispness of the chicken skin.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with toasted sourdough bread to soak up the sauce
Accompany with a glass of medium-bodied Italian red wine
Place on a bed of soft, buttery polenta
instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a wide braising pan over medium-high heat.
Place chicken skin-side down in the pan.
Sear for 6 minutes until the skin is deep golden and crisp.
Flip chicken and cook for 2 minutes.
Remove chicken from pan and set aside.
Add onion, carrot, and celery to the remaining fat.
Sauté vegetables for 8 minutes until softened.
Stir in garlic, rosemary, and sage. Cook for 1 minute.
Pour in red wine. Scrape the bottom of the pan to deglaze.
Simmer wine for 3 minutes until reduced by half.
Add crushed tomatoes and stir to combine.
Place chicken thighs back into the sauce.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 25 minutes.
Check internal temperature of chicken reaches 75°C.
Stir in olives and simmer uncovered for 5 minutes.
Remove rosemary sprigs before serving.
Garnish with chopped parsley.
notes: Always use a meat thermometer to ensure chicken reaches the safe internal temperature of 75°C
Browning the skin thoroughly at the start is essential for the final texture
The sauce should be thick and chunky, not watery

recipes.recipe_name: Mascarpone Chicken Gnudi with Candied Orange and Pistachio
recipes.visual_description: Four delicate, pillow-soft mascarpone chicken gnudi, each about 3 cm long, are artfully arranged on an elegant bone china plate. The gnudi are a creamy ivory color, lightly kissed with a golden hue from the butter. A shimmering, translucent orange glaze cascades gracefully over them, creating subtle pooling. A precise scattering of vibrant green, roughly chopped pistachios provides textural contrast and a pop of color. Tiny, jewel-like pieces of translucent candied orange peel are strategically placed to catch the light. The composition is organic and flowing, with ample negative space. The plate rests on a polished dark wood table, with dramatic, directional lighting creating soft shadows. A pristine white linen napkin, folded into a crisp triangle, is placed beside the plate. The overall presentation is minimalist and refined, showcasing the luxurious ingredients and delicate craftsmanship.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Served as a 'piccolo dolce' (small sweet) or a unique antipasto during a multi-course tasting menu.
Presented on individual small plates for each guest, reflecting a fine-dining Italian experience.
instructions: Poach chicken breast in lightly salted water until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Cool completely. Finely shred the cooked chicken.
In a bowl, combine shredded chicken, mascarpone, ricotta, egg yolk, potato starch, and a pinch of salt. Mix gently until just combined. Do not overmix.
Dust a clean surface with a little extra potato starch. Gently form the mixture into small, oval-shaped gnudi, about 2-3 cm long. Roll each gnudi lightly in potato starch to coat.

Bring a large pot of lightly salted water to a gentle simmer. Carefully drop the gnudi into the simmering water. Cook for 3-4 minutes, or until they float to the surface and are cooked through. Remove with a slotted spoon and drain well.

While gnudi cook, prepare the orange glaze. In a small saucepan, combine granulated sugar and orange juice. Heat gently, stirring until sugar dissolves. Simmer for 2-3 minutes until slightly thickened.
In a separate small pan, melt butter over low heat. Add the drained gnudi and gently toss to coat in butter.
Toast shelled pistachios in a dry pan until fragrant. Roughly chop.
To serve, arrange 3-4 warm gnudi on each plate. Drizzle with orange glaze. Garnish with finely diced candied orange peel and chopped pistachios.
notes: Handle gnudi very gently as the mixture is delicate.
Ensure water is barely simmering to prevent gnudi from breaking apart.
For best results, serve immediately after cooking.

recipes.recipe_name: Mango Passion Fruit Mousse Dome with Coconut Dacquoise
recipes.visual_description: A single, impeccably plated Mango Passion Fruit Mousse Dome rests on a pristine white bone china plate. The dome, a vibrant, glossy yellow-orange from its mirror glaze, reflects light subtly. Its perfectly smooth, curved surface contrasts with the delicate, textured edge of the coconut dacquoise base peeking out. Adjacent to the dome, a small, artfully arranged cluster of uniformly cut 5mm mango cubes provides a burst of fresh, bright yellow. A single, small, verdant mint sprig is precisely positioned for an elegant color accent. Abundant negative space surrounds the dessert, emphasizing its refined form. The plate sits on a smooth, grey-veined Carrara marble surface, illuminated by dramatic professional lighting that casts soft shadows, enhancing depth. A crisp white linen napkin, folded into a precise triangle, completes the ultra-minimalist, luxury setting.
instructions: Preheat oven to 160°C. Line a baking tray with parchment paper. Draw four 8 cm circles on the paper.
For the Dacquoise: Whip egg whites until soft peaks form. Gradually add 50g caster sugar, whip until stiff and glossy.
Gently fold in desiccated coconut, almond flour, and remaining 50g caster sugar.
Pipe or spread the dacquoise mixture into the drawn circles. Bake for 15-20 minutes until golden and crisp. Cool completely.
For the Mousse: Bloom 8g gelatin sheets in cold water for 5 minutes. Drain excess water.
Gently warm 50g mango puree with 50g caster sugar until sugar dissolves. Add bloomed gelatin, stir until dissolved.
Combine remaining mango puree and passion fruit puree with the warm mixture. Chill until slightly thickened.
Whip heavy cream to soft peaks. Gently fold into the chilled mango-passion fruit mixture until smooth.

Assemble the Domes: Pour mousse into silicone half-sphere molds (approx. 7 cm diameter). Place a cooled dacquoise disc on top of each mousse, pressing gently. Freeze for at least 4 hours, preferably overnight.
For the Glaze: Bloom 6g gelatin sheets in cold water for 5 minutes. Drain excess water.
Heat water, glucose syrup, and condensed milk until warm. Do not boil. Remove from heat.

Add white chocolate and bloomed gelatin. Stir until smooth. Add yellow food coloring if desired. Blend with an immersion blender, avoiding air bubbles. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve. Cool glaze to 32-35°C.
Remove frozen mousse domes from molds. Place on a wire rack over a tray.
Pour glaze evenly over each frozen dome, ensuring full coverage. Allow excess glaze to drip off. Carefully transfer domes to a clean plate using an offset spatula.
Garnish: Peel and dice fresh mango into small, precise 5mm cubes. Place a small cluster of mango cubes next to each dome. Add one small mint sprig for color and freshness.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Chicken and Napa Cabbage with Shiitake
recipes.visual_description: Cooked napa cabbage leaves, cut into large wedges, are neatly arranged in a shallow white porcelain bowl. Golden-brown seared chicken thigh chunks are nestled among the cabbage. Sliced rehydrated shiitake mushrooms are interspersed throughout. A glossy, savory brown sauce coats all ingredients, pooling slightly at the bottom. The dish is garnished with thinly sliced green onions, adding a vibrant green contrast. The arrangement is organic and inviting, showcasing the tender textures of the cabbage and chicken. Served on a light wooden table surface, accompanied by a small white rice bowl and a pair of dark wooden chopsticks. A simple gray cotton napkin is folded beside the bowl. Soft, even natural light highlights the dish, emphasizing its rich colors and appetizing textures.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Served with steamed white rice.
instructions: Rehydrate shiitake mushrooms: Place dried mushrooms in a bowl. Cover with hot water. Soak for 30 minutes until soft. Drain, reserving soaking liquid. Remove stems and slice caps.
Prepare chicken: Cut chicken thighs into 3 cm chunks. Season with 5 ml light soy sauce and a pinch of white pepper.
Prepare napa cabbage: Cut napa cabbage into large 5 cm wedges.
Prepare aromatics: Mince garlic and ginger. Thinly slice green onions for garnish.

Cook chicken: Heat vegetable oil in a large wok or pot over medium-high heat. Sear chicken chunks until golden brown on all sides. Remove chicken and set aside. Cook to internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Sauté aromatics: Add minced garlic and ginger to the wok. Stir-fry for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Braise cabbage: Add napa cabbage wedges to the wok. Stir-fry for 2-3 minutes until slightly wilted.
Combine ingredients: Return chicken to the wok. Add sliced shiitake mushrooms, remaining light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, oyster sauce, Shaoxing wine, and chicken broth. Bring to a simmer.
Cook: Cover the wok. Reduce heat to medium-low. Simmer for 10-15 minutes, or until cabbage is tender.
Thicken sauce: In a small bowl, whisk cornstarch with 30 ml water to create a slurry. Stir the slurry into the simmering sauce. Cook for 1-2 minutes until the sauce thickens.
Finish: Remove from heat. Stir in sesame oil. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and white pepper.
Serve: Garnish with thinly sliced green onions.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Pork Belly with Napa Cabbage
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Braised Pork Belly with Napa Cabbage is presented in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl. Three to four substantial, glistening cubes of dark reddish-brown pork belly, their skin tender and rendered, are arranged prominently. The pork is nestled amongst tender, translucent wedges of napa cabbage, which still retain a subtle pale green and white hue. Dark, earthy shiitake mushroom halves are interspersed, adding textural contrast. A rich, savory sauce coats all ingredients. The dish is garnished with a scattering of vibrant green, thinly sliced spring onions. The bowl sits on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a small white porcelain rice bowl filled with fluffy white rice, and a pair of dark wooden chopsticks. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's comforting appeal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately with steamed white rice.
Enjoy with chopsticks, allowing diners to pick up individual pieces of pork, cabbage, and rice.
instructions: Rehydrate shiitake mushrooms in warm water for 30 minutes. Squeeze dry and remove stems. Slice larger caps in half.
Cut pork belly into 3-4 cm cubes. Blanch pork in boiling water for 5 minutes. Drain and rinse thoroughly.
Heat vegetable oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear pork belly cubes until golden on all sides. Remove pork and set aside.
Slice ginger into thick rounds. Smash garlic cloves. Add ginger and garlic to the pot. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Return seared pork belly to the pot. Add Shaoxing wine, light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, rock sugar, star anise, and chicken stock. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 60 minutes, or until pork is tender.

Cut napa cabbage into large wedges. Add napa cabbage and rehydrated shiitake mushrooms to the pot. Continue simmering for another 20-25 minutes, until cabbage is tender and pork reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Stir in sesame oil. Taste and adjust seasoning as needed.
Slice spring onions thinly for garnish. Serve hot.

recipes.recipe_name: Salmon and Smoked Salmon Maki Rolls
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Salmon and Smoked Salmon Maki Rolls is elegantly presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Eight perfectly cut sushi pieces, each approximately 3 cm thick, are arranged in a neat line. The vibrant cross-sections reveal layers of pearly white sushi rice, dark green nori, bright orange fresh salmon batons, pale pink smoked salmon strips, creamy green avocado slices, crisp green cucumber julienne, and vibrant red bell pepper julienne. Textures are distinct and inviting. A small, neat mound of pale pink pickled ginger and a delicate swirl of green wasabi paste sit beside the rolls. A minimalist ceramic dish holds soy sauce. A simple wooden table, natural lighting, and dark wooden chopsticks complete the modern Japanese bistro aesthetic.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with soy sauce for dipping.
Offer pickled ginger (gari) to cleanse the palate between bites.
Provide a small amount of wasabi paste for heat.
instructions: Rinse sushi rice under cold water until water runs clear. Drain well.
Combine rice and water in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low. Cover and cook for 15 minutes.
Remove from heat. Let stand, covered, for 10 minutes. Do not lift lid.
Transfer cooked rice to a large non-metallic bowl. Gently fold in sushi rice vinegar.
Cool rice to room temperature.
Cut fresh salmon into 1 cm x 1 cm x 8 cm batons.
Slice smoked salmon into 1 cm wide strips.
Peel and pit avocado. Slice into 0.5 cm thick strips.
Peel cucumber. Remove seeds. Cut into 0.5 cm x 0.5 cm x 8 cm julienne strips.
Remove seeds from bell pepper. Cut into 0.5 cm x 0.5 cm x 8 cm julienne strips.
Place a nori sheet, shiny side down, on a bamboo sushi mat.
Moisten hands with water. Spread approximately 150 g of rice evenly over the nori, leaving a 2 cm border at the top.
Arrange strips of fresh salmon, smoked salmon, avocado, cucumber, and bell pepper horizontally across the rice, slightly below the center.
Drizzle a thin line of vegan mayonnaise over the fillings.
Lift the edge of the sushi mat. Roll tightly, pressing firmly to compact the ingredients.
Moisten the top border of the nori with water. Seal the roll.
Repeat for remaining nori sheets and fillings.
Slice each roll into 8 equal pieces using a sharp, wet knife.
Arrange rolls on serving plates. Serve immediately with soy sauce, wasabi, and pickled ginger.
notes: Ensure all ingredients are dairy-free, especially the mayonnaise. Use vegan mayonnaise.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Garlic Shrimp Pasta with Broccoli
recipes.visual_description: A single portion is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Linguine is loosely coiled in the center, forming a natural mound. Plump, pink, pan-seared shrimp are arranged casually on top and around the pasta. Vibrant green blanched broccoli florets are interspersed, adding color and texture. A light, glistening garlic-chili oil sauce coats all elements. The dish is garnished with fresh, bright green chopped Italian parsley and fine strips of lemon zest. The plate rests on a simple, light-colored wooden table. A neatly folded, light-grey cotton napkin is to the left. A simple fork with traditional flatware is on the right. The background is a soft, blurred modern bistro ambiance. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, enhancing its natural colors and textures.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread to soak up the sauce.
Offer freshly grated Pecorino Romano or Parmigiano Reggiano cheese on the side.
Pair with a light, dry white wine like Pinot Grigio.
instructions: Cook pasta according to package directions. Reserve 250 ml pasta water. Drain pasta.
Blanch broccoli florets in boiling salted water for 2-3 minutes. Drain. Set aside.
Heat 60 ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add 4 minced garlic cloves and 5 g red pepper flakes. Sauté for 1 minute. Do not brown garlic.
Add 500 g shrimp to the skillet. Cook for 2-3 minutes per side. Shrimp should be pink and opaque.
Pour in 120 ml white wine (if using). Scrape up browned bits from the pan. Simmer for 1 minute.
Add cooked pasta, blanched broccoli, lemon juice, and lemon zest to the skillet. Toss to combine.
Add reserved pasta water gradually. Toss until a light sauce coats the pasta.
Stir in 30 g fresh parsley. Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Serve immediately.
notes: Adjust red pepper flakes to desired spice level.
Ensure shrimp are not overcooked; they cook quickly.

recipes.recipe_name: Berry Custard Tartlets
recipes.visual_description: A single Berry Custard Tartlet sits centered on a simple, round, off-white ceramic plate with natural imperfections, placed on a well-used wooden dining table. The tartlet features a golden-brown, crisp shortcrust pastry shell, approximately 9 cm in diameter. Inside, a smooth, pale yellow vanilla custard is generously spooned, filling the shell to the brim. Neatly arranged on top of the custard are an abundance of fresh, vibrant mixed berries: plump, deep red raspberries, glossy, dark blue blueberries, and bright red strawberry halves. The berries are arranged naturally, creating a burst of color against the creamy custard and golden crust. A subtle sheen from a light apricot glaze covers the fruit. A casually folded beige cloth napkin rests beside the plate. Warm, cozy lighting from kitchen fixtures illuminates the scene, enhancing the inviting, homestyle atmosphere.
instructions: Combine flour, icing sugar, and salt in a bowl. Cut in cold butter until crumbly. Add egg yolk; mix until dough forms. Do not overmix. Wrap dough and chill for 30 minutes.
Preheat oven to 180°C. Roll dough 3 mm thick. Line 4 tartlet molds (8-10 cm diameter). Prick bases with a fork. Line with parchment paper, fill with baking beans. Bake for 15 minutes.
Remove beans and parchment. Bake tartlet shells for 5-7 more minutes until light golden. Cool completely on a wire rack.
Whisk 2 egg yolks, caster sugar, and cornflour in a bowl until smooth.
Heat milk and vanilla extract in a saucepan until simmering. Gradually pour hot milk into egg mixture, whisking constantly.
Return mixture to saucepan. Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, until thickened. Bring to a gentle boil for 1 minute. Remove from heat.
Transfer custard to a bowl. Cover surface with cling film to prevent a skin. Cool completely.
Spoon cooled custard into baked tartlet shells. Arrange mixed berries neatly on top of the custard.
Gently warm apricot jam with a teaspoon of water. Brush over berries for a subtle glaze.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Raspberry-Bacon Chutney
recipes.visual_description: A single pan-seared chicken breast, golden-brown and glistening, is the centerpiece on a clean white porcelain plate. Beside it, a neat pile of crispy roasted potato wedges with a light golden exterior and fluffy interior. Caramelized yellow onion slices, soft and amber-hued, are artfully arranged nearby. A generous spoonful of vibrant, deep red raspberry-bacon chutney, studded with diced bacon, is placed over a portion of the chicken. The dish is garnished with a scattering of fresh green chopped parsley, adding a pop of color and freshness. The overall presentation is balanced and inviting, with moderate negative space. The plate rests on a simple wooden table, accompanied by modern cutlery and a folded cotton napkin.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Toss potato wedges with 15ml olive oil, salt, pepper, and thyme sprigs. Spread on a baking tray. Roast for 30-35 minutes until golden and tender. Flip halfway through.
While potatoes roast, prepare the chutney. In a medium saucepan, cook half the diced bacon over medium heat until crispy. Remove bacon and set aside. Drain most of the rendered fat.
Add one finely diced yellow onion to the saucepan. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute more.

Stir in fresh raspberries, balsamic vinegar, sugar, and chicken stock. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 10-15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until raspberries break down and sauce thickens. Stir in the cooked crispy bacon. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.

Meanwhile, slice the remaining yellow onion thinly. In a separate pan, melt 15g butter with 15ml olive oil over medium-low heat. Add sliced onion. Cook slowly for 20-25 minutes, stirring occasionally, until deeply golden brown and caramelized. Season with salt.
Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and pepper. Heat remaining 15g butter and 15ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering.
Place chicken breasts in the hot skillet. Sear for 5-7 minutes per side, until golden brown and cooked through to an internal temperature of 75°C. Remove chicken from pan and let rest for 5 minutes.

To serve, place a pan-seared chicken breast on each plate. Arrange roasted potato wedges and caramelized onions alongside. Spoon a generous portion of raspberry-bacon chutney over the chicken. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Chicken with Raspberry-Bacon Glaze and Crispy Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate, centrally featuring a golden-brown, roasted chicken thigh with crispy skin. The chicken is whole, unsliced, and glistens with a rich, reddish-brown raspberry-bacon glaze. Around the chicken, golden-hued potato wedges are casually arranged, their skins showing a slight crispness. Pockets of deeply caramelized red onions, a rich reddish-purple, are tucked alongside the chicken and potatoes. The plate is garnished with a scattering of bright red fresh raspberries, offering a vibrant color contrast, alongside the remaining crispy bacon lardons. A delicate sprig of fresh thyme adds a touch of green. The composition is balanced and inviting, with moderate negative space. The dish sits on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by standard silver flatware and a folded white cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and colors, creating an approachable yet refined restaurant-quality presentation. The entire plate is visible, showcasing all elements clearly.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (390°F).
Wash and halve small new potatoes. Toss with 15ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread evenly on a baking tray.
Roast potatoes for 20 minutes.
Slice bacon into 1cm lardons. Cook in a large oven-safe skillet over medium heat until crispy. Remove bacon, drain on paper towel. Reserve 15ml bacon fat in skillet.
Thinly slice red onions. Add to skillet with reserved bacon fat. Cook over medium-low heat for 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until deeply caramelized. Remove onions, set aside.

For the glaze: Combine 100g fresh raspberries, chicken stock, balsamic vinegar, and honey/maple syrup in a small saucepan. Simmer for 5-7 minutes until slightly reduced. Mash raspberries. Strain mixture through a fine-mesh sieve into a clean bowl, pressing solids to extract liquid. Discard solids. Stir in half of the crispy bacon.
Pat chicken thighs dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Increase skillet heat to medium-high. Add remaining 15ml olive oil if needed. Sear chicken, skin-side down, for 5-7 minutes until skin is golden brown and crispy.
Flip chicken. Brush generously with raspberry-bacon glaze.
Transfer skillet to preheated oven. Add caramelized onions to the baking tray with potatoes for the last 15 minutes of potato roasting.
Roast chicken for 15-20 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Brush with more glaze halfway through.
Remove chicken from oven. Let rest 5 minutes.

Plate one chicken thigh per person. Arrange roasted potato wedges and caramelized onions alongside. Drizzle with remaining glaze. Garnish with remaining crispy bacon, fresh raspberries, and a fresh thyme sprig.

recipes.recipe_name: Black and White Tortellini with Smoked Provolone, Crab, and Caviar in Dashi Emulsion
recipes.special_requests: shrimp and provola inside tortelini, crab meat outside ,caviar outside, shrimp oil,3 tortelini on portion,tortilini are 2 colours black and white
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a modern designer plate with a subtle, organic pattern, resting on a polished grey-veined marble surface. Three perfectly formed tortellini, a sophisticated mix of glossy black from squid ink and creamy white, are arranged in an organic cluster. Each tortellini is plump, revealing the delicate pasta texture. A clear, golden dashi emulsion pools elegantly around the tortellini. Delicate mounds of sweet, flaky lump crab meat are artfully positioned alongside. Each tortellini is crowned with a glistening quenelle of premium black caviar, offering striking contrast. A vibrant ruby-red shrimp oil is drizzled sparingly, creating a subtle sheen. Finely sliced bright green chives are scattered precisely. Abundant negative space highlights precision. Traditional flatware rests on a pristine white linen napkin, folded into a precise triangle, completing the minimalist, high-end presentation under dramatic lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with fine dining flatware.
A small, elegant sake cup could be offered as an optional pairing.

ingredients.name: fresh lump crab meat, picked clean

instructions: Prepare Tortellini Dough: Divide flour in half. Make two wells on a clean surface. In one well, add one egg and a pinch of salt. Mix to form white dough. Knead until smooth, about 10 minutes. Wrap and rest 30 minutes. In the second well, add one egg, squid ink, and a pinch of salt. Mix to form black dough. Knead until smooth, about 10 minutes. Wrap and rest 30 minutes.

Make Shrimp Oil: Heat neutral oil in a small saucepan over medium-low heat. Add shrimp heads and shells. Gently simmer for 20-30 minutes until fragrant and oil is infused. Do not brown. Strain oil through a fine-mesh sieve, discarding solids. Set aside.

Prepare Tortellini Filling: Finely mince peeled shrimp. In a bowl, combine minced shrimp, grated smoked provolone, ricotta, chopped chives, and lemon zest. Season with salt and white pepper. Mix gently until just combined.

Form Tortellini: Roll both white and black dough very thin using a pasta machine (to setting 7 or 8). Cut dough into 5 cm squares. Place a small amount (about 5g) of filling in the center of each square. Fold each square into a triangle. Seal edges. Bring the two bottom points of the triangle together and press to form tortellini. Aim for 12 tortellini in total (3 per portion). Arrange on a floured tray.

Prepare Dashi Emulsion: Add water and kombu to a saucepan. Heat gently, do not boil. Remove kombu just before boiling (around 80°C). Bring dashi to a boil, then remove from heat. Add bonito flakes. Let steep for 30 seconds, then strain immediately through a fine-mesh sieve without pressing. Return dashi to clean saucepan. Add sake, mirin, and soy sauce. Bring to a gentle simmer. Whisk in cold butter cubes, one at a time, to create a light emulsion. Keep warm.
Cook Tortellini: Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil. Add tortellini and cook for 3-4 minutes, or until al dente and floating. Carefully remove tortellini with a slotted spoon.

Plate and Serve: Arrange three cooked tortellini (a mix of black and white) in a flowing, artistic composition on each plate. Spoon a generous amount of warm dashi emulsion around the tortellini. Artfully place small mounds of fresh crab meat next to the tortellini. Top each tortellini with a small quenelle of caviar. Drizzle shrimp oil sparingly over the dish. Garnish with finely sliced fresh chives. Serve immediately.
notes: The quality of dashi ingredients (kombu, bonito) is paramount for flavor.
Work quickly when forming tortellini to prevent the dough from drying.
The shrimp oil can be made in advance and stored.

recipes.recipe_name: Mexican Chicken & Bean Skillet
recipes.visual_description: A hearty individual portion of Mexican Chicken and Bean Skillet is presented on a rustic, warm-toned ceramic plate. Golden-brown seared chicken chunks are nestled amidst vibrant red diced tomatoes, tender green bell pepper strips, dark black beans, and diced onions. The dish boasts a rich, savory sauce, lightly thickened, with visible flecks of green cilantro and sliced fresh jalapeños. The textures are varied: firm chicken, soft beans, and slightly yielding vegetables. A sprinkle of fresh chopped cilantro and a bright lime wedge adorn the top. The plate is placed on a well-used wooden dining table, alongside culturally authentic elements: a simple ceramic rice bowl, a stack of warm corn tortillas, and a plain cloth napkin. Warm, cozy kitchen lighting illuminates the scene, highlighting the natural colors and comforting appeal of the home-cooked meal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas for scooping.
Accompany with a side of Mexican rice.
Offer sour cream or crema and guacamole as optional toppings.

ingredients.name: Red bell pepper, sliced into strips
Canned black beans, rinsed and drained

instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 3 cm chunks. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken chunks until golden brown on all sides. Remove chicken from skillet and set aside.
Add diced onion, minced garlic, bell pepper strips, and fresh jalapeño slices to the skillet. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until vegetables soften.
Stir in chili powder, ground cumin, and dried oregano. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in diced tomatoes and chicken broth. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared chicken to the skillet. Add rinsed black beans and sliced pickled jalapeños. Stir to combine.
Reduce heat to medium-low, cover, and simmer for 15-20 minutes, or until chicken is cooked through (internal temperature 75°C).
Taste and adjust seasoning as needed.
Serve hot, garnished with fresh chopped cilantro and lime wedges.

recipes.recipe_name: Risotto ai Fegatini e Funghi Porcini con Basilico
recipes.visual_description: The Risotto ai Fegatini e Funghi Porcini con Basilico is presented in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl. The risotto itself is fluid and creamy, a rich off-white to light-brown hue, naturally spread within the bowl. Irregular 2cm chunks of seared chicken liver, browned and tender, are scattered throughout, providing a dark contrast. Roughly chopped rehydrated porcini mushrooms add earthy texture and depth. A generous scattering of vibrant green fresh basil leaves, some whole, some torn, brightens the dish with color and aroma. A light dusting of finely grated Parmesan cheese may be visible. The bowl rests on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a white cotton napkin and traditional European silver flatware. The setting is a casual bistro with soft, even natural lighting. This is a single, refined individual portion, showcasing the dish's inviting textures and colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately as a primo piatto or main course.
Offer good crusty bread for dipping.
Pair with a glass of the dry white wine used in the recipe.
instructions: Rehydrate porcini: Place dried porcini in 250ml hot water for 20 minutes. Drain, reserving liquid. Squeeze excess water from mushrooms. Roughly chop rehydrated porcini. Strain reserved liquid through a fine-mesh sieve.
Prepare chicken livers: Trim any connective tissue from chicken livers. Pat dry. Cut into irregular 2cm chunks. Season with salt and pepper.

Sauté livers: Heat 15ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken liver chunks until browned on all sides and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C), about 3-4 minutes. Remove livers from pan. Set aside.

Start soffritto: In the same pan, add remaining 15ml olive oil and 20g butter. Add finely diced shallots. Cook until softened, about 3 minutes. Add minced garlic and chopped porcini. Cook for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Toast rice: Add Arborio rice to the pan. Stir constantly for 2 minutes until edges are translucent.
Deglaze: Pour in white wine. Stir until absorbed.

Add liquid: Add strained porcini liquid to the rice. Stir until absorbed. Begin adding hot chicken broth, one ladleful at a time. Stir frequently. Wait for liquid to be almost absorbed before adding the next ladleful. Continue for 18-20 minutes, until rice is al dente and creamy.

Finish risotto (Mantecatura): Remove from heat. Stir in remaining 40g cold butter and grated Parmesan cheese. Stir vigorously until butter and cheese are fully incorporated and risotto is creamy and fluid.
Combine: Gently fold in seared chicken liver chunks and finely chopped basil. Check seasoning.
Serve: Ladle risotto into warm shallow bowls immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Adzuki Bean and Pandan Coconut Layer Cake
recipes.special_requests: the star of the show is the red bean, do something unique inspired by south east asia, dont use typical things like matcha. find what compliments the red bean uniquely.
recipes.visual_description: A single, elegant slice of Adzuki Bean and Pandan Coconut Layer Cake is presented on a simple, round ceramic plate with a natural, slightly off-white glaze. The slice reveals distinct layers: a vibrant, light green pandan sponge cake, a rich reddish-brown adzuki bean paste filling, and a fluffy, bright white coconut cream frosting. The cake layers are evenly cut. A delicate sprinkle of golden-brown toasted shredded coconut adorns the top of the slice. The plate sits on a well-used wooden dining table. In the background, the full, round cake rests on a modest cake stand, showcasing its complete form. A casual cloth napkin and a small bowl of fresh lychees complete the homely Southeast Asian dining scene under warm kitchen lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Served chilled, often accompanied by strong black coffee or jasmine tea.
Enjoyed as a festive dessert for family gatherings and celebrations.
instructions: Rinse adzuki beans. Soak overnight or boil for 10 minutes, then drain.
Place soaked beans and 300 ml water in a pot. Simmer until very tender, about 60-90 minutes. Drain any excess water.
Mash beans with 100 g palm sugar until a coarse paste forms. Set aside to cool.
Preheat oven to 175°C. Grease and flour two 15 cm round cake pans.
Whisk eggs and 150 g palm sugar until pale and thick.
Sift flour and baking powder together. Gently fold into egg mixture.
Combine coconut milk, oil, and pandan extract. Fold into batter until just combined.
Divide batter evenly between prepared pans. Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until a skewer inserted comes out clean. Cool completely on a wire rack.
Scoop thick cream from chilled coconut cream can. Beat with powdered sugar until smooth and fluffy. Do not overmix.
Level cake layers if needed. Spread half of the adzuki bean paste on the first layer. Top with the second cake layer.
Spread remaining adzuki bean paste evenly over the top of the second layer.
Frost the entire cake with coconut cream frosting. Garnish with toasted shredded coconut.
Chill cake for at least 30 minutes before serving.
notes: For best results, chill coconut cream overnight to ensure separation of thick cream.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Ballotine, Seared Veal Medallions, Red Wine Mushroom Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A single portion presented on a pristine white bone china plate. A golden-brown seared veal medallion rests off-center. Next to it, two or three thick rounds of chicken ballotine, revealing a delicate mushroom and herb stuffing, are artfully arranged, slightly overlapping. A generous, organically shaped spoonful of earthy mushroom ragout is placed nearby. The plate is adorned with a rich, glossy dark red wine mushroom jus, spooned elegantly around the meats, creating a flowing pool. A delicate sprig of fresh thyme or chervil garnishes the sauce. Abundant negative space surrounds the composition. The setting features a luxurious white Carrara marble surface, traditional French silver flatware, and a precisely folded white linen napkin, all under dramatic professional lighting with soft shadows. The background is ultra-minimalist, emphasizing the dish's refined presentation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a crusty baguette to sop up the exquisite sauce.
A simple green salad with a light vinaigrette provides a fresh counterpoint.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C.
Butterfly chicken breasts. Pound gently to even thickness. Season with salt and pepper.

Finely dice 1 shallot, 1 garlic clove, 50g mushrooms, and 5g parsley. Sauté mixture in 5g butter until moisture evaporates. Cool completely. Spread evenly over chicken breasts. Roll chicken tightly into a cylindrical shape. Secure with butcher's twine. Season outside of ballotines.

Heat 15ml olive oil in an oven-safe pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken ballotines 3 minutes per side until golden brown. Transfer pan to preheated oven. Cook 15-20 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove from oven. Rest 5 minutes. Remove twine. Slice into thick rounds.
Season veal medallions with salt and pepper.

Heat 15ml olive oil and 10g butter in a clean pan over medium-high heat. Sear veal medallions 2-3 minutes per side for medium-rare. Adjust cooking time for desired doneness. Remove veal from pan. Rest.

For the sauce, add 10g butter to the pan used for veal. Sauté remaining minced shallot and garlic for 1 minute. Deglaze pan with red wine. Reduce by half. Add veal stock and 2 thyme sprigs. Simmer. Reduce sauce by two-thirds until it coats the back of a spoon (nappe consistency).

Strain sauce through a fine-mesh sieve into a clean saucepan. Discard solids. Return sauce to low heat. Whisk in 20g cold butter. Stir in 50ml heavy cream, if using, for added richness. Season sauce with salt and pepper to taste. Keep warm.
For mushroom ragout, dice remaining mushrooms. Heat 15g butter in a small pan. Sauté mushrooms until tender and browned. Season with salt, pepper, and remaining chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Veal Medallions and Chicken Supreme, Red Wine Mushroom Jus
recipes.visual_description: Seared chicken supreme with crispy, golden-brown skin, cut into two thick, diagonal pieces, is nestled against a perfectly seared veal medallion with a slight pink center. A rich, glossy red wine mushroom jus, studded with tender, browned shiitake and oyster mushroom slices, pools elegantly around the meats and flows artistically across the plate. A single, vibrant green sprig of fresh thyme or a sprinkle of finely chopped parsley provides a precise pop of color. The dish is presented on an expensive bone china plate with a subtle pattern, resting on a polished dark wood table. A pristine white linen napkin, folded into a precise triangle, and traditional European flatware are impeccably arranged. Abundant negative space and dramatic professional lighting enhance the luxurious, minimalist setting, highlighting the culinary art.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of creamy Pomme Purée or a delicate Parsnip Purée.
Pair with a glass of the same dry red wine used in the jus.
instructions: Pat chicken supremes dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a large oven-safe pan over medium-high heat. Place chicken skin-side down. Sear until skin is golden and crispy, about 8-10 minutes. Flip chicken.
Transfer pan to a preheated oven at 180°C. Roast for 15-20 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Rest chicken on a cutting board, tented with foil.
While chicken roasts, pat veal medallions dry. Season with salt and pepper.
In a clean pan, heat 15ml olive oil and 15g butter over medium-high heat. Sear veal medallions for 2-3 minutes per side for medium-rare. Remove veal from pan. Rest alongside chicken.

In the same pan used for veal, add 15g butter. Add diced shallots. Sauté until softened, about 2-3 minutes. Add minced garlic and sliced mushrooms. Sauté until mushrooms are tender and lightly browned, about 5-7 minutes.
Pour red wine into the pan. Scrape up any browned bits. Bring to a simmer. Reduce wine by half, about 5 minutes.
Pour in veal stock and add thyme sprigs. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Simmer gently until sauce thickens slightly and coats the back of a spoon, about 10-15 minutes. Remove thyme sprigs.
Whisk in remaining 30g cold butter, a cube at a time, off the heat, to emulsify and create a glossy sauce. Season with salt and pepper.

Slice each chicken supreme into two thick, diagonal pieces. Plate one chicken piece and one veal medallion per serving. Spoon generous amount of red wine mushroom jus over and around the meats. Garnish with chopped fresh parsley.
traditional_techniques: Monter au Beurre (finishing sauce with butter)

recipes.recipe_name: Adzuki Matcha Entremet
recipes.visual_description: A single, precisely cut slice of Adzuki Matcha Entremet stands elegantly on a pristine white porcelain dessert plate with a delicate gold rim. The slice, approximately 2 cm thick, reveals its intricate layers: a pale green Matcha Dacquoise base, a thin, dark brown Crispy Sesame Praline, a creamy, light purple-brown Adzuki Bean Mousse, a vibrant Matcha White Chocolate Ganache insert, and a final Dacquoise layer. The entire slice is coated in a glossy, dark chocolate mirror glaze. Abundant negative space surrounds the slice. A single edible gold leaf and two vibrant fresh raspberries artfully garnish the plate. The setting features a pristine white marble surface with dramatic, professional lighting and subtle shadows. A minimalist background, an elegant dessert fork, and a traditional Japanese green tea cup complete this sophisticated haute patisserie presentation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a small cup of freshly brewed matcha tea.
Enjoy with a delicate dessert fork.
Present on individual, elegant ceramic plates.
instructions: Prepare Adzuki Bean Paste (Anko): Rinse adzuki beans. Place in a pot with water, bring to boil, drain. Repeat twice to remove bitterness. Add 300 mL fresh water, simmer 1 hour until tender. Add sugar, cook 15 minutes, stirring until thick. Mash slightly. Cool completely.

Prepare Matcha Dacquoise: Preheat oven to 170°C. Sift almond flour, icing sugar, and matcha powder. Whip egg whites with granulated sugar to stiff peaks. Gently fold dry ingredients into meringue. Spread batter thinly onto a baking sheet lined with parchment paper, forming a rectangle (approx. 15x20 cm). Bake 12-15 minutes until lightly golden. Cool. Cut into two 8x18 cm rectangles.
Prepare Crispy Sesame Praline Layer: Melt white chocolate. Stir in sesame paste. Fold in feuilletine. Spread mixture onto one dacquoise rectangle. Place in freezer to set.

Prepare Matcha White Chocolate Ganache Insert: Hydrate gelatin in cold water. Heat cream until simmering. Remove from heat. Whisk in matcha powder until smooth. Pour hot cream over white chocolate, let sit 1 minute. Stir until smooth ganache forms. Squeeze excess water from gelatin, stir into hot ganache until dissolved. Pour into an 8x18 cm mold (or form using parchment paper on a tray), ensuring it's thinner than the dacquoise. Freeze until solid.

Prepare Adzuki Bean Mousse: Hydrate gelatin in cold water. Gently warm 50 g of prepared adzuki bean paste. Squeeze excess water from gelatin, stir into warm adzuki paste until dissolved. Fold in remaining adzuki paste. Whip heavy cream to soft peaks. Gently fold adzuki mixture into whipped cream.

Assemble the Entremet: Line a 10x20 cm rectangular mold with acetate or plastic wrap. Place the dacquoise with crispy sesame layer at the bottom. Pour half of the adzuki bean mousse over it. Gently place the frozen matcha ganache insert on top of the mousse. Cover with remaining adzuki bean mousse. Top with the second dacquoise layer. Freeze minimum 6 hours, preferably overnight.

Prepare Dark Chocolate Mirror Glaze: Hydrate gelatin in cold water. In a saucepan, combine sugar, water, and glucose syrup. Bring to 103°C. Remove from heat. Add cream. Pour mixture over dark chocolate. Add squeezed gelatin. Emulsify with an immersion blender, avoiding air bubbles. Strain glaze. Cool to 32-35°C.

Glaze and Garnish: Remove entremet from freezer. Unmold onto a wire rack placed over a tray. Pour glaze evenly over the frozen entremet, ensuring full coverage. Let excess drip. Carefully transfer entremet to a serving board or plate. Decorate with edible gold leaf and fresh raspberries.
Serve: Allow entremet to thaw in refrigerator for 2-3 hours before serving. Slice carefully with a hot, sharp knife.
notes: Ensure all ingredients are at specified temperatures for best results.
Precision in measurements and temperatures is crucial for entremet construction.
When folding ingredients, be gentle to maintain aeration.

recipes.recipe_name: Tortellini di Granchio e Gamberi con Consommé al Parmigiano e Dashi, Mousse di Parmigiano e Oli Aromatici
recipes.special_requests: Italian cuisine, Shrimp oil, basil oil, parmesan mousse,  3 Tortelini on portion
recipes.visual_description: Three perfectly formed, pale yellow tortellini, filled with succulent crab and finely diced shrimp, are gracefully arranged at the center of a wide-rimmed bone china plate. A pristine, golden consommé, infused with umami dashi and savory Parmesan, is meticulously poured around the tortellini, creating a shallow, reflective pool. A delicate quenelle of airy Parmesan mousse is placed beside the tortellini, adding cloud-like texture. Artful swirls of vibrant emerald basil oil and deep orange shrimp oil are precisely drizzled over the consommé, offering striking color contrast. A single, perfectly seared small shrimp and delicate microgreens provide a final touch. The dish rests on a premium white Carrara marble surface, flanked by elegant silver flatware and a folded white linen napkin. Dramatic lighting highlights the architectural precision against an ultra-minimalist background, embodying refined Italian artistry.

ingredients.name: Shrimp, peeled and deveined
ingredients.quantity: 250 g (200g for oil, 50g for filling, 4 small for garnish)

instructions: Prepare Shrimp Oil: Peel 200g shrimp. Reserve shrimp. Sauté shrimp shells with 2 sliced garlic cloves in 150ml neutral oil over low heat for 20 minutes. Strain oil through a fine sieve. Discard shells.

Prepare Basil Oil: Blanch 50g fresh basil leaves in boiling water for 10 seconds. Immediately transfer to ice bath. Squeeze excess water. Blend blanched basil with 100ml neutral oil until smooth. Strain through a fine sieve or cheesecloth. Reserve oil.

Prepare Dashi-Parmesan Consommé: Add 1L water and 10g kombu to a pot. Heat gently to 60°C. Remove kombu before water boils. Add 15g katsuobushi. Simmer for 30 seconds. Strain through a fine sieve. Return dashi to pot. Add 50g Parmesan rind. Simmer for 15 minutes. Strain consommé. Season with salt. Keep warm.

Prepare Parmesan Mousse: Heat 150ml heavy cream with 70g grated Parmesan and 1/2 tsp agar-agar in a saucepan. Stir until Parmesan melts and agar-agar dissolves. Season with a pinch of salt. Pour mixture into a siphon. Charge with N2O. Keep warm.

Prepare Tortellini Filling: Finely dice 50g cooked shrimp. In a bowl, combine 200g fresh crab meat, diced shrimp, 50g ricotta, 30g grated Parmesan, 1 tbsp chopped chives, and lemon zest. Season with salt and pepper. Mix gently.

Prepare Pasta Dough: On a clean surface, create a well with 200g '00' flour. Crack 2 eggs into the well. Gradually incorporate flour into eggs to form a dough. Knead for 10 minutes until smooth and elastic. Cover and rest for 30 minutes.

Form Tortellini: Roll pasta dough very thinly, either by hand or with a pasta machine. Cut dough into 5cm squares. Place a small amount of filling in the center of each square. Fold into a triangle, seal edges. Bring two points of the triangle together and pinch to form tortellini. Aim for 3 tortellini per portion, total 12 pieces.
Cook Tortellini: Bring a large pot of salted water to a gentle boil. Cook tortellini for 2-3 minutes until al dente. Drain well.
Sear Garnish Shrimp: Quickly sear the remaining 4 small shrimp in a hot pan until just cooked through. Season lightly.

Plate the Dish: Arrange 3 cooked tortellini gracefully at the center of each wide-rimmed bone china plate. Ladle the warm Dashi-Parmesan Consommé around the tortellini, creating a shallow pool. Dispense a delicate quenelle of Parmesan mousse next to the tortellini. Drizzle artful swirls of basil oil and shrimp oil over the consommé. Place one seared shrimp beside the tortellini. Garnish with a few delicate microgreens.
notes: This dish is a modern Italian interpretation, incorporating Japanese dashi for an umami-rich consommé. This fusion element elevates the classic Italian tortellini to a fine-dining experience.

recipes.recipe_name: Molten Chocolate Oat Lava Cakes
recipes.visual_description: A single Molten Chocolate Oat Lava Cake is centrally plated on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The cake, a rich dark brown, stands as a small, slightly domed cylinder with a delicate, set crust. A gentle pierce reveals a glossy, warm, flowing molten chocolate interior. A light dusting of unsweetened cocoa powder adorns the top. The plate maintains moderate negative space, enhancing the cake's prominence. The setting is a modern bistro: a simple wooden table surface, a white cotton napkin, and a polished dessert fork and spoon are positioned beside the plate. Natural, even lighting highlights the cake's textures and deep chocolate hues against a softly blurred, casual restaurant background.

ingredients.name: Cocoa powder (for dusting ramekins and garnish)

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Butter four 175 ml ramekins. Dust generously with cocoa powder.
Melt chocolate and 120 g butter in a heatproof bowl over simmering water. Stir until smooth. Remove from heat.
In a separate bowl, whisk whole eggs, egg yolks, sugar, and vanilla extract until pale and thick.
Fold melted chocolate mixture into egg mixture.
Sift 20 g cocoa powder, oat flour, all-purpose flour, and salt into the chocolate mixture. Gently fold until just combined. Do not overmix.
Divide batter evenly among prepared ramekins.
Bake 12-14 minutes. Edges should be set, center still wobbly.
Remove from oven. Let rest 1 minute.
Invert each cake onto a clean white porcelain plate.
Dust lightly with cocoa powder. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Honey-Almond Yogurt Tartlets with Berry Compote
recipes.visual_description: Four individual tartlets are presented on handcrafted ceramic plates in earth tones. Each tartlet features a golden-brown, rustic almond flour crust, cradling a smooth, creamy white Greek yogurt and honey filling. The filling is perfectly set, offering a gentle, inviting sheen. On top, a vibrant, rich berry compote, showcasing the natural colors of seasonal mixed berries (strawberries, blueberries, raspberries), is generously spooned. The berries are gently cooked, retaining some texture. A scattering of finely chopped toasted almond slivers and a small, fresh mint leaf garnish the compote, providing contrasting color and texture. The tartlets are arranged with ample negative space on a light reclaimed wood surface. The setting includes a simple, undyed linen napkin and perhaps a small sprig of foraged greenery in the background, all bathed in soft, natural lighting. The overall presentation is clean, natural, and highlights the wholesome ingredients and eco-conscious preparation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple herbal tea.
Present on a shared platter for a communal dessert experience.
instructions: Combine almond flour, all-purpose flour, icing sugar, and salt in a bowl.
Add cold butter. Rub in butter until mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Add egg yolk. Mix until dough forms. Do not overmix.
Wrap dough. Chill for 30 minutes.
Preheat oven to 180°C.
Roll dough to 3 mm thickness. Cut out circles to fit 4 individual tartlet molds (approx. 10 cm diameter).
Press dough into molds. Prick bottoms with a fork.
Line with parchment paper, fill with baking beans. Blind bake for 15 minutes.
Remove beans and paper. Bake for another 5-7 minutes, until golden. Cool completely.
Combine berries, honey/maple syrup, lemon zest, and water in a small saucepan.
Simmer over medium heat for 5-7 minutes, until berries soften and sauce thickens slightly.
Mash lightly with a fork if desired. Cool completely.
In a small saucepan, whisk agar-agar powder with water. Bring to a boil, stir for 1 minute until dissolved. Remove from heat.
In a separate bowl, whisk Greek yogurt, honey, and vanilla extract until smooth.
Gradually whisk in the warm agar-agar solution.
Pour the honey-yogurt filling into the cooled tartlet shells. Refrigerate for at least 2 hours, or until set.
Just before serving, spoon berry compote over each tartlet. Garnish with fresh mint leaves or toasted almond slivers.
notes: Use local, seasonal berries for the compote to enhance sustainability.
Any leftover berry compote can be stored and used for breakfast or other desserts.
Almond flour can be sourced from producers who utilize almond pulp from almond milk production, minimizing waste.

recipes.recipe_name: Mixed Berry and Almond Crumble with Honey Yogurt
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of warm Mixed Berry and Almond Crumble is presented in a classic round ceramic ramekin. The crumble topping is a rich golden brown, showcasing rustic textures from rolled oats and finely ground almonds, with some irregular, slightly darker patches from baking. Beneath, the vibrant deep reds and purples of the mixed raspberries, cranberries, and blueberries peek through, visibly bubbling with sweet juices around the edges. A generous, creamy white dollop of honey yogurt rests gracefully on one side of the crumble, its smooth surface contrasting with the rough texture of the topping. The ramekin sits on a well-used, light-toned wooden dining table, accompanied by a simple, polished metal spoon. A casually folded, plain linen napkin is placed nearby, completing a homely, comforting scene under warm, inviting kitchen lighting.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C.
Combine mixed berries and 60g honey in a medium bowl. Stir gently.
Divide berry mixture evenly among four individual oven-safe ramekins (approx. 200ml capacity) or a single 20cm diameter baking dish.
In a separate bowl, combine almond flour, rolled oats, 50g granulated sugar, and a pinch of salt.
Add cold, diced butter to the dry crumble ingredients. Use fingertips to rub butter into dry ingredients until a coarse, crumbly mixture forms.
Sprinkle crumble mixture evenly over the berries in the ramekins or baking dish.
Bake for 25-30 minutes. Crumble should be golden brown. Berries should be bubbling.
While crumble bakes, mix plain yogurt with remaining 30g honey until well combined.
Remove crumble from oven. Let cool slightly.
Serve warm with a generous dollop of honey yogurt.

recipes.recipe_name: Beef Bourguignon
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Beef Bourguignon is served in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl. The centerpiece features four to five large, succulent chunks of braised beef chuck, glistening with a deep, mahogany-colored glossy sauce. Interspersed among the meat are whole, tender pearl onions and golden-brown sautéed button mushroom halves. Bright orange carrot rounds provide a pop of color. The stew is finished with a sprinkle of finely chopped fresh parsley. The sauce has a rich, velvety consistency, pooling slightly around the base. The dish sits on a dark wood bistro table. A side of crusty baguette slices and a simple silver spoon rest on a white cotton napkin nearby.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty French baguette
Pair with a glass of Pinot Noir or red Burgundy
Traditionally served with buttery mashed potatoes or boiled potatoes
instructions: Pat beef chunks dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Sauté bacon lardons in a heavy pot until crisp. Remove and set aside.
Sear beef chunks in the bacon fat over high heat until browned on all sides. Remove beef.
Add sliced carrots and onions to the pot. Sauté for 5 minutes.
Stir in tomato paste and flour. Cook for 2 minutes.
Pour in red wine. Scrape the bottom of the pot to release browned bits.
Return beef and bacon to the pot. Add beef stock and bouquet garni.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 2.5 hours until meat is tender.
Sauté mushrooms and pearl onions in butter in a separate pan until golden.
Add mushrooms and pearl onions to the stew. Simmer for 15 minutes.
Remove bouquet garni. Season to taste.
Garnish with chopped parsley before serving.
notes: Ensure the beef is patted dry before searing to achieve a deep crust.
Use a high-quality dry red wine for the most authentic flavor profile.
The sauce should be thick enough to coat the back of a spoon.

recipes.recipe_name: Consommé de Volaille Clarifié, Tomate et Pomme de Terre
recipes.visual_description: A pristine white bone china bowl holds a single serving of refined Consommé de Volaille. The liquid is crystal clear, a delicate golden amber, reflecting light with elegant transparency. At the base of the bowl, a meticulously arranged cluster of shredded chicken confit, its tender strands a light ivory. Nestled beside it are vibrant red tomato concasse cubes, each a precise 5mm, offering a pop of color and soft texture. Interspersed are minute, pearly white potato brunoise cubes, precisely 2mm, adding subtle structure. A shimmering drizzle of lemon-garlic oil creates an iridescent swirl on the consommé's surface. A few delicate microgreens, such as chervil or sorrel, are artfully placed atop the chicken and vegetables, providing a fresh green contrast. The bowl sits on a polished superpremium grey veined marble surface. A pristine white linen napkin, folded into a precise triangle, rests to the side. A silver soup spoon is elegantly placed. The background is ultra-minimalist, emphasizing negative space and dramatic professional lighting with subtle shadows.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Served with a delicate cheese gougère
instructions: Prepare Chicken Stock: Place chicken bones, 1 roughly chopped onion, 1 chopped carrot, 1 chopped celery stalk, 2 crushed garlic cloves, bay leaf, thyme sprigs, and white peppercorns in a large pot. Cover with 3 litres cold water. Bring to a gentle simmer. Skim impurities. Cook for 3 hours, maintaining a bare simmer. Strain stock through a fine-mesh sieve. Discard solids.

Make Chicken Confit: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt. Place thighs and 4 peeled garlic cloves in a small oven-safe dish. Cover with olive oil. Ensure chicken is fully submerged. Bake at 140°C (285°F) for 2.5-3 hours, until very tender. Let cool in oil. Shred chicken meat once cool enough to handle. Reserve confit oil.

Clarify Consommé: Chill chicken stock completely. In a large pot, combine cold stock with 1 finely diced onion, 1 finely diced carrot, 1 finely diced celery stalk, and 3 whisked egg whites. Stir well. Place over medium heat. Slowly bring to a simmer, stirring occasionally. Stop stirring once raft forms. Create a small hole in the raft for steam to escape. Simmer gently for 45-60 minutes without disturbing.
Strain Consommé: Carefully ladle consommé through a cheesecloth-lined sieve without disturbing the raft. Discard raft and solids. Season consommé with salt to taste. Keep warm.
Prepare Tomato Concasse: Blanch tomatoes in boiling water for 30 seconds. Plunge into ice water. Peel skins. Halve tomatoes, remove seeds. Dice tomato flesh into small 5 mm cubes (concasse).
Prepare Potato Brunoise: Peel potato. Cut into 2 mm x 2 mm x 2 mm cubes (brunoise). Blanch potato brunoise in salted boiling water for 2-3 minutes until tender. Drain well.
Make Lemon-Garlic Oil: Finely grate lemon zest. Mince 1 confit garlic clove. Combine 30 ml reserved confit oil with lemon zest and minced garlic.

Assemble and Serve: Gently warm shredded confit chicken, tomato concasse, and potato brunoise. Divide evenly among four warm shallow bowls. Ladle hot, clear consommé around the components. Drizzle a small amount of lemon-garlic oil over each serving. Garnish with microgreens.

recipes.recipe_name: Spiced Chickpea & Fermented Red Cabbage Braise with Matcha Rice
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented in a handcrafted, earthy-toned ceramic bowl. A mound of vibrant green matcha-infused basmati rice sits slightly off-center, its individual grains distinct and fluffy. Adjacent to the rice, a generous portion of the rich, rustic chickpea and fermented red cabbage braise is spooned. The braise showcases tender, whole chickpeas in a savory, reddish-brown sauce, with soft, deep purple chunks of roughly chopped fermented red cabbage interspersed. A creamy, bright white chili yogurt is drizzled artfully over the braise, offering a contrasting swirl. The entire composition is garnished with a sprinkle of fresh, bright green chopped coriander and delicate strands of lemon zest, adding freshness and aroma. The scene is set on a light reclaimed wood table, with a simple undyed linen napkin and a rustic wooden spoon, bathed in soft, natural light.

ingredients.name: Red Chili
ingredients.quantity: 1, deseeded and finely chopped (or 1/2 tsp chili flakes)

instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add diced onion. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Stir in minced garlic, grated ginger, and chopped red chili. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add tomato paste, cumin powder, coriander powder, and turmeric powder. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Add drained chickpeas and roughly chopped fermented red cabbage. Pour in vegetable broth. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 15-20 minutes. Stir occasionally.
Remove lid. Stir in lemon juice and lemon zest. Season with salt and black pepper to taste. Keep warm.
While braise simmers, combine rinsed basmati rice, water, and salt in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low. Cover tightly. Simmer for 12-15 minutes, until water is absorbed.
Remove rice from heat. Gently stir in matcha green tea powder. Fluff with a fork. Keep covered for 5 minutes.
In a small bowl, whisk together plain yogurt, lemon juice, red chili flakes, and salt.
Ladle matcha rice into serving bowls. Spoon the chickpea and red cabbage braise alongside or over the rice. Drizzle with chili yogurt. Garnish with fresh coriander/mint and extra lemon zest.
notes: To quick-pickle red cabbage: Thinly slice 200g red cabbage. Place in a bowl with 1 tsp salt, 60ml white vinegar, and 1 tsp sugar. Massage for 2-3 minutes. Let sit for 30 minutes before using if pre-fermented cabbage is not available.

recipes.recipe_name: Sustainable Chickpea & Fermented Cabbage Bowl with Matcha-Ginger Dressing
recipes.visual_description: A single serving in a handcrafted ceramic bowl, cream tone, on a light reclaimed wood surface. Thinly sliced fresh red cabbage forms a crisp purple base. Golden-brown roasted chickpeas, with crispy exteriors, are piled alongside ruby-red fermented red cabbage, creating strong visual contrast. A generous, pale green matcha-ginger yogurt dressing drizzles over. Garnish: bright lemon zest and fresh black pepper. The presentation is natural, minimalist. An undyed linen napkin in natural beige is subtly placed. Soft natural lighting highlights colors and textures against a clean background, completing the sustainable aesthetic.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of whole grain flatbread or crusty sourdough bread for a complete meal.
Enjoy as a light yet satisfying lunch or dinner.
instructions: Prepare Fermented Red Cabbage: Thinly slice 300 g of red cabbage. Place in a bowl. Add 5 g salt. Massage cabbage for 5 minutes until it releases liquid. Pack tightly into a clean jar. Cover with its own liquid. If needed, add a little water to fully submerge. Seal loosely. Let ferment at room temperature for 1-2 days, then refrigerate.

Roast Chickpeas: Preheat oven to 200°C. Drain and rinse chickpeas. Pat dry thoroughly. Toss with 30 ml olive oil, 10 g grated ginger, and a pinch of salt and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet. Roast for 20-25 minutes, until golden and slightly crispy. Shake sheet halfway through.

Prepare Matcha-Ginger Yogurt Dressing: In a small bowl, combine yogurt, 5 g matcha powder, 10 g grated ginger, juice of half a lemon, 30 ml olive oil, and 5 ml maple syrup (if using). Whisk until smooth. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Prepare Fresh Cabbage: Thinly slice remaining 200 g red cabbage. Set aside.

Assemble Bowls: Divide fresh red cabbage among four serving bowls. Top with fermented red cabbage and roasted chickpeas. Drizzle generously with matcha-ginger yogurt dressing. Garnish with lemon zest and a sprinkle of fresh black pepper.
notes: For lacto-fermented red cabbage, allow 5-7 days for fermentation. This recipe uses a quick ferment for faster preparation.
Adjust ginger and lemon quantities in the dressing to suit personal preference.

recipes.recipe_name: Matcha Chickpea Patties with Pickled Cabbage and Ginger Yogurt
recipes.visual_description: Two golden-brown, round matcha chickpea patties are stacked slightly overlapping on a pristine white porcelain plate, positioned centrally. Each patty is topped with a vibrant mound of thinly sliced, bright purple pickled red cabbage, offering a sharp visual contrast. A creamy, off-white ginger yogurt sauce is artfully drizzled over the patties and cabbage, with some pooling delicately at the plate's base. Fresh, bright green mint leaves are scattered lightly over the dish, adding a final touch of color and freshness. The patties have a crisp exterior and a tender, earthy green interior from the matcha. The arrangement is balanced, allowing for moderate negative space around the food. The plate rests on a simple light wooden table in a modern bistro setting, accompanied by a neatly folded grey cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and inviting colors.

ingredients.name: Fresh mint or coriander, chopped, for garnish

instructions: Prepare pickled cabbage: Thinly slice red cabbage. In a bowl, combine cabbage with apple cider vinegar, sugar, and a pinch of salt. Mix well. Set aside to pickle for at least 15 minutes.
Prepare ginger yogurt: Grate fresh ginger. In a separate bowl, mix plain yogurt with grated ginger, lime juice, and a pinch of salt. Stir until smooth. Refrigerate until serving.
Make chickpea patty mixture: Drain and rinse chickpeas thoroughly. In a large bowl, mash chickpeas roughly with a fork or potato masher. Leave some texture.
Sauté aromatics: Heat 15ml of vegetable oil in a pan over medium heat. Add finely diced onion and minced garlic. Sauté for 3-4 minutes until softened and fragrant. Remove from heat.

Combine patty ingredients: Add the sautéed onion and garlic to the mashed chickpeas. Stir in matcha green tea powder, grated ginger (for patties), plain flour, ground cumin, ground coriander, salt, and black pepper. Mix thoroughly until well combined.
Form patties: Divide the mixture into 8 equal portions. Shape each portion into a flat, round patty, approximately 2cm thick.

Cook patties: Heat the remaining 45ml of vegetable oil in a large non-stick pan over medium heat. Once hot, carefully place the patties in the pan. Do not overcrowd. Cook for 4-5 minutes per side, until golden brown and heated through.

Plate and serve: Arrange two hot matcha chickpea patties on each plate. Top generously with the pickled red cabbage. Drizzle the ginger yogurt sauce over the patties and cabbage. Garnish with chopped fresh mint or coriander. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Pastelón de Berenjena
recipes.visual_description: A single rectangular portion of Pastelón de Berenjena is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The dish shows distinct layers: golden-brown baked eggplant planks, a rich, reddish-brown ground beef filling infused with annatto, and a bubbly, golden-edged melted mozzarella cheese topping. The eggplant layers are visibly tender, and the beef filling has a rustic texture. A sprinkle of fresh, vibrant green chopped cilantro garnishes the top, adding a pop of color. The plate sits on a simple wooden table surface, beside a folded cotton napkin and traditional flatware. The background is a subtly blurred, casual restaurant setting, lit with natural, even lighting, creating an inviting and authentic scene. The overall presentation is clean and professional, focusing on the dish's comforting, layered appearance.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of white rice (arroz blanco) or a simple green salad.
Offer a bottle of pique (Puerto Rican hot sauce) on the side for those who enjoy extra heat.
instructions: Slice eggplant lengthwise into 5 mm thick planks. Place on paper towels, sprinkle with salt. Let sit 30 minutes to draw out moisture. Pat dry.
Heat 30 ml olive oil in a pan over medium heat. Fry eggplant slices in batches until golden brown. Drain on paper towels. Alternatively, bake at 200°C for 15-20 minutes until tender.
To make annatto oil: Heat remaining 30 ml olive oil and annatto seeds in a small saucepan over low heat for 5 minutes. Seeds should not burn. Strain oil, discard seeds. Set aside.
In a large skillet, brown ground beef over medium-high heat. Break apart with a spoon. Drain excess fat.
Add diced onion, minced garlic, and diced green bell pepper to the beef. Cook 5-7 minutes until vegetables soften.
Stir in annatto oil, dried oregano, ground cumin, tomato sauce, salt, and pepper. Simmer 10 minutes, allowing flavors to meld. Remove from heat.
Preheat oven to 190°C. Lightly grease a 23x33 cm baking dish.
Arrange a layer of fried eggplant slices at the bottom of the baking dish. Overlap slightly.
Spread half of the beef mixture over the eggplant layer. Sprinkle with one-third of the mozzarella cheese.
Add another layer of eggplant slices. Top with the remaining beef mixture. Sprinkle with another one-third of the mozzarella cheese.
Finish with a final layer of eggplant slices. Top with the remaining mozzarella cheese.
Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until cheese is melted and bubbly and pastelón is heated through. Let rest 10 minutes before serving.
Garnish with fresh chopped cilantro.
notes: Salting the eggplant draws out moisture, preventing a soggy pastelón.
Annatto oil provides authentic color and subtle flavor; adjust quantity to preference.

recipes.recipe_name: Beef Tenderloin with Bitter Chocolate-Coffee Glaze, Celeriac Puree, and Glazed Carrots
recipes.visual_description: A single, perfectly seared beef tenderloin chunk, medium-rare, exhibiting a rich, caramelized crust. It rests alongside a flowing, creamy celeriac puree, its pale beige color providing a soft contrast. Two to three vibrant, glossy glazed carrot batons, cut into precise 6cm batons, are artfully positioned. A dark, intensely glistening bitter chocolate-coffee glaze is meticulously spooned around the beef and partially under the puree, creating dynamic lines and a sophisticated sheen. A delicate scattering of finely snipped chives adds a fresh green accent atop the beef. The dish is presented on an elegant, off-white bone china plate with a subtle, modern pattern. The setting features a premium dark wooden table, with a pristine white linen napkin folded precisely. Dramatic professional lighting casts soft shadows, highlighting textures against a minimalist background with abundant negative space.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Pat beef tenderloin portions dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat 15ml olive oil and 20g butter in an oven-safe pan over high heat. Sear beef portions 2-3 minutes per side until deeply browned.
Transfer pan to preheated oven. Roast 8-10 minutes for medium-rare (internal temperature 55-57°C). Remove from oven. Rest beef on a warm plate, covered, for 10 minutes.
In the same pan, add diced shallots. Sauté 2 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic and sauté 1 minute.
Pour in red wine. Bring to a simmer. Reduce by half.
Add beef stock and espresso. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to medium-low. Simmer 5-7 minutes until slightly thickened.
Remove pan from heat. Stir in chopped dark chocolate until melted and smooth. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.
Peel and dice celeriac into 2cm cubes. Place in a saucepan. Cover with cold salted water. Bring to a boil. Cook 15-20 minutes until very tender.
Drain celeriac well. Return to saucepan. Add 100ml heavy cream and 20g butter. Mash thoroughly or blend until very smooth. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.
Place carrot batons in a small saucepan. Add 20g butter, 5g sugar, and 60ml water. Bring to a simmer over medium heat.
Cook 8-10 minutes, shaking pan occasionally, until water evaporates and carrots are tender and glossy. Season with salt.

Place a portion of celeriac puree on each plate. Position a rested beef tenderloin chunk beside the puree. Artfully arrange 2-3 glazed carrot batons. Spoon chocolate-coffee glaze around the beef and puree. Garnish with finely snipped chives.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Mushroom-Bacon Cream Sauce, Roasted Cauliflower, and Garlic Mash
recipes.visual_description: A single portion is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate. A generous dollop of smooth, creamy garlic potato mash anchors one side. Adjacent, golden-brown roasted cauliflower florets are arranged artfully, showing their slight caramelization. A pan-seared chicken breast, cooked to a perfect golden-crusted exterior and presented whole (or sliced into two thick medallions), rests beside the mash. The chicken is generously draped with a rich, glossy mushroom-bacon cream sauce, flecked with tender sliced mushrooms and crispy bacon bits. A sprinkle of vibrant chopped fresh parsley adds a pop of green. The colors are warm and inviting: golden brown chicken, creamy white mash, earthy browns of mushrooms, and deep green parsley. The overall composition is balanced, leaving appropriate negative space on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin and classic flatware under natural, even lighting.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Toss cauliflower florets with 30ml olive oil, salt, pepper, and paprika. Spread on a baking sheet. Roast for 20-25 minutes, until tender and slightly caramelized.
Boil potato chunks in salted water until very tender, about 15-20 minutes. Drain well. Mash potatoes with warm milk, 50g butter, 2 minced garlic cloves, salt, and pepper until smooth. Keep warm.
In a large skillet, cook diced bacon over medium heat until crispy. Remove bacon with a slotted spoon. Reserve 15ml bacon fat in the skillet.

Pat chicken breasts dry. Season with salt and pepper. Add chicken to the skillet with bacon fat. Sear for 5-7 minutes per side, until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from skillet. Rest on a cutting board.

Add remaining 30g butter to the skillet. Sauté diced onion until softened, about 3 minutes. Add sliced mushrooms and 3 minced garlic cloves. Cook until mushrooms are tender and browned, about 5-7 minutes.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer, scraping up any browned bits. Stir in heavy cream. Simmer gently for 3-5 minutes, until sauce slightly thickens. Stir in crispy bacon. Adjust seasoning.

Serve: Plate a portion of garlic mash. Arrange roasted cauliflower florets. Place chicken breast (whole or sliced into thick medallions) beside. Spoon mushroom-bacon cream sauce generously over chicken. Garnish with fresh parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Basque Chicken Txilindron with Mushrooms and Olives
recipes.visual_description: A single golden-brown chicken thigh, whole and unsliced, rests as the centerpiece in a rustic handcrafted ceramic bowl in earth tones. It is generously coated in a rich, savory, deep red-orange Txilindron sauce. Diced red bell peppers and sliced earthy mushrooms are scattered artfully around the chicken, mingling with dark, brined black olives. The dish is garnished with a sprinkle of fresh, vibrant green chopped parsley, adding a pop of color and freshness. The sauce has a fluid, inviting consistency, clinging to the ingredients without pooling excessively. On the side, a thick slice of rustic, crusty bread is presented on the reclaimed wood table, ideal for soaking up the flavorful sauce. The setting features an undyed linen napkin, under soft natural light, creating an authentic Basque dining scene.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Served with crusty bread to soak up the sauce
Accompanied by local Basque cider or wine
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs skin-side down until golden brown, 5-7 minutes. Flip and sear other side for 3-4 minutes. Remove chicken.
Add diced onion and diced bell pepper to the pot. Sauté until softened, 8-10 minutes.
Add minced garlic and sliced mushrooms. Cook for 5 minutes until mushrooms soften.
Stir in Espelette pepper. Deglaze with white wine, scraping up browned bits. Reduce by half.
Add crushed tomatoes and chicken stock. Bring to a simmer.
Return chicken thighs to the pot, skin-side up. Add olives. Cover and reduce heat to low.
Simmer for 30-35 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) and is tender.
Uncover. If sauce is too thin, simmer for an additional 5-10 minutes uncovered to reduce.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley. Serve hot.

recipes.recipe_name: Basque Chicken and Mushroom Stew
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Basque Chicken and Mushroom Stew is presented in a deep, rustic earthenware bowl. Two golden-brown, tender chicken thighs (whole or halved into thick chunks) are nestled within a rich, earthy sauce. Abundant sautéed mushrooms, cut into substantial slices, and dark, glossy Kalamata olives are evenly distributed throughout the stew. The chicken exhibits a slight crispness from searing. A vibrant sprinkle of fresh, chopped parsley provides a pop of green against the deep brown and purple hues of the stew. The sauce is viscous, clinging to the ingredients, with visible flecks of Espelette pepper. The bowl sits on a well-worn wooden dining table, accompanied by a piece of crusty baguette and a simple linen napkin. Warm, inviting light illuminates the hearty dish, evoking a homely family kitchen.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty baguette for dipping into the rich sauce.
A simple green salad with a light vinaigrette complements the hearty flavors.
Traditionally enjoyed family-style, with components served in a shared pot or bowl.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt, black pepper, and a pinch of Espelette pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs until golden brown on both sides, about 3-4 minutes per side. Remove chicken and set aside.
Add diced onion to the pot. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add sliced mushrooms to the pot. Cook until softened and browned, releasing their liquid, about 5-7 minutes.
Pour in white wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Reduce by half, about 2 minutes.
Return chicken thighs to the pot. Add chicken stock, bay leaf, and the remaining Espelette pepper. Stir in pitted and halved olives.
Bring the liquid to a simmer. Cover the pot, reduce heat to low, and cook for 20-25 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) and is tender.
Remove bay leaf. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed.
Stir in fresh chopped parsley just before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Pollo ai Funghi e Olive
