Remove from heat. Stir in fresh lemon juice and chopped dill. Season sauce with a pinch of salt and pepper.
Arrange blanched asparagus on four individual plates. Place one pan-seared salmon fillet on each plate. Drizzle generously with the lemon-dill sauce.
Garnish each plate with a fresh lemon wedge.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Salmon with Mediterranean Panzanella
recipes.visual_description: A single pan-seared salmon fillet is presented atop a vibrant Mediterranean Panzanella salad on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The salmon, a thick chunk, boasts a golden-brown, crispy skin and a flaky, moist, pale orange flesh. It is placed slightly off-center on a bed of the rustic salad. The Panzanella features irregular 2-3 cm cubes of toasted golden-brown bread, mixed with quartered red and yellow cherry tomatoes, 1.5 cm chunks of crisp green cucumber, and thin slices of purple-red onion. Fresh green basil leaves are visibly scattered throughout the salad and also garnish the top of the salmon. The composition displays a balance of colors—rich orange, vibrant reds, yellows, and greens—and textures—crispy, flaky, crunchy, and juicy. Moderate negative space surrounds the dish. The setting is a modern bistro, with the plate resting on a simple wooden table. Traditional flatware (fork and knife) are neatly placed beside the plate, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting highlights the freshness of the ingredients, creating an inviting and approachable restaurant-quality presentation.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Tear bread into irregular 2-3 cm chunks. Toss bread with 30 mL olive oil, salt, and pepper on a baking sheet. Toast in oven for 10-15 minutes, until golden and crisp. Set aside to cool.
Halve or quarter cherry tomatoes. Cut cucumber into 1.5 cm chunks. Thinly slice red onion. Place all vegetables in a large bowl.
Mince garlic. In a small bowl, whisk together remaining 70 mL olive oil, red wine vinegar, minced garlic, salt, and pepper to make the dressing.
Add toasted bread chunks to the vegetables. Pour dressing over. Toss gently to combine. Let panzanella sit for at least 15 minutes to allow flavors to meld.
Pat salmon fillets dry. Season generously with salt and pepper on both sides.
Heat a large, oven-safe pan over medium-high heat. Add a splash of olive oil. Place salmon fillets skin-side down in the hot pan. Sear for 4-5 minutes, until skin is crispy and golden.
Flip salmon. Transfer pan to preheated oven. Cook for another 5-8 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C and salmon is cooked through.
Roughly chop fresh basil leaves. Stir most of the basil into the panzanella. Reserve some for garnish.
To serve, spoon a generous portion of panzanella onto each plate. Place one pan-seared salmon fillet on top of the panzanella. Garnish with reserved fresh basil.

recipes.recipe_name: Potato and Tomato Gratin with Cheesy Oat Crust
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Potato and Tomato Gratin with Cheesy Oat Crust is presented in a pristine white oval gratin dish. The top crust is a rich, golden-brown, showcasing the crisp texture of baked oats and melted, slightly browned cheese. Beneath the crust, vibrant red tomato slices are visible, contrasting with the creamy white potato layers. Thinly sliced potatoes are tender, with a subtle sheen from the rich cheese sauce. Fresh green thyme leaves are scattered on top as a garnish, providing a pop of color. The dish is centrally placed on a clean white round plate. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple light wooden table surface and a folded cotton napkin beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and colors against a minimal, blurred restaurant-style background. No cutlery is shown on the plate, but standard modern bistro cutlery is placed alongside.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F). Lightly grease a 20x25 cm baking dish.
Peel and thinly slice potatoes into 2 mm rounds. Use a mandoline for even slices.
Slice tomatoes into 5 mm rounds.
Finely dice the onion. Mince the garlic.
Heat olive oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Sauté diced onion until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Melt butter in a separate saucepan over medium heat. Stir in flour to create a roux. Cook for 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in milk and cream until smooth and thickened. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Grate 100g of cheese. Add to the sauce. Stir until melted and smooth.
Season the cheese sauce with salt, pepper, and a pinch of nutmeg. Remove from heat.
Arrange a layer of sliced potatoes in the prepared baking dish. Season with salt and pepper.
Top with a layer of sliced tomatoes. Scatter some sautéed onion and thyme leaves.
Pour a portion of the cheese sauce over the layers.
Repeat layering: potatoes, seasoning, tomatoes, onion, thyme, and sauce. Finish with a layer of potatoes and sauce.
Grate the remaining 50g of cheese. Combine with rolled oats in a small bowl.
Sprinkle the oat and cheese mixture evenly over the top of the gratin.
Bake for 45-55 minutes, or until potatoes are tender and the crust is golden brown and bubbly.
Let the gratin rest for 10 minutes before serving.
notes: For best results, use a mandoline to achieve uniformly thin potato slices for even cooking.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Tomato Paella
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of golden-yellow Chicken and Tomato Paella is carefully mounded on a round, clean white porcelain dinner plate. The saffron-infused short-grain rice is moist yet distinct, with a few grains showing a slight crispness from the socarrat. Prominently placed on the rice are two to three substantial chunks of seared chicken, their skinless surfaces a rich golden-brown. Vibrant red diced bell peppers and bright green peas are interspersed throughout the rice, adding color and texture. A light sprinkling of freshly chopped parsley garnishes the top. A single, bright yellow lemon wedge rests on the rim of the plate. The plate is centered on a simple wooden table surface, with a folded cotton napkin beside it. A rustic, polished fork is placed to the right of the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting the steam rising subtly from the warm rice. The background is a subtly blurred modern bistro setting, with hints of other tables and soft lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve directly from the paellera for a communal dining experience.
Accompany with lemon wedges for squeezing over individual portions.
Traditionally eaten with a spoon or fork, often directly from the pan in informal settings.
instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 4-5cm chunks. Season with salt and pepper.
Dice onion and red bell pepper into 1cm cubes. Mince garlic.
Grate or finely dice tomatoes.
Heat 30ml olive oil in a 30cm paellera or large, shallow pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken chunks until golden brown on all sides. Remove chicken and set aside. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).
Add remaining 30ml olive oil to the pan. Sauté diced onion and bell pepper for 5-7 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and smoked paprika. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in grated tomatoes. Cook for 5 minutes, reducing the liquid and deepening the color to create a sofrito.
Return chicken to the pan. Stir to combine with the sofrito.
Add rice to the pan. Stir for 2 minutes to coat rice grains with the sofrito and oil.
Heat chicken broth. Steep saffron threads in a small amount of warm broth for 5 minutes, then add to the main broth.
Pour hot saffron broth into the pan. Distribute ingredients evenly. Do not stir the rice after this point.

Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to medium-low. Cook uncovered for 15-20 minutes, or until most liquid is absorbed. Listen for a crackling sound, indicating the formation of socarrat (crispy rice crust).
Sprinkle frozen peas over the paella during the last 5 minutes of cooking.
Remove paella from heat. Cover loosely with foil or a clean kitchen towel. Let rest for 5 minutes.
Chop fresh parsley. Cut lemon into wedges.
Garnish paella with fresh parsley and serve immediately with lemon wedges.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Mexican Beef Stuffed Bell Peppers
recipes.visual_description: A single, vibrant red bell pepper half, roasted to tender-crispness, sits centrally on a clean white porcelain plate. It is generously stuffed with a rich, savory mixture of seasoned ground beef, finely diced tomatoes, and creamy melted Mexican cheese, presenting a hearty, inviting texture. The top is crowned with a golden-brown, bubbly layer of baked Mexican cheese. Beside the stuffed pepper, a fresh, crisp side salad of natural salad greens and bright red tomato wedges is neatly arranged, offering a refreshing contrast. A sprinkle of fresh, chopped cilantro garnishes the pepper, along with a bright green lime wedge. The dish is presented on a simple wooden table, with a folded cotton napkin beside the plate. The setting features a subtle, culturally authentic element like a small ceramic dish of salsa roja in the background. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's vibrant colors and textures.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas on the side.
Accompany with a small bowl of fresh salsa roja or guacamole.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Halve bell peppers lengthwise. Remove seeds and membranes. Place cut-side up on a baking tray.
Bake bell peppers for 10-15 minutes to slightly soften. Remove from oven.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add diced onion to skillet. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add ground beef to skillet. Brown thoroughly, breaking it apart. Drain excess fat.
Dice one tomato. Add diced tomato, cumin, and chili powder to the beef. Cook for 5 minutes.
Remove skillet from heat. Stir in cream cheese, 150 g Mexican cheese, milk, sriracha, egg, salt, and pepper. Mix well.
Evenly fill each par-baked bell pepper half with the beef mixture.
Sprinkle remaining 50 g Mexican cheese over the stuffed peppers.
Return baking tray to oven. Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until filling is heated through and cheese is golden and bubbly.
Chop fresh cilantro. Cut remaining tomato into wedges. Cut lime into wedges.
Toss salad greens with tomato wedges, a drizzle of olive oil, salt, and pepper for a simple side salad.
Serve stuffed bell peppers immediately, garnished with fresh cilantro and a lime wedge. Serve with the side salad.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Spinach Gnocchi
recipes.visual_description: The dish presents a generous, inviting portion of tender potato gnocchi, coated in a luscious, pale green creamy spinach sauce. The gnocchi, each a soft, pillowy oval, are gently nestled together, revealing subtle ridges. Interspersed throughout the sauce are visible flecks of vibrant green wilted spinach. A delicate dusting of finely grated Parmigiano-Reggiano covers the gnocchi, adding a subtle white contrast and texture. Freshly ground black pepper provides dark speckles, and a few strands of bright yellow lemon zest offer a final touch of color and freshness. The dish is served on a clean, round white porcelain plate, resting on a light wooden table. Italian-style silver flatware and a simple white cotton napkin accompany the plate, under soft, natural lighting, creating an approachable bistro ambiance.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately, often accompanied by crusty bread to sop up the sauce.
A light white wine like Pinot Grigio pairs well with this dish.
instructions: Mince garlic. Finely dice shallot. Grate Parmigiano-Reggiano. Zest and juice lemon.
Heat olive oil and butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Add shallot. Cook until softened, 3-4 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Add spinach to skillet in batches. Stir until wilted. Season with a pinch of salt and pepper.

Pour in vegetable broth, heavy cream, and lemon zest. Bring to a gentle simmer. Stir in grated Parmigiano-Reggiano and nutmeg. Cook 2-3 minutes, stirring, until sauce slightly thickens. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil. Add gnocchi. Cook according to package directions (2-3 minutes) until they float.
Using a slotted spoon, transfer cooked gnocchi directly into the skillet with the sauce. Add lemon juice. Toss gently to coat.
Divide gnocchi among four plates. Garnish with additional grated Parmigiano-Reggiano and fresh black pepper.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Gochujang Tofu and Cabbage Stir-fry
recipes.visual_description: The Spicy Gochujang Tofu and Cabbage Stir-fry is presented in a clean white porcelain bowl, mounded centrally to showcase its vibrant colors and textures. Golden-brown, pan-fried 2cm tofu cubes are interspersed throughout, offering a crispy contrast to the slightly wilted, bright green 2cm cabbage strips. Thin orange carrot batons and translucent onion wedges add visual depth. A glossy, deep red-orange gochujang sauce evenly coats all ingredients, giving a rich sheen. The dish is garnished with a scattering of white toasted sesame seeds and thinly sliced bright green spring onion pieces. The setting features a simple wooden table with a cotton napkin beside the bowl, metal chopsticks resting on a ceramic chopstick rest, and a small ceramic dish of crimson kimchi, all under natural, even lighting, creating an authentic Korean casual dining experience.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Served with a bowl of steamed white rice.
Accompanied by various banchan (side dishes), such as kimchi.
Eaten with chopsticks.
instructions: Press tofu. Drain water. Cut tofu into 2cm cubes.
Heat 1 tbsp vegetable oil in a large pan or wok. Pan-fry tofu cubes until golden brown and crispy on all sides. Remove from pan. Set aside.
Shred cabbage into 2cm wide strips. Slice carrot into thin batons. Slice onion into thin wedges. Mince garlic. Grate ginger.
In a small bowl, whisk together gochujang, soy sauce, sesame oil, rice vinegar, and brown sugar.
Add remaining 1 tbsp vegetable oil to the hot pan. Add onion, carrot, garlic, and ginger. Stir-fry for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add shredded cabbage to the pan. Stir-fry for 3-4 minutes until cabbage slightly wilts but retains some crispness.
Return cooked tofu to the pan. Pour the sauce over the ingredients.
Toss everything to coat evenly. Cook for another 1-2 minutes until the sauce thickens slightly and coats the ingredients.
Garnish with toasted sesame seeds and thinly sliced spring onion. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Gochujang Tofu and Cabbage Stir-fry
recipes.visual_description: The Spicy Gochujang Tofu and Cabbage Stir-fry is presented in a clean white porcelain bowl, mounded centrally to showcase its vibrant colors and textures. Golden-brown, pan-fried 2cm tofu cubes are interspersed throughout, offering a crispy contrast to the slightly wilted, bright green 2cm cabbage strips. Thin orange carrot batons and translucent onion wedges add visual depth. A glossy, deep red-orange gochujang sauce evenly coats all ingredients, giving a rich sheen. The dish is garnished with a scattering of white toasted sesame seeds and thinly sliced bright green spring onion pieces. The setting features a simple wooden table with a cotton napkin beside the bowl, metal chopsticks resting on a ceramic chopstick rest, and a small ceramic dish of crimson kimchi, all under natural, even lighting, creating an authentic Korean casual dining experience.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Served with a bowl of steamed white rice.
Accompanied by various banchan (side dishes), such as kimchi.
Eaten with chopsticks.
instructions: Press tofu. Drain water. Cut tofu into 2cm cubes.
Heat 1 tbsp vegetable oil in a large pan or wok. Pan-fry tofu cubes until golden brown and crispy on all sides. Remove from pan. Set aside.
Shred cabbage into 2cm wide strips. Slice carrot into thin batons. Slice onion into thin wedges. Mince garlic. Grate ginger.
In a small bowl, whisk together gochujang, soy sauce, sesame oil, rice vinegar, and brown sugar.
Add remaining 1 tbsp vegetable oil to the hot pan. Add onion, carrot, garlic, and ginger. Stir-fry for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add shredded cabbage to the pan. Stir-fry for 3-4 minutes until cabbage slightly wilts but retains some crispness.
Return cooked tofu to the pan. Pour the sauce over the ingredients.
Toss everything to coat evenly. Cook for another 1-2 minutes until the sauce thickens slightly and coats the ingredients.
Garnish with toasted sesame seeds and thinly sliced spring onion. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: White Chocolate Chili Lentil Risotto with Roasted Artichoke and Spiced Raisins
recipes.visual_description: The creamy lentil risotto is elegantly presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, forming a natural, inviting base. Roasted artichoke halves, with caramelized edges, are thoughtfully arranged atop. Vibrant green asparagus spears add fresh contrast. Small red Thai chili flecks are visible within the risotto, hinting at warmth, while plump, glistening spiced raisins are spooned over, providing a sweet counterpoint. Finely chopped fresh parsley garnishes the dish. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple wooden table surface, standard flatware, and a cotton napkin under natural, even lighting. A single portion is showcased, allowing moderate negative space and a professional, approachable arrangement.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Drain artichoke hearts; cut larger hearts into halves. Snap woody ends off asparagus. Toss artichokes and asparagus with 15ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Roast 10-12 minutes until tender-crisp.
Rinse lentils. Heat remaining 15ml olive oil in a large saucepan over medium heat. Add diced shallots. Cook 3 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute.
Add lentils. Stir 1 minute. Pour in white wine (if using). Scrape bottom of pan. Cook until liquid evaporates.

Add 200ml vegetable broth. Simmer until absorbed, stirring frequently. Continue adding remaining broth, 150ml at a time. Stir until almost fully absorbed before adding more. Cook until lentils are tender but still have a slight bite (al dente), about 25-30 minutes. Risotto should be creamy.
Remove from heat. Stir in butter and grated Parmesan (if using). Chop white chocolate into small pieces. Stir white chocolate and thinly sliced Thai chilies into risotto. Season with salt and pepper.
In a small saucepan, combine raisins, cinnamon stick, and 50ml water. Simmer 3 minutes until raisins plump. Remove cinnamon stick.
Ladle risotto onto warm plates. Arrange roasted artichoke pieces and asparagus spears over risotto. Spoon spiced raisins over the top. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley or chives.

recipes.recipe_name: Stuffed Ciabatta with Savory Mushroom & Cherry-Dark Chocolate Glaze
recipes.visual_description: A golden-crusted, generously stuffed ciabatta half sits diagonally on a clean white porcelain plate. The ciabatta is split lengthwise, revealing a rich, earthy filling of coarsely chopped sautéed cremini, shiitake, and oyster mushrooms, mixed with finely diced garlic and fresh thyme. A glistening, deep ruby-red cherry-dark chocolate balsamic glaze is artfully drizzled over the stuffed bread and around the plate. Fresh rosemary sprigs are placed beside the ciabatta. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple wooden table, a folded cotton napkin, and a water glass. Natural, even lighting highlights the texture of the bread and the vibrant colors of the glaze and herbs. The plate is well-proportioned with moderate negative space, showcasing the dish as the focal point.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Finely dice the onion. Mince 3 garlic cloves. Coarsely chop all mushrooms.
Heat 15 ml olive oil and butter in a large pan over medium heat. Sauté diced onion for 3 minutes until softened.
Add chopped mushrooms to the pan. Cook for 8-10 minutes until mushrooms release their liquid and brown. Add minced garlic and half the fresh thyme. Cook for 2 more minutes.
Pour in vegetable broth. Reduce heat and simmer until liquid is mostly absorbed. Stir in grated Parmesan cheese. Season with salt and pepper. Remove from heat.

For the glaze: Mince the remaining 1 garlic clove. In a small saucepan, combine cherries, balsamic vinegar, and minced garlic. Bring to a simmer over medium heat. Cook for 5-7 minutes, crushing cherries with a spoon, until the mixture thickens slightly.
Remove glaze from heat. Stir in dark chocolate until melted and smooth. Season with a pinch of salt. Set aside.
Slice ciabatta loaves lengthwise, but do not cut all the way through. Gently hollow out some of the soft bread from the inside of each half, creating a cavity.
Evenly spoon the mushroom mixture into the hollowed ciabatta halves. Drizzle remaining 15 ml olive oil over the stuffed ciabatta.
Place stuffed ciabatta on a baking tray. Bake for 15-20 minutes, or until the bread is golden brown and the filling is heated through.
Remove from oven. Slice each ciabatta loaf into two individual portions.
Serve immediately with a generous drizzle of the cherry-dark chocolate glaze. Garnish with fresh rosemary sprigs and remaining fresh thyme.
notes: Adjust glaze thickness by reducing longer for a thicker sauce, or adding a splash of water for a thinner consistency.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Apple and Cherry-Onion Confit
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. A generous bed of rich, glossy cherry-onion confit forms the base, showcasing thinly sliced, caramelized onions, softened red apple slices, and plump dried cherries in a deep ruby-red reduction. Nestled atop the confit is a single, perfectly pan-seared chicken thigh, skin-on and bone-in, exhibiting a beautifully crispy, golden-brown skin. The chicken is plump and tender, its natural shape maintained. A light drizzle of the confit's reduction gently coats the chicken. The entire composition offers a delightful interplay of textures and warm, inviting colors: golden brown, deep ruby red, and hints of green from a sprinkle of fresh chopped parsley. The plate is moderately spaced, allowing the dish to be the focal point. The setting is a modern bistro, with a simple wooden table, a folded cotton napkin, and standard flatware beside the plate, all under natural, even lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty baguette slices to soak up the sauce
A simple green salad with vinaigrette

ingredients.name: Red apple (e.g., Fuji), cored and thinly sliced

instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Place chicken skin-side down.
Sear chicken for 8-10 minutes until skin is golden and crispy. Flip chicken.
Transfer skillet to a preheated oven at 190°C. Cook for 15-20 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove chicken from skillet. Keep warm. Drain excess fat, leaving 15ml in the pan.
Add sliced onions to the skillet. Cook over medium heat for 10-12 minutes until softened and caramelized, stirring occasionally.
Stir in minced garlic and sliced apples. Cook for 5 minutes until apples slightly soften.
Pour in red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Simmer for 2 minutes.
Add chicken stock, dried cherries, and thyme sprigs. Bring to a simmer. Cook until liquid reduces by half, about 8-10 minutes.
Remove thyme sprigs. Stir in butter until melted and sauce slightly thickens.
Season confit with salt and pepper to taste.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
Adjust sweetness and acidity of the confit to your preference by adding a touch more stock or a splash of red wine vinegar.

recipes.recipe_name: Cassava Coconut Mousse, Verjus Spheres, Spiced Pigeon Pea Tuile
recipes.visual_description: A pristine white Cassava Coconut Mousse dome rests off-center on an elegant, large, off-white ceramic plate. Its smooth, gleaming surface hints at a delicate, airy texture. Around its base, translucent, glistening Verjus Spheres, like pale green-gold jewels, catch the light. Two to three thin, crisp, warm golden-brown Spiced Pigeon Pea Tuiles stand upright, providing architectural height and contrasting texture. A single delicate edible flower petal garnishes the mousse. Abundant negative space emphasizes precise placement and refined aesthetics. The setting is a luxurious dining table with a superpremium wooden surface, a crisp white linen napkin, and dramatic, focused lighting. An elegant dessert fork is placed beside the plate.
instructions: Prepare Pigeon Pea Tuiles:
Boil dried pigeon peas until very tender. Drain thoroughly.
Blend cooked pigeon peas to a smooth paste.
In a bowl, combine melted butter, icing sugar, flour, egg white, ground cardamom, and a pinch of salt. Mix until smooth. Fold in 20g of pigeon pea purée.
Spread very thin layers of batter onto a silicone mat or parchment paper. Bake at 160°C for 5-7 minutes until golden brown and crisp. Cool on a wire rack. Store in an airtight container.
Prepare Cassava Coconut Mousse:
Peel and cut cassava into small chunks. Boil until very tender. Drain well.
Blend cooked cassava with coconut cream and sugar until completely smooth. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve.
Soak gelatin sheets in cold water until softened. Squeeze out excess water.
Gently heat the cassava-coconut mixture. Stir in bloomed gelatin until dissolved. Remove from heat. Add vanilla extract.
Let the mixture cool to room temperature.
Gently fold in whipped heavy cream until combined.
Pour into desired molds (e.g., small spheres or domes). Chill for at least 4 hours, or until set.
Prepare Verjus Spheres (Reverse Spherification):
Blend verjus with sodium alginate using an immersion blender until smooth. Rest in the refrigerator for at least 2 hours to remove air bubbles.
Dissolve calcium lactate in distilled water in a wide, shallow container.
Using a pipet or syringe, carefully drop small amounts of the verjus-alginate mixture into the calcium lactate bath.
Let spheres cure for 2-3 minutes, gently stirring to prevent sticking.
Carefully remove spheres with a slotted spoon. Rinse gently in a separate bowl of clean water. Store in a small amount of verjus or syrup until serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Umami Mushroom & Fermented Onion Broth
recipes.visual_description: A clear, amber-hued mushroom broth is presented in a handcrafted, earthy-toned ceramic bowl. Rustic chunks of sautéed golden-brown mushrooms rest at the bottom, offering a rich textural contrast. Vibrant, thinly sliced pink-purple fermented red onions are artfully arranged on top, providing a pop of color and a tangy visual element. A delicate swirl of crimson hot sauce adds a dynamic accent. The dish is garnished with a sprinkle of bright green, finely chopped chives, emphasizing freshness and zero-waste. The bowl sits on a light, textured reclaimed wood surface, accompanied by an undyed linen napkin. Soft, natural lighting illuminates the scene, highlighting the organic textures and natural colors of the ingredients against a clean, minimalist background with subtle natural elements.

ingredients.name: Mushroom (various types, including stems and trimmings for broth)

instructions: Prepare broth ingredients. Roughly chop 2 onions (including skins) and 500g mushroom stems/trimmings. Smash garlic cloves and ginger.

Combine chopped onion, mushroom stems, garlic, ginger, 2 litres water, 10g salt, 5g peppercorns, and bay leaves in a large pot. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 60 minutes. Skim any foam.
Strain the broth through a fine-mesh sieve. Discard solids. Set broth aside. You should have approximately 1.5 litres of clear broth.

Prepare fermented onions. Thinly slice the red onion. In a clean jar, combine 5g salt with 250ml water to dissolve. Add sliced red onion to the brine. Ensure onions are submerged. Let sit at room temperature for 12-24 hours for a quick ferment, or refrigerate for longer preservation.
Slice remaining mushroom caps into rustic chunks. Sauté in a hot pan with a splash of oil until golden brown and tender. Season lightly with salt.
To serve, gently reheat the mushroom broth. Ladle into individual bowls. Add sautéed mushroom chunks. Top with a spoonful of fermented red onion slices.
Drizzle each bowl with 15ml hot sauce. Garnish with finely chopped fresh chives or spring onion greens.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Yam and Caramelized Onion Bruschetta
recipes.visual_description: Four pieces of golden-brown toasted bread, each generously topped. Roasted yam cubes, 1 cm, are soft orange with slightly crisped edges. Dark, glistening caramelized red onion strands, thinly sliced, sit atop the yam. Bright red, halved cherry tomatoes are scattered over, adding bursts of color and freshness. Fresh green basil leaves provide a vibrant contrast, casually placed. The arrangement is natural and slightly mounded on each bruschetta slice. The dish is presented on a simple, slightly irregular off-white ceramic plate on a rustic wooden dining table. A small, dark ceramic bowl holds extra fresh basil. A muted terracotta linen napkin is casually folded. A set of simple, silver flatware is placed beside the plate. Warm, natural light illuminates the scene, highlighting textures and colors, creating a relaxed family dining atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately while the bread is warm and crisp.
Offer a small cruet of high-quality extra virgin olive oil for additional drizzling.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Peel yam. Dice into 1 cm cubes. Toss with 30 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper.
Spread yam on a baking sheet. Roast for 20-25 minutes until tender and slightly caramelized.
While yam roasts, thinly slice red onions. Sauté in 30 ml olive oil over low heat for 20-25 minutes until deeply caramelized and sweet.
Add balsamic vinegar to caramelized onions. Stir well. Remove from heat.
Halve cherry tomatoes. Season with salt and pepper.
Slice crusty bread into 1.5 cm thick pieces. Toast until golden-brown.
Cut garlic cloves in half. Rub the cut side of garlic over each toasted bread slice.
Assemble: Place roasted yam cubes on each toasted bread slice. Top with caramelized onion. Arrange cherry tomato halves over the onion.
Garnish generously with fresh basil leaves. Serve immediately.
notes: The sweetness of the caramelized onions and roasted yams provides a pleasant contrast to the fresh acidity of the tomatoes.
Garlic rubbed on the warm bread adds a subtle aromatic base.

recipes.recipe_name: Arugula, Orange, and Avocado Salad with Mustard Vinaigrette
recipes.visual_description: The salad is presented on a rustic, off-white ceramic plate, filling it naturally without overcrowding. A generous mound of vibrant green arugula forms the fresh base. Scattered throughout are bright, juicy orange segments, creamy pale green diced avocado, and deep red cherry tomato halves. Thin, delicate slices of crimson red onion add a sharp, contrasting color and texture. The ingredients are casually arranged, overlapping slightly, showcasing their natural shapes and appealing colors. A light sheen of golden, emulsified vinaigrette coats the leaves and fruit, integrating the components. A sprinkle of small, dark brown toasted mustard seeds is visible on top, adding a subtle crunch and earthy aroma. The overall impression is fresh, colorful, and inviting, evoking a homestyle Italian meal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread (pane) for dipping in leftover dressing.
Often served as a light antipasto or a side dish to a main course.
A glass of light white wine, like Pinot Grigio, would complement this salad.
instructions: Prepare the oranges: Cut off top and bottom. Stand orange on cutting board. Slice away peel and white pith from top to bottom, following the curve. Over a bowl, carefully slice segments between membranes. Collect any juice.
Prepare the avocado: Halve, remove pit, scoop out flesh. Dice into 1.5 cm cubes.
Prepare the red onion: Peel and thinly slice.
Prepare the cherry tomatoes: Halve.

Make the vinaigrette: In a small bowl, whisk together white wine vinegar, Dijon mustard, honey (if using), salt, and pepper. Slowly drizzle in olive oil, whisking constantly until emulsified. Add collected orange juice.
Toast mustard seeds: In a dry small pan, toast mustard seeds over medium heat until fragrant and they begin to pop. Let cool.
Assemble the salad: In a large bowl, combine arugula, diced avocado, orange segments, sliced red onion, and halved cherry tomatoes.
Dress the salad: Pour vinaigrette over the salad. Toss gently to coat.
Serve: Transfer to a serving platter or individual plates. Sprinkle with toasted mustard seeds.
notes: For best flavor and texture, serve immediately after dressing.
Add a sprinkle of flaky sea salt just before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Lacto-Fermented Yam & Tomato Salad
recipes.visual_description: A single starter portion of Lacto-Fermented Yam & Tomato Salad is presented on a round, handcrafted ceramic plate in an earthy cream tone. The plate showcases a minimalistic, natural composition. Firm, vibrant orange lacto-fermented yam cubes are artfully arranged, interspersed with juicy, diced red tomatoes and delicate, thinly sliced translucent purple quick-pickled red onions. Fresh green oregano and mint leaves are scattered organically, adding bursts of color and texture. Crumbled white feta cheese provides a creamy contrast. The overall arrangement is unforced, allowing each ingredient to breathe. The plate is positioned on a light, reclaimed wood table. An undyed linen napkin in natural beige is subtly placed to the side. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the dish, highlighting its fresh textures and vibrant, natural colors. The background is clean and minimalist, featuring a hint of green foliage from a potted herb, creating an eco-conscious, rustic Mediterranean ambiance. No geometric shapes, just flowing, natural elements. The entire plate is visible.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve alongside warm pita bread or slices of crusty artisanal bread.
Offer a small bowl of high-quality extra virgin olive oil for dipping.
instructions: Prepare yam for fermentation: Peel yam. Reserve peels for crisps or stock. Cut yam into 2 cm small cubes.

Lacto-ferment yam: In a clean jar, combine 500 ml water and 10 g sea salt to create a 2% brine. Add yam cubes to the jar. Ensure yam is fully submerged. Seal jar loosely. Ferment at room temperature for 3-5 days, or until desired tanginess. Burp daily. Refrigerate after fermentation.

Quick-pickle red onion: Thinly slice red onion into rings. In a small saucepan, combine 120 ml white vinegar, 120 ml water, 30 g sugar, and 5 g sea salt. Bring to a simmer. Stir until sugar and salt dissolve. Pour hot brine over sliced red onion in a heatproof jar. Let cool. Refrigerate for at least 30 minutes.
Prepare fresh ingredients: Dice tomatoes into 1 cm pieces. Coarsely chop fresh oregano and mint.
Make dressing: In a small bowl, whisk together 60 ml extra virgin olive oil, 30 ml lemon juice, a pinch of sea salt, and black pepper.

Assemble salad: In a mixing bowl, combine fermented yam cubes, diced tomatoes, pickled red onion (drained), chopped oregano, and chopped mint. Gently toss with dressing. Crumble feta cheese over the salad.
Serve: Plate a small portion of salad as a starter.
notes: For zero-waste, yam peels can be tossed with olive oil and salt, then roasted until crispy for a snack or garnish.
Onion ends and trimmings can be added to vegetable stock.

recipes.recipe_name: Cherry and Potato Gateau with Candied Onion Crumble
recipes.visual_description: The dessert is presented as an individual portion on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate, centered. It features a neatly stacked two-layer round cake, approximately 8 cm in diameter and 6 cm tall. The potato cake layers are a light golden-brown, with a fine, moist crumb visible at the edges. Between the layers, a generous amount of glossy, deep ruby-red cherry compote peeks out, showcasing whole pitted cherries and their vibrant juices. The top of the cake is crowned with a swirl of pristine white, softly whipped cream, creating a gentle peak. Scattered over the cream and around the base of the cake are small, irregular crumbles of the candied onion, which are a rich golden-brown with hints of darker caramelized sugar, providing textural contrast. Two or three fresh, whole, dark red cherries with their green stems intact are artfully placed on top of the cream. The overall color palette is warm and inviting, with rich reds, golden browns, and creamy whites. The plate has ample negative space, highlighting the dessert. The table surface is a simple, light-colored wooden laminate. A clean, folded white cotton napkin rests beside the plate, with a silver dessert fork and spoon. Natural, even overhead lighting illuminates the dish, creating soft shadows.
instructions: Boil potatoes until very tender. Mash finely. Set aside to cool.
Preheat oven to 180°C. Grease and flour an 18cm round cake pan.
Whisk eggs and 100g caster sugar until light and fluffy.
Gently fold in mashed potatoes, 50g melted butter, milk, and vanilla extract.
Sift 120g all-purpose flour and baking powder together. Fold into the potato mixture until just combined. Do not overmix.
Pour batter into prepared pan. Bake 25-30 minutes, or until a skewer inserted comes out clean.
Let cake cool in pan for 10 minutes. Invert onto a wire rack to cool completely.
Combine pitted cherries, 50g caster sugar, and lemon juice in a saucepan.
Cook over medium heat, stirring, until cherries soften and release juices, 5-7 minutes.
Mix cornstarch with cold water to form a slurry. Stir into cherries. Cook, stirring, until thickened.
Remove from heat. Let cherry compote cool completely.
Melt 15g butter in a small pan over low heat. Add finely diced red onion.
Cook gently until onion is very soft and translucent, 8-10 minutes. Do not brown.
Add brown sugar. Cook, stirring, until sugar dissolves and onion is caramelized, 3-5 minutes.
Stir in rolled oats, almond flour, and a pinch of salt.
Spread mixture thinly on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper.
Bake at 160°C for 10-12 minutes, or until golden and crisp. Watch carefully to prevent burning.
Remove from oven. Let cool completely. Break into small crumbles.
Slice the cooled potato cake horizontally into two equal layers.
Place one cake layer on a serving plate. Spread half of the cherry compote evenly over it.
Top with the second cake layer. Spread remaining cherry compote.
Whip cream with icing sugar until soft peaks form.
Pipe or spoon whipped cream onto the top of the cake.
Sprinkle candied onion crumble over the cream. Garnish with fresh whole cherries.
notes: The candied onion crumble provides a surprising depth of flavor and texture, balancing the sweetness of the cherries and cake.
Ensure potatoes are mashed very smoothly for a fine cake texture.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Mushroom & Onion Umami Broth
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Fermented Mushroom & Onion Umami Broth is presented in a handcrafted, rustic ceramic bowl with a matte, earthy beige finish. The broth is a warm, translucent amber, hinting at its deep umami flavor. A delicate cluster of vibrant green, finely chopped fresh chives floats centrally. Beside this, a small arrangement of thinly sliced, glistening quick-pickled mushroom stems provides subtle textural contrast. On the opposite side, a sprinkle of crisp, golden-brown onion skins, some curled, offers a satisfying crunch and rustic charm. The bowl rests on a light, reclaimed wooden table, complemented by an undyed linen napkin and a simple wooden spoon. Soft natural light illuminates the scene, with a minimalist background featuring a hint of natural greenery, emphasizing a sustainable aesthetic.

ingredients.name: Vegetable Scraps (e.g., carrot peels, celery ends)

instructions: Dice 200g mushrooms and 1 large onion. In a bowl, combine diced mushrooms, diced onion, and 5g salt. Mash and massage ingredients for 2-3 minutes. Cover loosely and let sit at room temperature for at least 2 hours, or up to 24 hours for deeper flavor.

Carefully peel and reserve all onion skins. Trim and reserve all mushroom stems. In a large pot, combine reserved mushroom stems, onion skins, remaining 200g sliced mushrooms, 1 large sliced onion, crushed garlic cloves, sliced ginger piece, and 1.2 litres water. Add optional vegetable scraps. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 45 minutes. Strain broth through a fine-mesh sieve, pressing solids to extract liquid. Discard cooked solids.

Thinly slice 100g fresh mushroom stems (can use some reserved from step 2 if enough, or fresh). In a small saucepan, combine 50ml apple cider vinegar, 50ml water, 5g sugar, and a pinch of salt. Bring to a boil, then remove from heat. Add sliced mushroom stems. Let cool and steep for at least 30 minutes.
Preheat oven to 150°C. Spread clean, reserved onion skins on a baking tray. Bake for 10-15 minutes until crispy and lightly browned. Watch carefully to prevent burning.

Combine the fermented mushroom & onion base (from step 1) and the strained zero-waste broth (from step 2) in a clean pot. Bring to a gentle simmer. Stir in 30ml hot sauce and 30ml soy sauce. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and black pepper.
Ladle hot soup into individual bowls. Garnish each serving with a spoonful of quick-pickled mushroom stems, a sprinkle of crispy onion skins, and fresh chopped parsley or chives.
notes: The longer the mushroom and onion base ferments, the deeper the umami flavor will become. Adjust fermentation time to your preference.
This recipe emphasizes zero-waste cooking by utilizing mushroom stems and onion skins for broth and garnish.

recipes.recipe_name: Vanilla Coconut Mousse Dome with Sugar Cane-Lime Glaze
recipes.visual_description: A pristine white bone china plate showcases a single, perfectly spherical vanilla coconut mousse dome, approximately 7 cm in diameter. It is cloaked in a translucent, shimmering sugar cane-lime glaze, reflecting light and hinting at the creamy white mousse within. Adjacent, a precise scattering of golden-brown coconut sable crumbs offers textural contrast. Opposite, a vibrant yellow-orange mango-passion fruit compote quenelle adds a bright pop of color. Abundant negative space highlights the dessert's architectural precision. The setting features a luxurious white Carrara marble surface, dramatically lit with soft shadows. A pristine white linen napkin, precisely folded, and a minimalist silver dessert fork complete the elegant, uncluttered scene, focusing entirely on the dessert's sophisticated presentation.

ingredients.name: Granulated sugar (from sugar cane, for compote)

instructions: Prepare Coconut Sable: Combine flour, powdered sugar, desiccated coconut, and salt in a bowl. Cut in solid coconut oil until crumbly. Press onto a baking tray. Bake at 160°C for 15-20 minutes until golden. Cool completely. Crumble into fine pieces.

Prepare Mango-Passion Fruit Compote: Combine diced mango, passion fruit pulp, and 10 g sugar in a small saucepan. Simmer gently for 5-7 minutes until mango softens slightly and liquid thickens. Cool completely.

Prepare Vanilla Coconut Mousse: Scoop thick coconut cream from chilled cans, leaving liquid behind. Heat 200 ml of coconut cream with vanilla bean seeds and pod, and 50 g sugar in a saucepan. Bring to a simmer. Whisk in 2 g agar-agar powder. Simmer for 1 minute, stirring constantly. Remove vanilla pod. Let cool to room temperature, stirring occasionally.
Whip remaining 200 ml coconut cream until light and fluffy. Whip plant-based whipping cream to soft peaks. Gently fold both whipped creams into the cooled vanilla coconut cream mixture.
Pour mousse into four individual silicone dome molds (approx. 7-8 cm diameter). Freeze for at least 4 hours, or until solid.

Prepare Sugar Cane-Lime Glaze: Combine 100 g sugar and 50 ml water in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, stirring until sugar dissolves. Add lime juice and 1 g agar-agar powder. Simmer for 1 minute, stirring. Let cool to 35-40°C.
Assemble: Unmold frozen mousse domes. Place on a wire rack set over a tray. Pour glaze evenly over each dome, ensuring full coverage. Let excess glaze drip off.
Carefully transfer glazed domes to serving plates. Garnish each plate with a scattering of coconut sable crumbs and a small quenelle of mango-passion fruit compote. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Savory Red Bean Paste & Aged Cheddar Canapés with Crisp Bean Sprouts
recipes.visual_description: The dish presents an array of exquisitely crafted canapés, arranged organically on an elegant, elongated white porcelain sharing platter. Each canapé features a crisp, golden artisanal sourdough base, providing a subtle textural foundation. A precisely spread layer of rich, dark mahogany-colored savory red bean paste forms the core, its smooth, slightly glossy surface contrasting with the crisp bread. Nestled atop the paste is a delicate, vibrant tangle of blanched bean sprouts, their pale white tails and tiny yellow heads offering a fresh, crunchy texture and a bright pop of color. Finely grated aged cheddar, a delicate golden veil, is artfully scattered over the sprouts, adding a nuanced yellow hue and a creamy visual element. A scattering of glossy black sesame seeds and finely snipped micro cilantro provides a final, precise touch of dark contrast and verdant freshness. The composition is minimalist, with abundant negative space highlighting the intricate details of each small bite. The overall impression is one of sophisticated balance, showcasing contrasting textures and harmonious colors.

ingredients.name: Micro cilantro or chives, finely snipped

instructions: Prepare Savory Red Bean Paste: In a small saucepan, combine sweet red bean paste, soy sauce, mirin, rice vinegar, 5ml sesame oil, minced garlic, grated ginger, and white pepper.
Heat gently over low heat for 5-7 minutes, stirring constantly. Ensure flavors meld and paste thickens slightly. Let cool completely.
Prepare Cheddar: Grate aged cheddar finely or use a vegetable peeler to create delicate shavings.
Prepare Bean Sprouts: Blanch mung bean sprouts in boiling salted water for 30 seconds. Immediately transfer to an ice bath to stop cooking. Drain thoroughly.
Toss drained bean sprouts with 5ml sesame oil, 5ml rice vinegar, and a pinch of salt.
Assemble Canapés: Spread a thin, even layer of the cooled savory red bean paste onto each sourdough crisp.
Top Canapés: Arrange a small, delicate tangle of seasoned bean sprouts on top of the red bean paste on each crisp.
Garnish Canapés: Sprinkle finely grated or shaved cheddar over the sprouts. Finish with a few black sesame seeds and finely snipped micro cilantro or chives.
Serve: Arrange canapés elegantly on a sharing platter for immediate enjoyment.

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Baked Chicken with Lemon-Herb Potatoes and Roasted Broccoli
recipes.visual_description: A single individual portion of Mediterranean Baked Chicken with Lemon-Herb Potatoes and Roasted Broccoli is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. A golden-brown, crispy-skinned chicken thigh rests centrally, its surface glistening from baking. Around the chicken, roasted potato wedges are artfully arranged, exhibiting a tender interior and lightly browned edges, flecked with vibrant green rosemary. Bright green broccoli florets, slightly charred at their tips from roasting, add a pop of color and texture. A fresh lemon wedge is placed alongside for garnish, and a sprinkle of chopped fresh parsley adds a final touch of freshness. The overall composition is balanced, with moderate negative space, showcasing the natural colors and textures of the ingredients. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple wooden table surface, a cotton napkin beside the plate, and natural, even lighting. Traditional flatware is neatly placed. The background is minimal, suggesting a casual yet refined restaurant atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty artisan bread for soaking up pan juices.
A simple green salad with a light vinaigrette.
A glass of crisp white wine.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Line a large baking tray with parchment paper.
Wash potatoes. Cut into 2 cm wedges. Place in a large bowl.
Add 30 ml olive oil, half the minced garlic, half the dried oregano, chopped rosemary, salt, and pepper to potatoes. Toss to coat evenly.
Spread potato wedges in a single layer on the prepared baking tray.
Roast potatoes for 20 minutes.
While potatoes roast, pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt, pepper, and remaining dried oregano.
In a small bowl, combine 30 ml olive oil, remaining minced garlic, and zest of one lemon. Brush this mixture over the chicken thighs.
After potatoes have roasted for 20 minutes, add chicken thighs to the baking tray, nestled among the potatoes.
Return tray to oven. Roast for another 25-30 minutes, or until chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C and skin is golden brown and crispy.
While chicken and potatoes roast, cut broccoli into medium florets. Place in a bowl.
Toss broccoli with remaining 20 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper.
After chicken and potatoes have roasted for 25-30 minutes, add broccoli florets to the baking tray. Toss lightly with pan juices.
Continue roasting for 10-15 minutes, until broccoli is tender-crisp and slightly charred.
Remove tray from oven. Squeeze juice from one lemon over the entire dish. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.
Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C for food safety.
Adjust roasting times slightly based on oven calibration and chicken size.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Korean Gochujang Salmon with Kimchi Fried Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single pan-seared salmon fillet, with its deeply caramelized, vibrant reddish-orange gochujang glaze and crispy skin, is presented whole on a clean white porcelain plate. Adjacent to it, a generous mound of kimchi fried rice, showing a rich reddish hue from the kimchi and flecks of bright green from thinly sliced green onions, is neatly arranged. The rice exhibits varied textures with some grains slightly crisped. The dish is garnished with a sprinkle of toasted sesame seeds over both the salmon and rice, enhancing its authentic Korean aesthetic. A small side dish of bright red kimchi or pickled radish sits nearby. Wooden chopsticks are placed beside the plate on a simple wooden table, under natural, even lighting, conveying a modern bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with small side dishes (banchan) such as pickled radishes or cucumber kimchi.
Offer individual ceramic bowls for the rice for a traditional dining experience.
Provide chopsticks as the primary eating utensil.
instructions: Rinse rice thoroughly. Cook rice with 600ml water in a rice cooker or pot. Set aside.
Combine gochujang, gochugaru, 15ml soy sauce, 15ml sesame oil, 2 minced garlic cloves, grated ginger, mirin, and honey in a bowl. Mix well to create marinade.
Pat salmon fillets dry. Brush marinade generously over salmon. Marinate for 15-20 minutes at room temperature.
Heat 15ml vegetable oil in a large wok or pan over medium-high heat. Add remaining 2 minced garlic cloves and white parts of chopped green onions. Stir-fry for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add chopped kimchi to the pan. Stir-fry for 3-4 minutes until slightly softened.
Add cooked rice to the pan. Break up any clumps. Add remaining 15ml soy sauce and stir-fry for 5-7 minutes until rice is heated through and slightly crispy.
Stir in remaining 15ml sesame oil and green parts of chopped green onions into the fried rice. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Heat remaining 15ml vegetable oil in a separate non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Place marinated salmon fillets skin-side down.
Sear salmon for 4-5 minutes until skin is crispy and golden. Flip carefully. Cook for another 3-5 minutes until salmon is cooked through (internal temperature 63°C/145°F).
If using, fry eggs sunny-side up in a separate small pan.
Serve each salmon fillet alongside a portion of kimchi fried rice. Garnish with toasted sesame seeds and additional fresh green onions. Top fried rice with a fried egg, if desired.

recipes.recipe_name: Mixed Vegetable Sabzi Masala
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant Mixed Vegetable Sabzi Masala is presented in a pristine white porcelain bowl. The curry features tender, diced red and yellow bell peppers and soft, sliced brown mushrooms, all coated in a rich, glossy reddish-orange gravy infused with finely caramelized onions and diced tomatoes. Fresh, bright green cilantro leaves are scattered generously over the top, providing a striking color contrast. The bowl is positioned slightly off-center on a simple wooden table. A portion of fluffy white Basmati rice is served in a small metal katori bowl, alongside a piece of warm, slightly charred naan bread. The scene is bathed in natural, even lighting, highlighting the textures and sheen of the curry and its accompaniments, evoking a modern bistro setting with authentic Indian elements.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve hot with freshly made naan bread
Serve with fluffy Basmati rice
Accompany with a side of cooling raita (yogurt dip)
Offer Indian pickles or chutney for extra flavor
instructions: Heat oil or ghee in a large pot or karahi over medium heat.
Add cumin seeds. Let them splutter.
Add chopped onions. Sauté until golden brown, about 8-10 minutes.
Stir in ginger paste, garlic paste, and green chili (if using). Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add diced bell peppers and sliced mushrooms. Sauté for 3-4 minutes until slightly softened.
Add diced tomatoes, turmeric powder, coriander powder, and red chili powder. Mix well.
Cook, stirring occasionally, until the tomatoes break down and the oil separates from the masala, about 8-10 minutes.
Pour in water or vegetable stock. Bring to a simmer. Cover and cook for 5 minutes.
Stir in heavy cream and garam masala. Cook for another 2-3 minutes until the curry thickens slightly.
Season with salt to taste. Remove from heat.
Garnish generously with fresh chopped cilantro before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Matcha-Ginger Chickpea Patties with Edamame-Red Cabbage Slaw
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant and inviting dish presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate. Two golden-brown chickpea patties, approximately 7 cm in diameter and 2 cm thick, are positioned slightly overlapping on one side of the plate. Their exterior is subtly speckled with dark green matcha, offering a crisp texture. Adjacent to the patties, a mound of colorful edamame-red cabbage slaw provides a striking contrast. The red cabbage is thinly shredded, displaying deep purple hues, interspersed with bright green edamame. The slaw is fresh and slightly glistening from its light dressing. The dish is garnished with a sprinkle of finely chopped fresh cilantro and thin, diagonal slices of green scallion, adding freshness and a pop of color. The plate is set on a light wooden table, with a simple cotton napkin folded beside it. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a small bowl of extra soy-ginger dipping sauce on the side.
Offer chopsticks as part of the table setting.
Pair with a light green tea.
instructions: In a large bowl, mash drained chickpeas coarsely with a fork or potato masher. Leave some texture.
Add matcha powder, grated ginger, minced garlic, flour, panko breadcrumbs, soy sauce, sesame oil, salt, and pepper to the mashed chickpeas. Mix until well combined.
Divide the mixture into 8 equal portions. Shape each portion into a patty, about 2 cm thick.
Heat vegetable oil in a large non-stick skillet over medium heat.
Carefully place patties in the hot oil. Cook for 4-5 minutes per side, until golden brown and crisp.
Remove patties from skillet. Drain on paper towels. Keep warm.
In a separate medium bowl, combine shredded red cabbage and thawed edamame.
In a small bowl, whisk together rice vinegar, sesame oil, soy sauce, honey (if using), grated ginger, salt, and pepper.
Pour dressing over the cabbage and edamame. Toss to coat evenly.
Plate two chickpea patties per serving. Place a generous portion of the edamame-red cabbage slaw alongside. Garnish with fresh cilantro and sliced scallions.
notes: For a firmer patty, refrigerate the mixture for 30 minutes before shaping.
Adjust matcha quantity to personal preference; a little goes a long way.

recipes.recipe_name: Matcha Chickpea and Edamame Patties with Ginger-Red Cabbage Slaw
recipes.visual_description: A single portion showcases two golden-brown, round matcha chickpea and edamame patties, approximately 8 cm in diameter and 2 cm thick, arranged slightly overlapping on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The patties exhibit a crisp exterior texture from the panko, with subtle green flecks visible within. Alongside the patties, a vibrant mound of ginger-red cabbage slaw is neatly placed. The slaw features finely julienned red cabbage, offering striking purple hues, interspersed with bright green slivers of green onion. The overall composition is balanced with moderate negative space, highlighting the contrasting colors and textures. A pair of dark wooden chopsticks rests beside the plate. The setting is a modern bistro with a simple light wooden table surface and natural, even lighting, creating an inviting, authentic cultural dining experience.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a small bowl of steamed jasmine rice.
Offer a side of sweet chili dipping sauce or extra soy-ginger sauce.
instructions: Drain and rinse chickpeas. Steam edamame until tender, about 3 minutes. Peel and grate ginger. Mince garlic.

In a food processor, combine chickpeas, edamame, half of the grated ginger, minced garlic, half of the green onions (chopped), matcha powder, 15 ml soy sauce, 5 ml sesame oil, flour, and a pinch of salt and pepper. Pulse until mostly smooth but still textured.
Form the mixture into 8 patties, about 2 cm thick. Dredge each patty lightly in panko breadcrumbs.
Heat 30 ml vegetable oil in a large non-stick pan over medium heat. Cook patties for 4-5 minutes per side, until golden brown and crispy. Set aside on a wire rack.
Thinly slice red cabbage into fine julienne strips. Zest and juice the lime.
In a medium bowl, whisk together remaining grated ginger, 30 ml rice vinegar, 15 ml maple syrup, 15 ml soy sauce, 10 ml sesame oil, lime juice, and a pinch of salt and pepper for the slaw dressing.
Add julienned red cabbage and remaining chopped green onions to the dressing. Toss to combine. Let sit for 5 minutes to slightly soften.
Plate 2 patties per serving. Serve with a generous portion of the ginger-red cabbage slaw.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Potato Curry
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Chicken and Potato Curry served in a shallow ceramic bowl on a dark wooden table. The chicken is cut into large 4cm chunks, coated in a thick, vibrant orange-brown gravy. Beside the chicken, 3cm potato cubes appear soft with rounded edges from simmering. The curry sits naturally over a mound of fluffy, long-grain white basmati rice. A functional garnish of chopped fresh cilantro is scattered on top. The plate is accompanied by a small side of lime wedges and pickled red onions. Lighting is warm and directional, highlighting the steam and glossy sauce texture. The arrangement is casual and asymmetrical, showing the entire plate in a lived-in kitchen setting with authentic utensils.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with fresh lime wedges for acidity.
Include a side of pickled red onions.
Eat with a traditional spoon or clean hands.
instructions: Wash rice. Soak in water for 20 minutes.
Boil rice in salted water until tender. Drain.
Peel potatoes. Cut into 3cm cubes.
Cut chicken into 4cm chunks.
Heat oil in a pot.
Sauté diced onion until golden.
Add minced garlic and grated ginger. Stir 1 minute.
Add turmeric, cumin, and coriander. Stir well.
Add chicken chunks. Sear until browned.
Add potato cubes and chopped tomato.
Add 250ml water.
Cover and simmer for 20 minutes.
Confirm chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Stir in garam masala and salt.
Serve curry over rice.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches a safe 75°C.
Use waxy potatoes to ensure they hold their shape during simmering.
Soaking the rice ensures long, separate grains.

recipes.recipe_name: Mushroom Risotto
recipes.visual_description: A single, individual portion of creamy Mushroom Risotto is presented in a shallow, clean white porcelain bowl. The risotto is free-flowing, exhibiting a fluid, velvety texture, not dry or molded. The Arborio rice grains are plump and glistening, interspersed with richly browned, sliced cremini and shiitake mushrooms. The dish has a warm, earthy color palette of creamy beige and deep brown, accented by vibrant green flecks of fresh chopped parsley. A generous sprinkle of finely grated Parmesan cheese provides a light, contrasting top layer. The bowl sits on a simple light wooden table. Beside it, a silver fork and spoon are arranged with a folded white cotton napkin. The setting is a modern bistro, illuminated by soft, natural, even lighting, with a subtly blurred restaurant background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately after preparation.
Offer extra grated Parmesan cheese at the table.
Pair with a light Italian white wine.
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add diced onion. Sauté until translucent, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add sliced mushrooms. Sauté until tender and browned, about 8-10 minutes.
Add Arborio rice. Stir constantly for 2 minutes until rice grains are translucent at the edges.
Pour in white wine. Stir until completely absorbed.
Add one ladleful of warm chicken stock. Stir continuously until absorbed.
Continue adding stock, one ladleful at a time, stirring constantly. Wait for each addition to be absorbed before adding the next. This process takes 18-20 minutes.
The rice should be creamy and al dente.
Remove from heat. Stir in butter and grated Parmesan cheese.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Stir in chopped fresh parsley. Serve immediately.
notes: Keep chicken stock warm throughout the cooking process for best results.
Stirring constantly helps release starch from the rice, creating a creamy texture.
Risotto should be served immediately; it thickens as it cools.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Tuscan Chicken and Mushroom Pasta
recipes.visual_description: Plated on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate, a generous swirl of al dente tagliatelle forms the base. The pasta is generously coated in a creamy, blush-colored sauce, flecked with vibrant red sun-dried tomatoes and halved bright red cherry tomatoes. Juicy, golden-brown chicken chunks are scattered throughout, alongside earthy, sautéed cremini mushroom slices. Dark green wilted spinach leaves provide a fresh color contrast. A light dusting of finely grated Parmesan cheese covers the dish, with a few fresh parsley leaves providing a final green accent. The arrangement is organic and inviting, showcasing the rich textures. The plate sits on a simple wooden table, accompanied by traditional silver flatware and a folded cotton napkin. Natural, even light highlights the dish's warmth and appealing textures.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty Italian bread to sop up the sauce.
Pair with a light green salad dressed with vinaigrette.
Offer additional grated Parmesan cheese at the table.
instructions: Cut chicken into 2-3 cm chunks. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken until golden brown and cooked through. Remove chicken from pan.
Add sliced mushrooms to the pan. Sauté until softened and browned. Remove mushrooms.
Add diced onion to the pan. Cook until translucent, about 3 minutes.
Add minced garlic and chopped sun-dried tomatoes. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Scrape up any browned bits.
Stir in heavy cream and halved cherry tomatoes. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Return cooked chicken and mushrooms to the pan. Stir in fresh spinach. Cook until spinach wilts.
Meanwhile, cook pasta in salted boiling water according to package directions until al dente. Drain pasta. Reserve 100 ml pasta water.
Add drained pasta to the sauce. Toss to combine. If sauce is too thick, add reserved pasta water as needed.
Stir in half of the grated Parmesan cheese.
Serve immediately. Garnish with remaining Parmesan and fresh parsley.
notes: Adjust red pepper flakes to taste for a spicier kick.
Fresh basil can be used instead of parsley for garnish.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Rice Arancini Bites with Tomato Dipping Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A collection of 10-12 perfectly golden-brown Chicken and Rice Arancini Bites are arranged on a rustic, rectangular slate serving platter. The arancini are roughly spherical, with a visibly crispy, textured panko crust, and are casually stacked or placed close together. Their warm, inviting golden-brown hue contrasts with a small, round ceramic bowl of vibrant red tomato dipping sauce placed slightly off-center on the platter. The sauce is smooth with small flecks of herbs. A scattering of fresh, bright green parsley sprigs garnishes the arancini and the platter, adding a pop of color. The setting is a homely family kitchen with a well-used wooden dining table, illuminated by warm, cozy lighting. A simple, casually folded cloth napkin sits nearby, adding to the relaxed, inviting atmosphere. The focus is entirely on the food, showcasing its appealing textures and colors.
instructions: Finely dice cooked chicken breast. Set aside.
Cook rice: Combine rice and chicken broth in a saucepan. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes until liquid is absorbed. Let stand 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.
Prepare aromatics: Finely dice onion and red bell pepper. Mince garlic.
Sauté vegetables: Heat 15 ml olive oil in a pan. Add diced onion and bell pepper. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic and tomato paste. Cook for 1 minute.
Combine arancini mixture: In a large bowl, mix cooked rice, sautéed vegetables, diced chicken, Parmesan cheese, and chopped parsley. Season with salt and pepper. Mix well. Let cool completely.
Form arancini: Once cooled, take spoonfuls of the mixture and roll into small, uniform balls, about 3-4 cm in diameter. You should get 8-12 balls.
Set up breading station: Place flour in one shallow dish, beaten eggs in a second, and panko breadcrumbs in a third.
Bread arancini: Roll each ball first in flour, shaking off excess. Dip in beaten egg, then roll in panko breadcrumbs, pressing gently to coat fully.

Fry arancini: Heat vegetable oil in a deep pan to 170°C. Carefully place arancini in the hot oil. Fry for 3-5 minutes, turning occasionally, until golden brown and cooked through. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C. Drain on paper towels.
Make tomato sauce: Heat 15 ml olive oil in a small saucepan. Add crushed tomatoes, sugar, salt, and pepper. Simmer for 10-15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until slightly thickened.
Serve: Arrange hot arancini bites on a serving platter. Serve with the warm tomato dipping sauce.

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish Arroz con Pollo
recipes.visual_description: A wide, shallow white porcelain bowl contains a vibrant mound of golden-hued short-grain rice. Two whole bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs rest atop the rice, featuring a deeply seared, crispy bronze skin. Evenly distributed through the rice are 1cm cubes of charred red bell pepper and finely diced translucent onions. The rice is moist and slightly glossy from the olive oil and tomato reduction. Sprigs of fresh, bright green flat-leaf parsley are scattered over the dish. The plate sits on a rustic light oak table next to a folded white cotton napkin and a polished silver fork. Natural side-lighting highlights the textures of the crispy skin and the individual grains of rice.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve in a traditional shallow terracotta dish or paella pan
Accompany with a side of garlic aioli
Pair with a chilled glass of Spanish Albariño
instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a wide pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down for 6 minutes until golden.
Flip chicken and sear for 3 minutes. Remove from pan.
Sauté onion and red pepper in the same pan for 5 minutes.
Add garlic and thyme. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in grated tomato. Cook for 4 minutes until liquid evaporates.
Add rice to the pan. Stir for 2 minutes to toast the grains.
Pour in white wine. Scrape the bottom of the pan to deglaze.
Add chicken stock. Bring to a simmer.
Place chicken thighs back into the pan on top of the rice.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 20 minutes.
Verify chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove from heat. Let rest covered for 5 minutes.
Garnish with fresh parsley before serving.
notes: Do not stir the rice once the stock is added to allow a crust to form
Grate the tomatoes to remove skins easily while keeping the pulp

recipes.recipe_name: Murgh Biryani
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant Murgh Biryani is presented in a traditional copper handi, with a single portion gently mounded onto a pristine white porcelain dinner plate. The basmati rice, cooked to distinct, long grains, shows subtle saffron-golden hues and hints of the rich brown chicken gravy. Tender, bone-in chicken pieces are nestled within the rice. Finely chopped fresh green coriander leaves and mint leaves add emerald bursts. Crispy, golden-brown fried onion slivers are sprinkled generously, providing textural contrast. A bright lemon wedge sits beside the biryani. The setting is a modern bistro with a simple wooden table, a cotton napkin, and a small ceramic bowl of Raita, with soft, natural lighting highlighting the dish's warmth and complex textures.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of cooling Raita (yogurt dip with cucumber and mint).
Accompanied by Salan (a tangy, spicy curry) or Papadum (crispy lentil wafers).
Traditionally eaten with hands or a spoon.
instructions: Marinate Chicken: In a large bowl, combine chicken pieces with yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, red chili powder, turmeric, coriander powder, cumin powder, garam masala, 10g salt, and slit green chilies. Mix well. Add half of the chopped mint and coriander. Marinate for at least 1 hour, or up to 4 hours in the refrigerator.

Prepare Onions: Heat 70 mL ghee or oil in a heavy-bottomed pot. Fry thinly sliced onions over medium heat until golden brown and crispy, about 15-20 minutes. Remove half of the fried onions and set aside for layering and garnish.

Cook Chicken Base: To the remaining oil and onions in the pot, add the marinated chicken. Cook on medium-high heat for 10-15 minutes, stirring occasionally. The chicken will partially cook and the gravy will thicken slightly. Ensure chicken reaches 75°C later during dum cooking.

Par-boil Rice: While chicken cooks, wash basmati rice thoroughly until water runs clear. Bring a large pot of water to a rolling boil. Add 5g salt and the whole spices (bay leaves, cardamom, cloves, cinnamon). Add the washed rice and cook for 5-7 minutes until 70% cooked (grains are still firm but bendable). Drain immediately.

Layer Biryani (Dum Cooking): Spread the partially cooked chicken and gravy evenly at the bottom of the heavy-bottomed pot. Layer half of the par-boiled rice over the chicken. Sprinkle with some reserved fried onions, remaining chopped mint, and coriander. Add the remaining rice. Top with the rest of the fried onions, saffron (soaked in 50 mL warm milk), and kewra water (if using).
Seal and Cook: Cover the pot tightly with a lid. Cook on very low heat for 20-25 minutes. This allows flavors to meld and the rice to fully cook in the steam.
Rest and Serve: Turn off the heat and let the biryani rest for 10 minutes, still covered. Gently mix the biryani from the bottom up using a flat spoon to combine the chicken and rice layers.
Garnish: Garnish with fresh coriander leaves and lemon wedges. Serve hot.

recipes.recipe_name: Tacos de Tinga de Pollo con Maíz Asado
recipes.visual_description: A single Tacos de Tinga de Pollo con Maíz Asado is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. A warm corn tortilla, folded, is generously filled with succulent, shredded chicken tinga, braised to a rich red-brown hue. Scattered over the tinga are golden, slightly charred roasted corn kernels. A delicate sprinkle of bright white crumbled cotija cheese and vibrant green chopped cilantro adds color and texture. A thin drizzle of creamy white crema Mexicana cascades over the toppings. The chicken is presented as tender shredded pieces, not sliced. The plate is positioned on a simple wooden table surface, with moderate negative space. A small, rustic ceramic bowl of red salsa and a lime wedge are placed beside the taco. A folded cotton napkin rests nearby. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's fresh ingredients and appealing textures, creating a casual yet refined Mexican bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a variety of authentic salsas, such as salsa roja or salsa verde, for diners to customize.
Offer pickled red onions or thinly sliced radishes as additional garnishes.
Pair with a refreshing horchata or agua fresca for a complete meal.
Encourage diners to add a squeeze of fresh lime juice to enhance the flavors.

ingredients.name: Fresh corn cobs or frozen corn kernels

instructions: Place chicken thighs in a pot. Cover with water. Add a pinch of salt. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat. Simmer for 15-20 minutes until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C. Remove chicken. Shred chicken using two forks. Reserve 250 ml of the cooking broth.

If using fresh corn, cut kernels from cobs. Spread corn kernels on a baking sheet. Roast in a preheated oven at 200°C for 10-15 minutes, or until lightly charred. If using frozen corn, roast similarly.

Dice the large onion. Mince the garlic cloves. In a large pot or Dutch oven, heat vegetable oil over medium heat. Add diced onion. Sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes. Add minced garlic. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.

Add crushed tomatoes, minced chipotle peppers, adobo sauce, bay leaf, dried oregano, and ground cumin to the pot. Stir well. Pour in the reserved 250 ml chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 10 minutes, allowing flavors to meld and sauce to thicken slightly.

Add the shredded chicken to the sauce. Stir to coat thoroughly. Continue to simmer for another 5-10 minutes, ensuring chicken is heated through and absorbs the sauce's flavors. Season with salt and black pepper to taste. Remove bay leaf.
Warm corn tortillas on a comal or dry pan until pliable and lightly toasted, about 30 seconds per side.

To assemble, fill each warm tortilla with a generous portion of chicken tinga. Top with roasted corn kernels, crumbled cotija cheese, a drizzle of crema Mexicana, and fresh chopped cilantro. Serve immediately with lime wedges.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Marsala with Sautéed Mushrooms
recipes.visual_description: A single, golden-brown chicken breast cutlet, halved horizontally and pounded, is centered on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Rich, glossy Marsala sauce, infused with savory shallots and garlic, is generously spooned over the chicken. Sautéed cremini mushroom slices, cooked until tender and lightly browned, are artistically arranged around the chicken, partially submerged in the deep amber sauce. A vibrant sprinkle of fresh, chopped parsley garnishes the dish, adding a bright green contrast. The plate sits on a simple wooden table, accompanied by traditional silver flatware and a folded cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting the golden chicken, earthy mushrooms, and the luxurious texture of the sauce. This is a single, refined restaurant-style portion.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve alongside freshly cooked fettuccine pasta or creamy polenta.
Offer with crusty Italian bread for dipping in the rich sauce.
instructions: Halve each chicken breast horizontally to create 8 thinner cutlets. Pound each cutlet to 1.5 cm thickness. Season generously with salt and black pepper. Lightly dredge chicken cutlets in flour, shaking off excess.

Heat olive oil and half of the butter in a large sauté pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken cutlets in batches for 4 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Remove chicken from pan and set aside.
Add remaining butter to the pan. Sauté thinly sliced shallots for 2 minutes. Add minced garlic; sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add sliced cremini mushrooms to the pan. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until mushrooms are tender and browned.
Pour in Marsala wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Simmer for 2 minutes to reduce slightly.
Stir in chicken broth. Bring the sauce to a gentle simmer. Cook until the sauce slightly thickens.
Return the cooked chicken cutlets to the pan with the sauce. Simmer for 2-3 minutes to heat the chicken through.
Garnish generously with freshly chopped parsley before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Sriracha Chicken Rice Noodles
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Sriracha Chicken Rice Noodles is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. Glistening rice noodles form a base, intermingled with vibrant green peas and golden-brown seared chicken cubes (2.5 cm). Chicken pieces are scattered, showcasing caramelized edges. A light reddish-orange sriracha sauce coats the dish. Fresh cilantro leaves and thinly sliced spring onion rounds garnish the top. A lime wedge sits on the plate rim. Colors are lively: pale noodles, bright green peas, deep golden chicken, and red-orange sauce. Textures include tender noodles, firm peas, and juicy chicken. The plate rests on a simple light wooden table. A dark grey cotton napkin is folded beside it. Dark wood chopsticks are placed parallel. Natural, even lighting, with a blurred modern bistro background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Served with additional sriracha or chili garlic sauce on the side for extra heat.
Accompanied by a small bowl of clear broth.
Eaten with chopsticks.
instructions: Cut chicken breast into 2.5 cm cubes. Season with salt and pepper.
Soak rice noodles in hot water for 5-7 minutes until tender. Drain and rinse with cold water. Set aside.
Mince garlic and ginger. Thinly slice shallots. Chop spring onions into 2.5 cm pieces.
In a bowl, whisk together sriracha sauce, soy sauce, rice vinegar, brown sugar, chicken broth, and sesame oil.

Heat vegetable oil in a large wok or skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken cubes. Sear until golden brown and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken and set aside.
Add shallots to the wok. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant. Add minced garlic and ginger. Sauté for another minute.
Add green peas to the wok. Stir-fry for 2 minutes. Return cooked chicken to the wok.
Add drained rice noodles and the prepared sriracha sauce to the wok. Toss everything together until well combined and heated through, about 2-3 minutes.
Stir in chopped spring onions. Squeeze fresh lime juice over the noodles.
Garnish with fresh cilantro leaves and a lime wedge. Serve immediately.
